contemporaryApplications.descEn: Ecstatic union is a key topic in consciousness studies and phenomenology of religion

philosophers.name: 塞内卡
philosophers.nationality: 古罗马（生于西班牙科尔多瓦）
philosophers.role: 罗马斯多亚三巨头之一，尼禄之师
philosophers.summary: 罗马斯多亚哲学的旗手，尼禄的导师兼首席顾问，也是哲学史上最富戏剧性的人物之一：一边写《论生命之短暂》《论幸福生活》劝人淡泊，一边在帝国的权力中心管理政务、积累巨额财富。他的散文把斯多亚的「不动心」变成了可操作的生存智慧，被后世称为「哲学家的道德导师」。公元 65 年他因被指控参与政变而奉旨自尽，死得比任何人都像自己写的哲学。
philosophers.summaryEn: The banner-carrier of Roman Stoicism, tutor and chief advisor to Nero, and one of philosophy's most dramatic figures: writing essays on tranquility while wielding power and amassing wealth at the empire's center. His prose turned Stoic apatheia into actionable life-wisdom. Ordered to commit suicide in 65 AD on conspiracy charges, he died exactly like his own philosophy.

representativeWorks.title: 《论生命之短暂》
representativeWorks.content: 塞内卡最著名的随笔之一：我们不是生命太短，而是浪费太多。只有把时间用于自我修炼的人，才真正「拥有」生命；忙碌于外务的「大忙人」其实从未活过。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Life is not short — we waste it. Only those who devote time to self-cultivation truly possess their lives; the busy are the ones who never live.

representativeWorks.title: 《论幸福生活》
representativeWorks.content: 系统阐述斯多亚的幸福论：幸福在于与自然一致、以德性为善。他坦诚地为「哲人拥有财富」辩护——财富本身不是恶，关键在于灵魂是否依赖它。
representativeWorks.contentEn: A systematic Stoic account of happiness: the good life follows nature and rests on virtue. He famously defends the sage's right to wealth — the problem is not possession but dependence.

representativeWorks.title: 《致卢基里乌斯书信集》
representativeWorks.content: 124 封哲学书信，是斯多亚修身术的百科全书：如何面对死亡、愤怒、贫穷、流放，如何入睡、旅行、读书。西方道德随笔传统的开山之作。
representativeWorks.contentEn: 124 philosophical letters — an encyclopedia of Stoic spiritual exercises: facing death, anger, poverty, exile, sleep, travel, reading. The founding text of the Western moral essay.

coreThoughts.desc: 塞内卡对死亡有近乎偏执的清醒：人唯一能真正拥有的是当下这一刻，过去已逝、未来未定。把生命抵押给未来的野心，等于提前自杀。所以「每天都当作最后一天来过」不是悲观，而是唯一能让人真正活着的策略。这个主题被后人称为「存在的紧迫性」，海德格尔的「向死而生」在塞内卡这里已有完整雏形。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：塞内卡说我们不是活得短，而是浪费得多——只有把握住每一个「现在」，生命才算真正属于你。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像旅行者只拥有正在走的这一段路，过去的路已经走完、未来的路还没到——盯着终点赶路的人，其实错过了整趟旅行。
coreThoughts.l3: 塞内卡区分「拥有时间」（把时间用于自我完善）与「消磨时间」（把时间交给他人与外务）。他主张 memento mori（记住你必死）：死亡的意识不是恐惧的来源，而是清醒与自由的来源——知道会失去，才懂得拥有。
coreThoughts.descEn: We own only the present instant; the past is gone, the future uncertain. To live every day as if it were your last is not pessimism but the only strategy for truly living. Heidegger's being-toward-death is fully prefigured here.
coreThoughts.l1En: We don't live too briefly — we waste too much. Only those who seize the present truly own their lives.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a traveler: you possess only the road you are walking now, not the miles behind or ahead.
coreThoughts.l3En: Seneca's memento mori: the awareness of death is not fear but freedom — knowing you can lose something is the condition of truly owning it.

coreThoughts.desc: 斯多亚的核心：幸福不取决于外部境遇，而取决于内心对境遇的判断。愤怒、恐惧、贪婪都是「判断错误」——以为外物能决定我们的幸福。塞内卡用一生（包括临死）示范：风暴来临时的内心宁静，才是德性真正的考场。他特别重视「预先思考厄运」（praemeditatio malorum）：想象最坏情况，反而获得处变不惊的能力。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：外部世界你管不了，但你对它的态度完全由你决定——把判断权收回来，就没什么能伤害你。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像船在风浪里：你控制不了浪，但你可以训练水手的沉稳——斯多亚就是训练那个「内在水手」。
coreThoughts.l3: 斯多亚的二分法（dichotomy of control）：可控的（判断、意愿、德性）与不可控的（财富、健康、名誉）。情绪（pathos）是错误判断（krisis）的产物，德性即正确的判断。praemeditatio malorum 与认知行为疗法（CBT）的「认知重评」高度同构。
coreThoughts.descEn: Happiness depends not on circumstances but on our judgments of them. Anger, fear, greed are mistaken judgments. By premeditating misfortune one gains the power to remain unmoved when it arrives — a discipline strikingly parallel to modern cognitive therapy.
coreThoughts.l1En: You cannot control the world, but you fully control your attitude toward it. Take back judgment, and nothing can harm you.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a ship in a storm: you can't control the waves, but you can train the sailor within.
coreThoughts.l3En: The dichotomy of control; emotions as mistaken judgments; virtue as right judgment. Praemeditatio malorum anticipates cognitive reappraisal in CBT.

famousEvents.title: 科西嘉流放
famousEvents.desc: 因牵涉宫廷政治，被皇帝克劳狄乌斯流放科西嘉岛八年。流放期间写作《论慰藉》等，把苦难转化为哲学素材。
famousEvents.descEn: Banished to Corsica by Claudius for eight years on palace intrigue; he turned exile into philosophical material.

famousEvents.title: 尼禄弑母与权力旋涡
famousEvents.desc: 尼禄弑母后，塞内卡替他起草了向元老院的辩解信。这件事成为后世衡量其哲学与道德一致性的焦点：一个倡导德性的人如何为暴行辩护？
famousEvents.descEn: After Nero murdered his mother, Seneca drafted his justification to the Senate — the classic test case of the gap between Stoic virtue and political reality.

famousEvents.title: 奉旨自尽
famousEvents.desc: 被指控参与皮索政变，尼禄赐死。塞内卡从容切开血管，与妻子、朋友们讨论哲学直至断气，史称「哲学家的死亡」。
famousEvents.descEn: Accused in the Pisonian conspiracy, he was ordered to die. He calmly opened his veins, discoursing on philosophy with friends until the end — the archetypal philosopher's death.

philosophers.scientificEval: 塞内卡的《自然问题》讨论了地震、彗星、河流等自然现象，虽以斯多亚的目的论解释为主，但保持了对经验观察的重视，是中世纪自然哲学的重要资源。他对情绪的认知分析（情绪=判断）被现代情感科学视为认知理论的前驱，其「预先思考厄运」与认知行为疗法的技术家族相似性已被心理治疗史承认。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: His Natural Questions, though Stoically teleological, preserved empirical attention and fed medieval natural philosophy. His cognitive theory of emotion (emotion as judgment) is recognized as a forerunner of modern affective science, and his premeditation of misfortune parallels CBT techniques.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 塞内卡一生都在德性理想与帝国权力之间走钢丝。早年师从斯多亚教师阿塔卢斯等，哲学是他少年时的救赎（他体弱多病、情绪激烈）。此后的人生：律师、元老、流放、还朝、成为尼禄之师、独揽大权、失势、自尽——每一次转折都被他写成道德的操练。他的哲学不是书斋里的体系，而是「如何在坏时代里保持体面」的实战记录，这恰恰是斯多亚最打动人的地方。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: Seneca's life was a tightrope between virtue and imperial power: sickly youth, lawyer, senator, exile, tutor of Nero, master of Rome, downfall, suicide. His philosophy is less a system than field-notes on keeping one's dignity in a bad time — exactly what makes Stoicism compelling.
philosophers.aiReview: 塞内卡是哲学史上「知行分裂」最著名的案例，也正因为这种分裂，他比任何完人哲学家都更真实。一边是《论幸福生活》里「财富不能带来幸福」，一边是帝国最富有的政客；一边教人不动心，一边替尼禄的暴行起草公文。辩护者说：他至少在自己的死亡上做到了知行合一；批评者说：他活成了自己哲学的反面教材。或许公允的评价是——塞内卡的著作因为包含了这种挣扎而格外有生命力，两千年来，每个在体制内试图保有一点灵魂空间的人，都能在他的书里找到自己的处境。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Philosophy's most famous case of theory-practice divide — and precisely because of it, more real than any flawless sage. Defenders note he at least died as he taught; critics call him the anti-example of his own doctrine. Fairly judged, his writings live because they contain this very struggle: everyone trying to preserve a little soul inside a system finds their own situation in his pages.

philosophers.anecdote: 塞内卡体弱多病、哮喘缠身，却活到 69 岁高龄（在当时算长寿），把养生也写成了哲学：《论生命的短暂》里他说，「每天都当作最后一天」的人反而活得最久。临死前他按自己的哲学行事——与妻友谈论不朽，饮毒而不得死，最后在浴缸的热气中断气。
philosophers.anecdoteEn: Asthmatic and sickly, Seneca nonetheless lived to 69. His death followed his own script: discussing immortality with friends, taking poison that failed to kill him, finally suffocating in the warm steam of a bath.

philosophers.name: 爱比克泰德
philosophers.role: 罗马斯多亚三巨头之一，奴仆出身的哲学导师
philosophers.summary: 斯多亚哲学史上最具传奇色彩的人物：生为奴隶，瘸了一条腿，被主人打断后反而说「你很快就要打断它了」——用斯多亚的预言式幽默回应暴行。获释后他在罗马和尼科波利斯讲学，学生中包括罗马贵族甚至皇帝哈德良。他本人不着一字，全靠学生阿里安记录成《手册》和《谈话录》。这两本书把斯多亚哲学浓缩成了一句句可执行的格言，至今仍是斯多亚主义在当代复兴的第一读本。
philosophers.summaryEn: The most legendary figure of Stoicism: born a slave, crippled — when his master broke his leg he remarked, 'you will soon break it too', a prophecy fulfilled. Freed, he taught in Rome and Nicopolis to aristocrats and emperors. He wrote nothing; his student Arrian recorded the Handbook and Discourses, which compress Stoicism into executable maxims and remain the first text of the modern Stoic revival.

representativeWorks.title: 《手册》
representativeWorks.content: 由学生阿里安记录、浓缩爱比克泰德教导的 53 条箴言，开篇就是著名的「二分法」：「有些事情取决于我们，有些则不。」全书以极简的句子教人如何面对死亡、侮辱、失去、欲望——西方实践哲学的袖珍圣经。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Fifty-three maxims of Epictetus' teaching recorded by Arrian, opening with the famous dichotomy: 'Some things are up to us, some are not.' A pocket bible of practical philosophy.

representativeWorks.title: 《谈话录》
representativeWorks.content: 阿里安记录的课堂实录四卷，比《手册》更完整地呈现爱比克泰德的教学风格：诘问、反讽、设喻，把抽象的斯多亚原理变成对具体人生的诊断。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Four books of class transcripts by Arrian, fuller than the Handbook, showing Epictetus' method of questioning, irony, and analogy — diagnosing concrete lives with abstract Stoic principles.

coreThoughts.desc: 爱比克泰德手册的第一课，也是整个斯多亚实践哲学的地基：把一切事物分成两类——取决于我们的（判断、意愿、欲望、回避）与不取决于我们的（身体、财富、名誉、他人、死亡）。幸福 = 只在意前者；痛苦 = 误把后者当作自己能力的范围。这句话听起来简单，执行起来需要一生的训练，因为它要求你重新定义「什么是我的」。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：世界上只有两类事——你管得着的（自己的态度和选择）和你管不着的（别人的看法、身体、命运）。把心只放在前者上，就没人能夺走你的安宁。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像足球赛：你能控制的是自己的拼抢和态度，控制不了的是比分、裁判和对手——为一个控制不了的结果生气，是拿别人的脚踢自己的心。
coreThoughts.l3: 二分法（dichotomy of control）是斯多亚「自由」概念的基础：自由不是为所欲为，而是不受非我所能控制之物的奴役。爱比克泰德进一步提出「判断」是灵魂唯一的领地——外物可以伤害你的身体，但不能伤害你的选择。这一区分后来被认知疗法直接继承。
coreThoughts.descEn: Some things are up to us — judgments, will, desire, aversion. Others are not — body, wealth, reputation, others, death. Happiness consists in caring only about the former; misery in treating the latter as ours to command. A simple sentence requiring a lifetime of training.
coreThoughts.l1En: Only two kinds of things exist: what you control (your attitudes and choices) and what you don't (others' opinions, health, fate). Put your heart only in the first, and nothing can rob your peace.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a football match: you control your own effort, not the score, the referee, or the opponent.
coreThoughts.l3En: Freedom, for Epictetus, is not doing whatever you want but refusing enslavement to what is not yours. The judgment is the soul's only territory. This distinction is inherited directly by cognitive therapy.

coreThoughts.desc: 一个被解放的奴隶来教导自由，这是爱比克泰德最大的反讽，也是他最深的洞见：真正的奴役不是锁链，而是把幸福寄托于他人施舍——为了讨好老板、名声或情人而扭曲自己，才是灵魂的奴隶制。他从不否认身体会痛、人会死，但他坚持：在这些无法选择的事实面前，如何回应——是恐惧还是尊严——永远是自由的。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：身体可以被锁住，灵魂不可以——只要你不在乎别人怎么看你，就没有人能用舆论锁住你。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像关在笼子里的鸟：它不再唱歌，不是因为笼子，而是因为放弃了歌唱的意愿——爱比克泰德说，放弃意愿才是真正的笼子。
coreThoughts.l3: 爱比克泰德在《谈话录》中反复使用「slave/free」的对照：自由人即「不把自己的幸福抵押给非己之物」的人。他尤其强调面对死亡与失落的「预备」（premeditatio），并把「扮演好命运分配给你的角色」作为斯多亚的生活伦理——命运是舞台，角色是给定的，演技是自由的。
coreThoughts.descEn: A freed slave teaching freedom is Epictetus' greatest irony and deepest insight: real slavery is not chains but mortgaging your happiness to others' approval. The body may be locked; the response — fear or dignity — is always free.
coreThoughts.l1En: The body can be chained, the soul cannot — as long as you don't care what others think, no one can lock you with opinion.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a caged bird that stops singing: not because of the cage, but because it gave up the will to sing.
coreThoughts.l3En: The free person is one who never mortgages happiness to what is not theirs. Life is a play: the role is given, the acting is free.

famousEvents.title: 奴隶生涯与断腿预言
famousEvents.desc: 少年时为奴，主人埃帕弗洛狄托（曾任尼禄秘书）残酷拷打他。据传主人扭断他的腿时，他平静地说：「你很快就要打断它了。」获释时腿已残疾。
famousEvents.descEn: As a young slave he was tortured by his master Epaphroditus; legend says when his leg was being twisted he calmly remarked 'you will soon break it' — and it broke. He was lame for life.

famousEvents.title: 被逐出罗马
famousEvents.desc: 与许多哲学家一道被皇帝图密善逐出罗马（当时哲学教师常被视为危险分子），他移居希腊的尼科波利斯继续讲学，直至去世。
famousEvents.descEn: Banished by Domitian along with other philosophers in 89 AD, he settled in Nicopolis, Greece, and taught there for the rest of his life.

philosophers.scientificEval: 爱比克泰德对情绪的认知主义分析（情绪源于信念与评价）经现代心理学确认为认知疗法（REBT/CBT）的直接理论先导——艾利斯（Albert Ellis）明确承认其学说源自斯多亚与爱比克泰德。其「控制二分法」被当代积极心理学、压力管理与韧性训练广泛采用，成为少有的「两千年前的理论，两千年后被实验室方法验证」的案例。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: Epictetus' cognitivism about emotion (emotions arise from beliefs and evaluations) was explicitly acknowledged by Albert Ellis as the direct ancestor of REBT/CBT. His dichotomy of control is used across positive psychology, stress management, and resilience training — a rare case of ancient theory validated by modern experimental methods.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 爱比克泰德的思想线索清晰：奴隶的处境教会他区分「能控制」与「不能控制」；斯多亚学校（师从穆索尼乌斯·鲁弗斯，一位同样被流放的哲学家）给他提供了系统的概念工具；讲学的生涯则让他把哲学从理论改造成「训练」（askesis）。他没有写过一部体系著作——他自称「老瘸腿」，说自己只配做一个「哲学的铁匠」，把别人冶炼出的金属打成日常可用的工具。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: His line of thought is clear: slavery taught him the dichotomy of control; the Stoic school of Musonius Rufus gave him the concepts; teaching turned philosophy into training (askesis). He wrote no system — he called himself a 'lame old man', a blacksmith of philosophy hammering others' metal into daily tools.
philosophers.aiReview: 爱比克泰德是斯多亚哲学里最「好用」的一个，因为他的理论直接从极端处境里长出来：一个残废的奴隶教罗马贵族怎么面对失去，这比任何书斋论证都有说服力。他的二分法听起来朴素，却是少数能真正改变行为模式的哲学工具——当代认知行为疗法基本就是它的现代化。当然，批评者也指出：二分法的另一面是「斯多亚式的认命」，把社会不公归因于「你的判断问题」，可能成为系统性压迫的心理润滑剂。但对一个身处罗马帝国底层的奴隶来说，这已经是能给自己争取尊严的最大武器。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Epictetus is the most usable Stoic because his theory grew from extremity: a crippled slave teaching aristocrats how to face loss. His dichotomy is one of the few philosophical tools that actually changes behavior — CBT is essentially its modernization. Critics note the doctrine's shadow: 'it's your judgment problem' can lubricate systemic injustice. But for a slave at the bottom of the Roman Empire, it was the greatest weapon of dignity available.

philosophers.anecdote: 传说他终生未婚、独居陋室，门边只挂一盏灯。那盏灯后来被一个雅典人高价买走当纪念品——他听了大笑：「那么他买这盏灯一定是为了看东西吧？」他把一切身外之物都看成可以随时放下的道具。
philosophers.anecdoteEn: He lived alone in a humble hut with a single lamp; a collector later bought the lamp at auction as a relic. Epictetus laughed: 'So he bought it in order to see by it, no doubt?' Everything external was for him a prop one may set down at any time.

philosophers.name: 波爱修斯
philosophers.role: 「最后一位罗马人」，古代哲学通向中世纪的桥梁
philosophers.summary: 罗马元老、哲学家、翻译家，被誉为「最后一位罗马哲学家和第一位经院哲学家」。他计划把柏拉图和亚里士多德全部著作译成拉丁文（未竟），他译的亚里士多德《范畴篇》等成为中世纪拉丁西方学习逻辑的教科书。在狱中等待处决时写下《哲学的慰藉》——以哲学与人格化的「哲学夫人」对话，讨论命运、幸福与自由意志，成为中世纪最畅销的哲学书之一，深刻影响了但丁、乔叟和整个经院传统。
philosophers.summaryEn: Roman senator, philosopher, and translator — 'the last Roman philosopher and the first scholastic'. He planned to translate all of Plato and Aristotle into Latin; his translations of Aristotle's Categories and others became the standard logic textbooks of the medieval West. Imprisoned awaiting execution, he wrote The Consolation of Philosophy — a dialogue with Lady Philosophy on fortune, happiness, and free will — among the most widely read books of the Middle Ages, influencing Dante, Chaucer, and the whole scholastic tradition.

representativeWorks.title: 《哲学的慰藉》
representativeWorks.content: 狱中绝笔，五卷散文与诗歌交替。哲学夫人现身安慰囚徒：财富、权力、名声皆为「善的赝品」，真正的幸福是完满的善即上帝；命运之轮虽有升降，但最高的善与自由意志永在人心之内。文笔之美与思想之深使它成为中世纪最流行的哲学书。
representativeWorks.contentEn: His prison masterpiece, alternating prose and verse. Lady Philosophy consoles the prisoner: wealth, power, fame are counterfeit goods; true happiness is the perfect Good, God; the wheel of fortune turns, but the highest good and free will remain within the soul. The most popular philosophical book of the Middle Ages.

representativeWorks.title: 《论三位一体》
representativeWorks.content: 以亚里士多德范畴论解析基督教三位一体教义，示范了「哲学为神学服务」的经院方法——后被经院哲学家视为方法论典范。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Applying Aristotle's categories to the Christian Trinity, exemplifying the scholastic method of philosophy serving theology.

coreThoughts.concept: 命运之轮与哲学的慰藉
coreThoughts.desc: 波爱修斯从权力的巅峰跌落狱中，面对的核心问题是：如果上帝公正且全能，为什么好人遭殃？他的回答分两层：第一，世俗的「好运」（财富、地位）根本不是善，命运之轮本来就会转动，把幸福押在轮子上等于自愿上绞架；第二，真正的善（德性、智慧、完满的善即上帝）不可被夺走，而且上帝以永恒之眼同时看见全部时间，他的预知不取消人的自由意志。最后他给出著名的「慰藉」：没有上帝允许，邪恶不能发生；恶人其实比受害者更可怜。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：人生像坐命运之轮，好运会转走，但只有把幸福寄托在转不走的东西上（德性与智慧），才是真正安全的活法。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像坐旋转木马：抓着栏杆（身外之物）的手会被甩开，但坐在木马上的人（内心）本身不会掉——波爱修斯教你坐稳自己的心。
coreThoughts.l3: 《哲学的慰藉》第五卷处理自由意志与神预知的兼容：上帝不在时间中，而是「永恒的现在」（nunc stans），他从永恒视角「看见」而非「预定」人的选择，故预知不取消自由。这一分析是后来奥古斯丁-阿奎那路线的标准进路。
coreThoughts.conceptEn: The Wheel of Fortune and Consolation
coreThoughts.descEn: If God is just and omnipotent, why do the good suffer? Boethius answers: worldly fortune is not genuine good — the wheel turns by nature; the true Good (virtue, wisdom, God) cannot be taken away. God's eternal vision of all time does not cancel free will.
coreThoughts.l1En: Life is a wheel of fortune: luck will spin away, but only those who invest happiness in what cannot spin away — virtue and wisdom — are truly safe.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a carousel: the hand gripping the railing (external goods) will be torn off, but the rider's seat (the soul) holds steady.
coreThoughts.l3En: Book V reconciles foreknowledge and freedom: God is not in time but in an eternal present, 'seeing' rather than 'willing' human choices — the standard Augustinian-Thomistic solution.

coreThoughts.concept: 共相问题（唯名论/实在论之争的起点）
coreThoughts.desc: 波爱修斯翻译亚里士多德《范畴篇》时，在注释中提出了一个追问，这个追问将折磨整个中世纪：共相（如「人」「白」）是独立存在的实体，还是仅仅存在于思想中的名称？他的讨论被后世经院哲学家（阿伯拉尔等）接棒，演变成唯名论与实在论的大战——这场争论直接影响了中世纪神学、认识论乃至近代科学对「普遍规律」的定位。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：他说「人」这个字到底对应真实存在的东西，还是只是一个方便归纳的标签？——这个问题后来吵了整整一千年。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像「水果」这个词：苹果是真实存在的，「水果」本身在哪里？——波爱修斯的问题就是「共相」版本的「水果在哪」。
coreThoughts.l3: 波爱修斯提出五种方案（属/种是否存在、是否可感、是否独立于个体等），为经院哲学提供了标准问题集。唯名论（阿伯拉尔、奥卡姆）与实在论（安瑟伦、阿奎那）的分歧由此展开，其影响延续至近代（贝克莱、休谟对抽象观念的批判）。
coreThoughts.descEn: In commenting on Aristotle's Categories, Boethius posed the question that would torment the whole Middle Ages: do universals ('humanity', 'whiteness') exist independently, or only as names in thought? His framing fed the thousand-year nominalist/realist controversy, whose echoes reach modern debates about the reality of laws and kinds.
coreThoughts.l1En: Does the word 'human' refer to something really existing, or is it just a convenient label? — a question argued for a thousand years.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like the word 'fruit': apples exist; where does 'fruit' itself exist? Universals are 'fruit' in philosophical form.
coreThoughts.l3En: His five questions set the agenda for the scholastic debate: are universals real, corporeal, separable from individuals? Nominalists and realists divided accordingly — a dispute echoing into Berkeley and Hume's critique of abstract ideas.

famousEvents.title: 从执政官到死囚
famousEvents.desc: 波爱修斯身居东哥特国王狄奥多里克朝中要职，因维护元老院传统、牵涉宫廷政治，被诬以叛国罪下狱。次年即被处决（一说是绞杀，一说是斧劈）。
famousEvents.descEn: Holding high office under Theodoric the Ostrogoth, he was accused of treason for defending senatorial tradition and imprisoned in 523; executed the next year.

famousEvents.title: 狱中写《哲学的慰藉》
famousEvents.desc: 在等待处决的狱中写下《哲学的慰藉》，随后从容就义。此书成为他在历史上真正的纪念碑。
famousEvents.descEn: While awaiting execution he wrote the Consolation, then met death calmly. The book became his true monument.

philosophers.scientificEval: 波爱修斯翻译并注释了亚里士多德的逻辑著作（《范畴篇》《解释篇》）与波菲利《导论》，还著有三段论专著与音乐理论《音乐原理》——后者是中世纪音乐理论的权威教材，影响了数百年。他的「共相问题」设定了中世纪认识论的议程，其关于「声音之数学比例」的音乐理论被视为最早的声学理论之一。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: Boethius translated and commented on Aristotle's logic (Categories, On Interpretation) and Porphyry's Isagoge, wrote on syllogisms, and composed Fundamentals of Music — the standard music-theory textbook for centuries, containing early acoustic theory via mathematical ratios.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 波爱修斯的思想轨迹清晰：早年以翻译和注释亚里士多德逻辑著称（逻辑学家的波爱修斯），晚年转向神学与哲学的终极问题（慰藉者的波爱修斯）。从「把希腊逻辑带给拉丁西方」到「用哲学回答生死」，他的工作合起来恰好完成了古代哲学向中世纪的思想交接：方法上是亚里士多德的，关怀上是柏拉图式的（灵魂、至善、不朽）。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: His trajectory is clear: early Boethius the logician translated and commented on Aristotle; late Boethius the consoled turned to ultimate questions of God, fortune, and the soul. Together the two phases complete the handover from antiquity to the Middle Ages: Aristotelian in method, Platonic in concern.
philosophers.aiReview: 波爱修斯值得记住的一点是：他几乎一个人保住了古代逻辑学在西方的火种。当西罗马帝国崩塌、希腊语在西欧近乎失传时，他的拉丁译文成为未来一千年里欧洲人接触亚里士多德逻辑的主要管道；而《哲学的慰藉》则证明，哲学最锋利的时刻往往出现在生命最脆弱的时刻。有人批评他把太多力气花在调和柏拉图与亚里士多德、哲学与基督教上——但这恰恰是他的历史位置：一个站在两个世界之间的人，必须把两边都接住。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Boethius alone kept the flame of ancient logic alive in the West: his Latin translations were the main conduit to Aristotle's logic for a thousand years. The Consolation proves philosophy cuts sharpest at life's most fragile hour. Critics say he spent too much effort harmonizing Plato with Aristotle, philosophy with Christianity — but that was his historical station: standing between two worlds, he had to catch both.

furtherReading.title: 《哲学的慰藉》（中译本）
furtherReading.desc: 狱中绝笔，中世纪最畅销哲学书

philosophers.anecdote: 波爱修斯一生高居罗马政坛巅峰，被狄奥多里克尊为「国师」，却在权力的最高处骤然跌落。传说他在狱中听到诗歌，忽然看见哲学夫人现身——这个「狱中幻象」成为西方文学中最著名的慰藉场景之一。而他的死法至今仍是悬案：有人说是被绞杀，有人说是被斧头砍死，但所有人都同意，他死前刚刚写完了一本关于「如何平静地死」的书。
philosophers.anecdoteEn: At the peak of Roman politics he fell overnight into prison. Legend has it that in his cell he heard verse and saw Lady Philosophy appear — the most famous consolation scene in Western literature. His death remains disputed (hanging or axe), but all agree he died just after writing a book on dying peacefully.

goldenQuotes.text: 命运之轮旋转不歇：登上高处者不可自得，落入低谷者亦不必绝望。
goldenQuotes.textEn: The wheel of fortune turns without rest: he who is raised high should not exult, he who is cast down need not despair.

goldenQuotes.text: 没有比一个不幸而自以为是幸福的人更不幸的了。
goldenQuotes.textEn: No one is more miserable than he who is miserable and thinks himself happy.

philosophers.name: 安瑟伦
philosophers.nationality: 意大利（后任英格兰坎特伯雷大主教）
philosophers.role: 经院哲学之父，本体论证明的提出者
philosophers.summary: 被称为「经院哲学之父」的意大利本笃会修士，后任坎特伯雷大主教。他坚信「信仰寻求理解」（fides quaerens intellectum）：先信，然后为信仰寻找理性的理由。他最著名的贡献是「本体论证明」——仅凭「上帝」这个概念本身就论证上帝必然存在，这个论证在千年后仍被笛卡尔、莱布尼茨、康德反复检验，至今是宗教哲学的核心考题。
philosophers.summaryEn: Called the father of scholasticism, this Italian Benedictine monk later became Archbishop of Canterbury. He held that faith seeks understanding (fides quaerens intellectum): believe first, then seek reasons for faith. His famous ontological argument — that God's existence follows from the very concept of God — was tested by Descartes, Leibniz, and Kant a millennium later and remains a core problem in philosophy of religion.

representativeWorks.title: 《宣讲》（Proslgion）
representativeWorks.content: 包含著名的「本体论证明」的小册子：上帝是「无法设想比之更伟大的存在」，若它只存在于思想中，则还能设想一个同样伟大且实际存在的——那将更伟大，矛盾。故上帝必然实际存在。康德的「存在不是谓词」反驳、罗素的「最伟大的岛屿」反例，全都从这段短论证开始。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Contains the ontological argument: God is 'that than which nothing greater can be conceived'; if He existed only in thought, a greater being could be conceived — contradiction. Therefore God must exist in reality. Kant's 'existence is not a predicate' and Russell's 'greatest island' parody all begin from this short argument.

representativeWorks.title: 《独白》
representativeWorks.content: 《宣讲》的姊妹篇，从经验事实（万物有等级、有来源）一步步推理出至善至高的存在，代表「后天」（宇宙论式）进路，与《宣讲》的先验进路互补。
representativeWorks.contentEn: The companion to the Proslogion, arguing a posteriori from grades of goodness and sources of being to a supreme being — the cosmological route complementing the ontological one.

coreThoughts.desc: 安瑟伦的论证可以这样走一遍：上帝被定义为「无法设想比之更伟大的存在」。它至少存在于思想中（你能想到这个定义）。但如果它只存在于思想中，那你就能设想一个「同样伟大并且实际存在」的存在——那显然比「仅存在于思想中」的上帝更伟大。于是「仅存在于思想中的上帝」就不是「无法设想比之更伟大的存在」了，矛盾。所以，为了不自相矛盾，上帝必须实际存在。这个论证的魅力和麻烦都在于：它宣称单凭「概念」就能推出「存在」，康德后来指出其漏洞——「存在」不是一个描述性质的谓词，「一千塔勒」并不因为被设想就真的存在。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：你把「最伟大的存在」想出来了，那它就必须存在——因为一个只存在于脑子里的「最伟大」，比不过一个真正存在的「最伟大」。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像你想象「最高的山」——既然想象里有一座最高的山，那么真正的最高峰就必须存在，否则你的想象还能再高一点，就不是「最高」了。
coreThoughts.l3: 标准表述（Proslogion 2-3）：上帝 = quo maius nihil cogitari potest。论证分两步：①仅思想中存在 → 可设想更伟大者 → 矛盾；②不可设想不存在的存在（necessarium）比可设想不存在者更伟大。后世：笛卡尔（第五沉思）、莱布尼茨（完备性论证）继承；康德「存在非谓词」、甘克尔（Gaunilo）「最完美岛屿」反驳。当代模态本体论（Plantinga）复兴该论证。
coreThoughts.descEn: God is 'that than which nothing greater can be conceived'. He exists at least in thought. But if He existed only in thought, a greater being — one existing in reality as well — could be conceived, contradicting His definition. Therefore God exists in reality. The charm and the trouble: existence is claimed to follow from a concept alone.
coreThoughts.l1En: Think of 'the greatest conceivable being' — then it must exist, because a merely imagined greatest loses to a real one.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like imagining 'the highest mountain': if your imagination contains a highest peak, the real one must exist, or your imagination could go higher.
coreThoughts.l3En: Standard form: God is that than which nothing greater can be conceived. (1) If He existed only in the understanding, a greater — existing also in reality — is conceivable, contradiction. (2) That which cannot be conceived not to exist is greater than what can. Descartes and Leibniz follow; Kant's 'existence is not a predicate' and Gaunilo's perfect island counter-attack; revived by Plantinga's modal version.

coreThoughts.desc: 安瑟伦给中世纪哲学立下的总纲：不是「理解了才信」，而是「信了再去理解」。信仰是起点而非终点——理性不是信仰的敌人，而是信仰的侍女与奖赏。这个态度决定了经院哲学的基本格局：哲学（理性）为神学（信仰）提供论证，而不是替代它。后来的阿奎那、司各脱都在这条线上工作。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：安瑟伦说「我信，是为了理解」——先站到信仰里，再用理性把你相信的东西想清楚。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像学游泳：先跳进水里（信），再学会换气（理解）——在岸上永远学不会。
coreThoughts.l3: fides quaerens intellectum 成为经院哲学的座右铭。它与「理解寻求信仰」（阿伯拉尔）相对，标示了信仰与理性之优先级的经典争论。安瑟伦另一名句：「我相信，为的是我能理解」（credo ut intelligam）。
coreThoughts.descEn: The motto of scholasticism: not 'understand, then believe', but 'believe, then understand'. Faith is the starting point, reason its servant and reward. This set the whole medieval pattern: philosophy argues for theology rather than replacing it.
coreThoughts.l1En: Anselm: 'I believe in order to understand' — stand inside faith first, then use reason to think it through.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like learning to swim: jump in (believe), then learn to breathe (understand).
coreThoughts.l3En: fides quaerens intellectum vs Abelard's understanding seeking faith — the classic debate on the priority of faith and reason. Also: 'credo ut intelligam' (I believe that I may understand).

famousEvents.title: 坎特伯雷之争
famousEvents.desc: 被英王威廉二世任命为坎特伯雷大主教后，安瑟伦与王权爆发「主教叙任权」之争，两度流亡罗马，坚持教权高于王权——中世纪政教关系的标志性事件。
famousEvents.descEn: As Archbishop of Canterbury he clashed with William II over investiture — who appoints bishops — twice exiled to Rome, insisting on church authority over royal power.

famousEvents.title: 本体论证明的诞生
famousEvents.desc: 据其传记，安瑟伦在祷告中突然获得「那个无法设想比之更伟大的存在」的洞见，激动不已，遂成《宣讲》第二章的论证——一个祷告中的灵感，变成了一千年的哲学考题。
famousEvents.descEn: According to his biographer, the insight 'that than which nothing greater can be conceived' struck Anselm in prayer; he hurried to write it down — an inspiration in prayer becoming a millennium of philosophical debate.

philosophers.scientificEval: 安瑟伦的「存在不是可分析的谓词」争论在逻辑学与语言哲学层面具有持久价值：当代模态逻辑（Plantinga 的可能世界论证）重新检验其结构，语言分析哲学则从「概念蕴含存在」这一命题出发发展出对存在量词的精微分析。他「信仰寻求理解」的纲领奠定了中世纪大学的理性训练传统，客观上为近代科学所需的论证规范准备了土壤。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: The ontological argument has lasting value in logic and philosophy of language: modal logic (Plantinga) retests its structure, and analytic philosophy analyzes 'existence' through its lens. His program of faith seeking understanding founded the rational training of medieval universities, objectively preparing the soil for modern scientific norms of argument.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 安瑟伦的哲学始终服务于一个目标：用最严密的理性为信仰奠基。他早年任教于诺曼底的贝克修道院（那里培养了一代经院学者），中年因神学争论写作《宣讲》《独白》，晚年则深陷政治斗争，在流亡中完成《上帝为何化身为人》（Cur Deus Homo），把「道成肉身」也论证成了理性上可理解的必然。他的一生示范了经院哲学的理想人格：修士与逻辑学家、神秘主义者与辩证法家，同一个人。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: Anselm's philosophy always served one goal: grounding faith in the strictest reason. Teacher at Bec, author of the Proslogion in mid-life, later embroiled in politics, he wrote Cur Deus Homo in exile, arguing even the Incarnation as rationally necessary. His life exemplifies the scholastic ideal: monk and logician, mystic and dialectician in one person.
philosophers.aiReview: 安瑟伦的「本体论证明」是人类思想史上被反驳次数最多、又不断复活的论证——这个事实本身就说明它触到了某种深层结构。批评它很容易（康德：存在不是谓词），但每次你以为已经埋葬了它，总会有人（最近是模态逻辑学家）把它挖出来重新打磨。更耐人寻味的是他「信仰寻求理解」的姿态：在现代人看来信仰和理性是对立的，安瑟伦却认为它们根本是一回事的两面——先决意相信，然后全力以赴去理解。你可以不同意他的前提，但不能不承认：能把一个祷告中的灵感经营成一千年后仍在辩论的哲学问题，这种思维的严谨与疯狂，都是罕见的。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: The ontological argument is the most refuted and most resurrected proof in intellectual history — a fact that suggests it touches something deep. Easy to attack (Kant: existence is not a predicate), yet every time it is buried, someone (recently modal logicians) digs it up and polishes it. His faith-seeking-understanding stance seems naive to moderns who oppose faith and reason; Anselm saw them as two faces of one act — resolve to believe, then think with all your might.

furtherReading.title: 安瑟伦《宣讲》（中译《论上帝存在》）
furtherReading.desc: 本体论证明原典，篇幅极短

philosophers.anecdote: 安瑟伦幼年曾梦见上帝邀他登上高山之巅吃「生命之粮」，醒来后终生以此为信念之源。晚年他面对英王的打压，留下名言：「你是在鞭打一个老修士。」——这位一生以逻辑服人的人，最后却以忍耐和顺服赢得尊敬。
philosophers.anecdoteEn: As a child he dreamed God invited him to the summit of a mountain to eat 'the bread of life' — a vision that anchored his faith for life. Pressured by the king in old age, he said, 'You are beating an old monk' — the great logician ultimately won respect through patience.

philosophers.name: 布鲁诺
philosophers.role: 文艺复兴自然哲学家，宇宙无限论的殉道者
philosophers.summary: 多明我会修士出身，因思想激进被逐出教团，从此在欧洲各国流浪讲学。他比哥白尼走得更远：不仅太阳不是宇宙中心，连宇宙本身都是无限的，有无数个世界、无数个太阳系，宇宙中不存在中心。他把宇宙的无限性上升为哲学命题——神是无限的，他的作品（宇宙）也必须是无限的。1600 年他在罗马鲜花广场被宗教裁判所烧死，成为科学史上最著名的殉道者之一。
philosophers.summaryEn: A Dominican friar expelled for radicalism, he wandered Europe lecturing. He went beyond Copernicus: not only is the sun not the center, the universe itself is infinite, containing countless worlds and suns, with no center at all. He elevated cosmic infinity to a philosophical thesis — God is infinite, so His work must be infinite too. Burned at the stake in Rome's Campo de' Fiori in 1600, he became one of science's most famous martyrs.

representativeWorks.title: 《论无限、宇宙与诸世界》
representativeWorks.content: 布鲁诺的核心著作：论证宇宙无限、有无数世界。他反驳亚里士多德「月下/月上」的等级宇宙观，主张宇宙的齐一性与无限性——这是对中世纪封闭宇宙论的彻底爆破。
representativeWorks.titleEn: On the Infinite Universe and Worlds
representativeWorks.contentEn: His core work: the universe is infinite with countless worlds. Against Aristotle's hierarchical cosmos he argues for uniformity and infinity — the radical demolition of the medieval closed universe.

representativeWorks.title: 《论原因、本原与太一》
representativeWorks.content: 哲学体系的形而上学基础：万物在「太一」中统一，形式与质料、神与自然是同一个东西的两面——一种泛神论的自然哲学，预示了斯宾诺莎。
representativeWorks.contentEn: The metaphysical basis of his system: all things are unified in the One; form and matter, God and nature are two faces of one substance — a pantheism that prefigures Spinoza.

coreThoughts.desc: 中世纪的标准宇宙观是亚里士多德-托勒密的封闭宇宙：地球居中，恒星天穹是宇宙的边界，天界与月下世界本质不同。布鲁诺把这个宇宙「炸开」：空间无限，恒星就是远方的太阳，行星围绕它们旋转，宇宙中处处相同——没有中心，没有边界，没有「天上人间」的等级。这个宇宙观不仅是天文学的革命，更是神学的革命：如果神是无限的，他的作品就不可能是有限的。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：布鲁诺说宇宙没有边、没有中心，满天的星星都是远方的太阳，周围也都绕着行星——地球只是无数世界里的一个。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像在一片没有尽头的海洋上，你不会说哪一滴水是「中心」——布鲁诺的宇宙就是这样一片没有岸的海洋。
coreThoughts.l3: 布鲁诺吸收哥白尼的日心说并推向极端：无限空间（infinito spazio）中星体均匀分布。他因此否定亚里士多德的自然位置/轻重之别，为惯性思想的出现扫清概念障碍；其「统一原则」预示斯宾诺莎的实体一元论。伽利略受其宇宙观启发，但科学上保持谨慎。
coreThoughts.conceptEn: The Infinite Universe and Many Worlds
coreThoughts.descEn: Bruno blows up the closed Aristotelian-Ptolemaic cosmos: space is infinite, stars are distant suns with their own planets, everywhere is the same — no center, no edge, no celestial hierarchy. A theological as much as astronomical revolution: an infinite God cannot have a finite work.
coreThoughts.l1En: The universe has no edge and no center; every star is a distant sun with planets around it — Earth is just one of countless worlds.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like an endless ocean where no drop is 'the center' — Bruno's cosmos is an ocean without shores.
coreThoughts.l3En: He radicalized Copernicus: infinite space with uniformly distributed stars; denied Aristotle's natural places and the heavy/light distinction, clearing conceptual ground for inertia; his unity principle prefigures Spinoza's monism. Galileo took inspiration but scientific caution.

coreThoughts.desc: 布鲁诺的形而上学：万物是一个「太一」（Uno）的不同显现，神即自然（Deus sive Natura），形式与质料不可分，无限与有限在存在中统一。这不是传统的有神论（神在宇宙之外创造它），而是内在论：神是宇宙的生命、力量和必然性本身。这套思想让他在当时被视为危险分子，却在两个世纪后成为斯宾诺莎和德国浪漫派的先驱。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：布鲁诺认为神不在宇宙外面「造」宇宙，神就是宇宙本身的生命与法则——万物都是同一个本体的模样。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像一棵树：树干、枝叶、果实各不相同，但都是同一棵树的生命——布鲁诺说，万物就是那个「太一」长出的枝叶。
coreThoughts.l3: 「太一」概念源于新柏拉图主义（普罗提诺），布鲁诺将其彻底自然化：形式内在于物质，物质本身即神圣。其「对立面的一致」（coincidentia oppositorum）吸收库萨的尼古拉，后经斯宾诺莎、谢林、黑格尔而进入德国观念论主流。
coreThoughts.descEn: All things are manifestations of one 'Uno': God is Nature (Deus sive Natura), form and matter inseparable, the infinite and finite unified. Not theism (God outside the world) but immanence: God is the life, power, and necessity of the cosmos itself. A dangerous doctrine then; the forerunner of Spinoza and German Romanticism.
coreThoughts.l1En: God does not create the universe from outside — God is the universe's own life and law; all things are faces of one substance.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a tree: trunk, leaves, fruit all differ, yet all are one life — things are the branches the One grows.
coreThoughts.l3En: The One (Neoplatonic in origin) is naturalized: form is in matter; matter is divine. The coincidence of opposites (from Nicholas of Cusa) flows through Spinoza, Schelling, and Hegel into German idealism.

famousEvents.title: 流亡欧洲十五载
famousEvents.desc: 因质疑三位一体等教义被控异端，布鲁诺逃离意大利，辗转日内瓦、巴黎、伦敦、法兰克福等地，在牛津等大学讲学辩论，以雄辩和古怪著称。
famousEvents.descEn: Charged with heresy for questioning the Trinity, he fled Italy and wandered Geneva, Paris, London, Frankfurt, lecturing and debating at Oxford and other universities, famous for eloquence and eccentricity.

famousEvents.title: 鲜花广场的火刑
famousEvents.desc: 1592 年在威尼斯被捕，押送罗马宗教裁判所，监禁八年拒绝悔罪。1600 年 2 月 17 日，在罗马鲜花广场被烧死。行刑前他拒绝亲吻十字架，据说留下遗言：「你们宣判时的恐惧，也许比我赴死时的恐惧更大。」
famousEvents.titleEn: The Fire in Campo de' Fiori
famousEvents.descEn: Arrested in Venice in 1592, tried in Rome for eight years, he refused to recant. On 17 February 1600 he was burned at the stake in Campo de' Fiori, refusing the crucifix; his reported last words: 'Perhaps your fear in passing this sentence is greater than mine in receiving it.'

philosophers.scientificEval: 布鲁诺不是实验科学家，但他的无限宇宙论在概念层面为近代天文学清障：它否定了「天界与月下的绝对区分」和「自然位置」理论，为惯性原理和统一物理学的思想提供了宇宙论前提。他关于恒星即远方的太阳、行星绕其运行的观点被 19 世纪天文观测证实。历史学上，他的死被普遍视为思想自由与宗教权威冲突的象征事件。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: Not an experimental scientist, Bruno nonetheless cleared conceptual ground for modern astronomy: abolishing the heaven/earth distinction and natural places prepared the way for inertia and unified physics. His vision of stars as distant suns with orbiting planets was confirmed by nineteenth-century observation. His death became the symbol of thought's freedom versus authority.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 布鲁诺的思想有一个坚定的核心：把「无限」贯彻到底。神是无限的→宇宙必须无限→空间无限→诸世界无限→物质永恒→万物统一于太一。每一条都是对上一条的逻辑推进。他在伦敦时期（1583-1585）写作最丰，哲学体系基本成型；此后十五年他在欧洲的流亡与辩论，更像是把这个体系像火种一样播撒。1592 年的被捕，几乎是这套「无限」哲学的必然结局——他拒绝为有限的世界观收回无限的宇宙。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: Bruno's thought has one firm core: push 'infinity' to the end. God is infinite, therefore the universe, space, and worlds are infinite; matter is eternal; all is unified in the One. Each thesis follows from the last. His London years (1583-85) produced the mature system; the exile that followed was its propagation; the arrest of 1592 was almost the necessary conclusion — he refused to retract an infinite universe for a finite worldview.
philosophers.aiReview: 布鲁诺的形象充满张力：对后世他是科学的殉道者、自由思想的英雄；对当时的他，自己的死因其实主要是神学异端（质疑三位一体、基督神性），宇宙论只是其中一条罪状。这提醒我们，历史的叙事常常比事实更整齐。但无论如何，他在概念层面对「封闭宇宙」的爆破是真实的贡献——没有他，哥白尼的日心说可能仍只是「另一种数学模型」而非「我们住在无限宇宙的一个角落里」这一令人眩晕的洞见。他的泛神论与宇宙无限论，两个世纪后仍滋养着斯宾诺莎、歌德与浪漫派。烧死一个敢于把宇宙想「大」的人，是人类思想史上最昂贵的错误定价之一。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Bruno's image is full of tension: martyr of science to posterity, heretic to his contemporaries — his death was mainly about theology (Trinity, Christ's divinity), cosmology being one charge among many. History's narratives are neater than facts. Yet his conceptual demolition of the closed cosmos is real: without him, heliocentrism might have remained 'another mathematical model' rather than the vertigo of 'we live in a corner of an infinite universe'. His pantheism and cosmic infinity still nourished Spinoza, Goethe, and the Romantics two centuries later.

furtherReading.title: 《论无限、宇宙与诸世界》（中译本）
furtherReading.desc: 布鲁诺核心著作，宇宙无限论的宣言

philosophers.anecdote: 布鲁诺一生都以「诺拉努斯」（取自故乡诺拉）自称，意为「不归者」——他似乎早就知道自己回不去。在牛津辩论时，他因衣着古怪、言辞狂放被嘲笑为「意大利的丑角」；行刑那天，罗马鲜花广场的人群据说比过节还多。1889 年，意大利人在广场为他立起雕像，底座朝向梵蒂冈——当年烧死他的地方，如今是他永久的纪念碑。
philosophers.anecdoteEn: He called himself 'Nolanus' (from his hometown Nola) — 'the one who does not return', as if he knew. At Oxford he was mocked as 'the Italian jester'. In 1889, Italians erected his statue in Campo de' Fiori, facing the Vatican — a permanent monument on the very site of his execution.

philosophers.name: 蒙田
philosophers.role: 随笔文体开创者，近代怀疑论与人文主义的代表
philosophers.summary: 法国波尔多贵族、法官，38 岁隐退乡间城堡，以「我知道什么？」（Que sais-je?）为座右铭，写下了 107 篇《随笔集》——一种全新的文体，也是欧洲第一次大规模地「写自己」。他考察风俗、教育、死亡、友谊、食人族……以彻底的怀疑检验一切「理所当然」，又以惊人的宽容拥抱人类的全部差异。帕斯卡称他为「认识自己的人」，莎士比亚、培根、笛卡尔、爱默生都从他那座塔楼的书房里借过火。
philosophers.summaryEn: A Bordeaux nobleman and magistrate who retired to his castle at 38, adopting 'What do I know?' (Que sais-je?) as his motto and writing 107 Essays — a new genre and Europe's first large-scale project of writing the self. He examines customs, education, death, friendship, cannibals, testing every 'obvious' truth with radical doubt and embracing human difference with astonishing tolerance. Pascal called him 'the man who knew himself'; Shakespeare, Bacon, Descartes, and Emerson all borrowed fire from his library tower.

representativeWorks.title: 《随笔集》
representativeWorks.content: 三卷 107 篇随笔，从《论友谊》《论死亡》到《论食人族》《论儿童教育》。以自身为标本解剖人性，以怀疑为刀切开一切教条——现代散文与自传文学的起点，也是近代人文主义的宣言书。
representativeWorks.contentEn: 107 essays in three books, from friendship and death to cannibals and education. Dissecting humanity with the self as specimen and cutting dogma with doubt — the origin of the modern essay and autobiography, and a manifesto of Renaissance humanism.

coreThoughts.desc: 蒙田的怀疑论不是要摧毁知识，而是要人诚实：理性并不比习俗更可靠，感官会骗人，所谓「真理」常常只是习惯。但他没有停在虚无——他问「我知道什么？」，意思是：既然我不能确定，我就要学会与不确定共处，宽容不同答案，过好眼前的生活。这是一种「愉快的怀疑论」：放下对确定性的执念，反而获得了自由。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：蒙田说「我什么也不敢确定」——但这不是绝望，而是放下：既然都想不通，就别为想不通的事打架，好好过日子。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像雾天开车：你没法看清整条路（确定性），但你可以慢下来、看近处、稳稳地开——蒙田教你在这团雾里从容。
coreThoughts.l3: 蒙田受皮浪主义（经由塞克斯都·恩披里柯）启发，但将其温和化：怀疑（doute）导向宽容（tolérance）与自然生活。他率先以「食人族」等异文化反观欧洲文明的「野蛮」，是文化相对主义的重要先驱；其方法论（以自我为观察对象）预示了近代经验心理学。
coreThoughts.descEn: Montaigne's skepticism is not destructive but honest: reason is no more reliable than custom; senses deceive; 'truth' is often habit. Since certainty is unattainable, learn to live with uncertainty — tolerate different answers and live well. A cheerful skepticism: letting go of the demand for certainty is itself liberation.
coreThoughts.l1En: Montaigne: 'I am not sure of anything' — not despair but relief: if we cannot settle everything, let's not fight over it; let's live well.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like driving in fog: you can't see the whole road, but you can slow down, watch close, and drive steadily.
coreThoughts.l3En: Inspired by Pyrrhonism via Sextus Empiricus but softened: doubt leads to tolerance and natural living. His use of the cannibals to mirror European 'barbarism' makes him an early cultural relativist; his method of self-observation prefigures empirical psychology.

coreThoughts.desc: 蒙田把「认识你自己」（德尔斐箴言）变成了一生的工程：通过诚实地记录自己的欲望、怯懦、身体、情绪，来认识普遍的人性。他说「我就是我这本书的题材」——这部自我之书之所以是哲学，是因为他相信：没有人比我更了解人性，因为我就是一个人。随笔（essai）一词本义是「尝试」，蒙田用一生证明：思想不必是体系，可以是持续的自我拷问。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：蒙田说要想了解人，最好的标本就是自己——他把自己的一切（包括拉屎放屁）都写进书里，因为「我就是一个人」。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像医生解剖自己：蒙田拿起手术刀，先解剖的是他自己——因为他认为天下人的心都差不多。
coreThoughts.l3: 蒙田开创「主体性写作」传统：哲学不再谈论抽象的人，而是一个具体的「我」的生活。其文体（essai = 尝试）与内容（自我审视）共同构成现代自传与随笔的范式，深刻影响笛卡尔的《方法谈》（虽然后者走向确定性）、卢梭《忏悔录》与帕斯卡《思想录》。
coreThoughts.descEn: Montaigne turned 'know yourself' into a life's work: record honestly your desires, cowardice, body, moods, to know universal human nature. 'I am myself the matter of my book.' The essay (essai = attempt) proves thought need not be a system; it can be sustained self-examination.
coreThoughts.l1En: To understand humans, the best specimen is yourself — Montaigne wrote everything about himself because 'I am a man'.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a doctor dissecting himself: Montaigne's scalpel went first into his own flesh, since all hearts are alike.
coreThoughts.l3En: He founded subjective writing: philosophy about a concrete 'I', not abstract Man. The essay form and self-examination shaped Descartes' Discourse, Rousseau's Confessions, and Pascal's Pensées.

famousEvents.title: 隐退塔楼书房
famousEvents.desc: 38 岁那年，蒙田卖掉官职，退隐家族城堡，在塔楼书房刻满希腊拉丁格言，开始写作随笔。「我退休了，我把余生献给我自己。」
famousEvents.descEn: At 38 he sold his office, retired to the family castle, covered his library tower with Greek and Latin maxims, and began writing. 'I retire; I dedicate my remaining life to myself.'

famousEvents.title: 波尔多市长
famousEvents.desc: 他两次当选波尔多市长（1581、1583），在宗教战争的血腥年代以调解与宽容著称——一个怀疑论者成了乱世中最稳的治理者。
famousEvents.descEn: Elected mayor of Bordeaux twice (1581, 1583), he governed with moderation during the Wars of Religion — a skeptic proving the steadiest hand in troubled times.

philosophers.scientificEval: 蒙田对感官可靠性的怀疑（《为雷蒙·塞邦辩护》）系统整理了古代怀疑论的论据，为笛卡尔的普遍怀疑提供了问题清单与动力——笛卡尔的方法论怀疑正是对「蒙田式怀疑」的认真回应。其文化相对主义、宽容理论与对「自然」的观察兴趣，为近代人类学、教育学（洛克、卢梭）与宗教宽容传统提供了直接资源。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: His Apology for Raymond Sebond systematized ancient skeptical arguments, supplying Descartes with the agenda for universal doubt — the Discourse is a serious answer to Montaigne's doubt. His cultural relativism, tolerance, and observational interest in nature fed modern anthropology, education theory (Locke, Rousseau), and the tradition of religious toleration.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 蒙田的思想轨迹是「从法官到怀疑者」：早年做法官时，他目睹司法不公与宗教屠杀，对「确信」产生了本能的警惕；36 岁翻译塞克斯都·恩披里柯的《皮浪主义纲要》（拉丁文），系统地接受了怀疑论；此后 20 年，他把怀疑从认识论问题转化为生活方式——不是否定一切，而是对一切「暂且悬置」，留出空间给宽容与生活本身。他晚年修改《随笔集》时不断增补，正如人生没有定稿。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: His arc runs 'from magistrate to skeptic': witnessing judicial injustice and religious slaughter bred distrust of certainty; at 36 he translated Sextus Empiricus' Outlines of Pyrrhonism, systematically absorbing skepticism; for twenty years he turned doubt from an epistemological issue into a way of life — suspending judgment to make room for tolerance and living itself. He kept revising the Essays until his death, as life has no final draft.
philosophers.aiReview: 蒙田是现代人的「哲学安慰剂」：当你被体系的严密压得喘不过气，或者被教条的自信激怒，读他几页就能缓过来。他开创的随笔文体让哲学第一次可以像聊天一样进行；他「我知道什么？」的座右铭比任何宏大体系都更经得起时间。当然，批评者会说：他的怀疑是舒服的怀疑，他在城堡里讨论食人族，却对自己庄园的农奴视而不见——「贵族的怀疑论」。这话不算冤枉，但也别苛求：在宗教战争烧遍欧洲的年代，一个主张「别为观点杀人」的人，已经是在逆流而行。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Montaigne is modern philosophy's comfort: when systems crush you or dogmatic confidence enrages you, a few pages restore you. He made philosophy conversational; his 'What do I know?' outlasts any grand system. Critics: his doubt was comfortable — discussing cannibals from a castle while serfs worked below, 'an aristocrat's skepticism'. Not entirely unfair; but in an age when religious war burned Europe, one who said 'don't kill for opinions' was already swimming upstream.

furtherReading.title: 《蒙田随笔全集》（马振骋中译本）
furtherReading.desc: 三卷全译，第 3 卷《论经验》尤其精彩

philosophers.anecdote: 蒙田最著名的逸事是「摔跤」：1588 年他在巴黎街头被一群暴徒劫持，同行者被杀，他凭沉着和机智脱险。事后他写道，那一刻他像哲学家一样接受了死亡的可能，却发现「活着真好」。他还说自己的记忆力坏到「刚借出书就忘了」，但他把这当成美德——健忘的人不容易记仇。
philosophers.anecdoteEn: His most famous adventure: in 1588 Paris street thugs seized him; companions were killed, he escaped through composure and wit, afterward writing that he had accepted death 'like a philosopher' and found life sweet. He claimed his memory was so bad he forgot books the moment he lent them — and called it a virtue: forgetful people bear no grudges.

relationships.description: 视苏格拉底为「认识你自己」的师祖与怀疑的榜样
通过塞克斯都·恩披里柯继承皮浪主义怀疑论

philosophers.name: 帕斯卡
philosophers.role: 数学家、物理学家、哲学家，概率论奠基人之一
philosophers.summary: 天才中的天才：12 岁独立证明欧几里得定理，16 岁写出《圆锥曲线论》，19 岁发明世界上第一台机械计算器（帕斯卡加法器），26 岁通过真空实验证明气压随高度变化。在科学巅峰之际，他经历「火之夜」的神秘体验，转向宗教与哲学，留下《思想录》——一部未完成的护教著作，却成为法国古典散文的巅峰和存在哲学的先声。他的「赌注论证」：上帝是否存在无法证明，但相信的期望收益是无限的——至今仍是理性决策论与宗教哲学的核心案例。
philosophers.summaryEn: A genius among geniuses: at 12 he independently proved Euclid, at 16 wrote on conic sections, at 19 invented the first mechanical calculator, at 26 demonstrated barometric pressure with vacuum experiments. At his scientific peak he experienced a 'night of fire' and turned to religion and philosophy, leaving Pensées — an unfinished apology that became the summit of French classical prose and a prelude to existential philosophy. His wager: God's existence cannot be proven, but the expected payoff of belief is infinite — still a core case in decision theory and philosophy of religion.

representativeWorks.title: 《思想录》
representativeWorks.content: 未完成的护教著作，由草稿与断片汇编而成。全书围绕「人的伟大与可悲」：人是会思想的芦苇，既知道自己的渺小又渴望无限。「赌注论证」「两种无限」「几何精神与敏感精神」都出自这里。它比任何体系都更接近现代人的精神困境。
representativeWorks.contentEn: An unfinished apology assembled from notes and fragments. Centered on 'the greatness and misery of man': man is a thinking reed, aware of his smallness yet longing for the infinite. The wager, the two infinites, the esprit de géométrie and esprit de finesse all originate here — closer to modern spiritual predicament than any system.

representativeWorks.title: 《致外省人信札》
representativeWorks.content: 为冉森派辩护、抨击耶稣会道德松弛的十八封信札，以锋芒毕露的讽刺与严密逻辑闻名，被视为法国散文与讽刺文学的典范。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Eighteen letters defending Jansenism and attacking Jesuit casuistry — famous for sharp irony and rigorous logic, a model of French prose and satire.

representativeWorks.title: 《论液体的平衡与空气的重量》
representativeWorks.content: 总结其真空与大气压实验：真空可以在自然界中存在，气压随高度下降。帕斯卡压强的概念直接奠基了流体静力学。
representativeWorks.titleEn: Treatises on the Equilibrium of Liquids and the Weight of Air
representativeWorks.contentEn: His vacuum and barometric experiments: nature abhors no vacuum, and air has weight. The concept of pressure founded hydrostatics.

coreThoughts.desc: 帕斯卡的名言：人的全部尊严就在于思想。宇宙可以轻易碾碎我——一阵风、一滴水——但我仍然比杀死我的宇宙高贵，因为我「知道」自己被杀死，而宇宙不知道。这句话同时道出了人的伟大（思想）与可悲（脆弱）。在帕斯卡看来，现代人的困境就在这伟大与可悲之间：我们知道太多以至于不能无知地快乐，知道太少以至于不能确定地安心。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：人是宇宙里最脆弱的芦苇，但会思想的芦苇比杀死它的宇宙更尊贵——因为只有人知道自己在想什么。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像一根在暴风雨里摇摆的芦苇：它会被折断，但它知道自己会断——宇宙不知道自己在做什么，芦苇知道。
coreThoughts.l3: 帕斯卡的人学：双重的无限（无限大与无限小之间的人）、双重的深渊。人是「中间者」（milieu），既非天使也非野兽，正是这中间状态构成了人的尊严与悲剧。存在主义（克尔凯郭尔、加缪）反复回到这个起点。
coreThoughts.descEn: Man's whole dignity lies in thought. The universe can crush me — a vapor, a drop of water — yet I am nobler than what kills me, because I know I am dying, and the universe knows nothing. Greatness and misery in one image; the modern condition between too much and too little knowledge.
coreThoughts.l1En: Man is the frailest reed, but a thinking reed is nobler than the universe that kills it — only man knows what he thinks.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a reed in a storm: it will break, but it knows it will break — the universe does not know what it does; the reed does.
coreThoughts.l3En: His anthropology: man between the two infinites, the 'middle' creature, neither angel nor beast — this middle state is his dignity and his tragedy. Kierkegaard and Camus return here.

coreThoughts.desc: 帕斯卡面对的问题是：理性无法证明上帝存在，但人必须选择信或不信。于是他把它变成一个决策问题——如果信而上帝存在，你得无限；信而上帝不存在，你损失有限；不信而上帝存在，你失无限；不信而上帝不存在，你所得有限。期望值计算：赌「信」的期望收益是无穷大，所以理性的人应该信。这个论证不是证明上帝存在，而是证明「信」是理性上划算的赌注——它被后世博弈论、决策论反复研究，也常被批评（「你无法选择相信什么」）。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：帕斯卡说信不信上帝没法用道理证明，那就用算账：信了如果真有，赚翻天；信了如果没真，也没亏什么——这买卖理性上划算。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像买一张彩票：中奖概率不高，但万一中了是无穷大——帕斯卡说信仰就是这么一张「期望值无限大」的彩票。
coreThoughts.l3: 帕斯卡赌注（Pascal's Wager）的期望值论证：P(上帝)×∞ − 有限成本 > 0。批评：①信念无法自愿获得（克利福德、威廉·詹姆斯回应）；②「许多神」问题——为何是基督教的神而非别的神；③多神论赌注使论证失效。但它开启了对宗教信念的决策论分析。
coreThoughts.descEn: Reason cannot prove God, yet one must choose. So Pascal frames it as a decision problem: if you believe and God exists, infinite gain; believe and He doesn't, finite loss; don't believe and He exists, infinite loss. Expected value: belief is the rational bet. Not a proof of God, but of belief as rational — studied ever since in game and decision theory.
coreThoughts.l1En: Faith can't be proven, so do the math: believe and if God exists, infinite win; believe and if not, little lost — rationally, belief is the better deal.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a lottery ticket with infinite expected value: the odds may be low, but the prize is infinite.
coreThoughts.l3En: The wager's expected-value form: P(God)×∞ − finite cost > 0. Criticisms: belief is not voluntarily acquired (Clifford, James); the many-gods problem; infinite expected value is ill-defined. Yet it opened decision-theoretic analysis of religious belief.

famousEvents.title: 火之夜
famousEvents.desc: 1654 年 11 月 23 日夜，帕斯卡经历约两小时的强烈宗教体验，写下著名的「纪念」（Mémorial）：「火。亚伯拉罕的上帝，以撒的上帝，雅各的上帝，不是哲学家和学者的上帝。」他把这张纸缝进外套内衬，终身随身携带。
famousEvents.descEn: On the night of 23 November 1654, Pascal underwent an intense two-hour religious experience and wrote the famous Mémorial: 'Fire. God of Abraham, God of Isaac, God of Jacob — not of the philosophers and scholars.' He sewed the paper into his coat lining and wore it for life.

famousEvents.title: 第一次近代思想论战
famousEvents.desc: 《致外省人信札》卷起轩然大波，也把冉森派与耶稣会的争论推向全欧洲，被视为「第一次现代知识分子论战」。
famousEvents.descEn: The Letters stirred Europe-wide controversy between Jansenists and Jesuits — called the first modern intellectual controversy.

philosophers.scientificEval: 帕斯卡的科学贡献可列入数学史前二十：16 岁《圆锥曲线论》提出帕斯卡定理；19 岁发明加法器（计算机硬件史的重要节点）；与费马通信奠定概率论基础；大气压与真空实验确立帕斯卡原理（压强）。其「无限小」思想（无穷小分析）直接通向微积分。科学史上罕见地集纯数学、实验物理、哲学、神学于一身。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: Pascal's science ranks in the mathematical top tier: Pascal's theorem at 16; the mechanical calculator at 19 (a milestone in hardware history); correspondence with Fermat founding probability theory; barometric experiments establishing Pascal's principle. His infinitesimal thinking leads directly to calculus. Rarely has one person combined pure mathematics, experimental physics, philosophy, and theology.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 帕斯卡的一生是两次转向：第一次，从法律世家之子转向科学（12-30 岁），把才华全部投入数学与物理；第二次，从科学转向宗教（31-39 岁），「火之夜」之后，他认为科学的无限并不能抚慰心灵的无垠——「几何学家的精神」之外还需要「敏感的精神」。他晚年计划写一部护教著作《为基督教辩护》，只留下成堆的断片，即《思想录》。科学的帕斯卡与信仰的帕斯卡不是两个人，而是同一个人的两次尝试：一次试图理解世界，一次试图理解自己在世界中的位置。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: Two turnings: first from a lawyer's family to science (ages 12-30), pouring talent into mathematics and physics; second from science to religion (31-39) — after the Night of Fire, scientific infinity could not console the infinity of the heart: beyond the geometrical mind lies the intuitive one. His planned apology became only fragments: the Pensées. The scientific and the believing Pascal are one person making two attempts: to understand the world, and to understand his place in it.
philosophers.aiReview: 帕斯卡是「天才的多重宇宙」：他可以在同一周里推进概率论、写讽刺信、设计公交车（他提议的巴黎公共交通）——然后说这一切都比不上「安静地坐在房间里」。他的《思想录》之所以不朽，是因为它诚实地展示了一个聪明到极点的人如何在意义问题上束手无策：「这无限空间的永恒沉默让我恐惧。」两百年后，尼采和加缪面对的是同一个沉默。批评者会指出赌注论证的功利色彩和「火之夜」的不可验证，但帕斯卡从不声称自己有答案——他声称的是：这个问题值得你赌上一切，而假装它不存在，是唯一真正的错误。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Pascal is a multiverse of genius: advancing probability, writing satire, designing buses — then saying all of it matters less than 'sitting quietly in a room'. The Pensées endure because they honestly show a supremely clever man at his wit's end over meaning: 'The eternal silence of these infinite spaces terrifies me.' Nietzsche and Camus face the same silence. Critics note the wager's utilitarianism and the unverifiability of the Night of Fire; but Pascal never claimed answers — only that the question is worth everything, and pretending it away is the one real error.

furtherReading.title: 《思想录》（何兆武中译本）
furtherReading.desc: 帕斯卡断片集，法国散文巅峰

philosophers.anecdote: 帕斯卡 31 岁「火之夜」后，他的生活简化为祈祷与苦修。他腰间系着带刺的腰带，提醒自己谦卑；他停止一切「无用的」科学工作（尽管偶尔忍不住验证新发现）。他最后一次科学活动是 1662 年：有人告诉他牙疼处有疼痛，他竟设计出某种缓解方法——研究者至今不清楚那是什么装置。39 岁去世时，他留下的除了《思想录》断片，还有那句著名的：「耶稣将临到我的灵魂里。」
philosophers.anecdoteEn: After the Night of Fire, his life became prayer and austerity: a spiked belt to humble the flesh, science abandoned as 'useless' (though curiosity occasionally leaked). His last scientific act in 1662: on hearing someone's toothache, he devised some remedy — historians still don't know what. He died at 39 leaving the Pensées fragments and the words: 'Jesus will come into my soul.'

goldenQuotes.text: 这无限空间的永恒沉默使我恐惧。

goldenQuotes.text: 人是宇宙中一颗微粒，却比杀死他的宇宙更高贵——因为他知道自己会死。
goldenQuotes.textEn: Man is but a reed, the feeblest in nature, but he is a thinking reed. The universe knows not that it kills; man knows he dies.

philosophers.name: 伏尔泰
philosophers.role: 启蒙运动的旗手，思想自由的象征
philosophers.summary: 启蒙时代最耀眼的明星：哲学家、剧作家、诗人、历史学家、科学家与公共知识分子于一身。他一生与专制和教权作战——两次入巴士底狱、被流放英国、长期流亡瑞士，以笔为剑写下《哲学通信》《老实人》《哲学辞典》等巨著。他那句「我不同意你的观点，但我誓死捍卫你说话的权利」虽为后人概括，却精准定格了他的精神：宽容、理性、战斗。他活了 84 岁，在旧制度的心脏巴黎迎来了万人空巷的凯旋——启蒙的胜利，在他活着的时候就已发生。
philosophers.summaryEn: The brightest star of the Enlightenment: philosopher, playwright, poet, historian, scientist, and public intellectual in one. He fought despotism and clerical power all his life — twice in the Bastille, exiled to England, long in Swiss exile — writing Philosophical Letters, Candide, and the Philosophical Dictionary with a pen as sword. 'I disapprove of what you say, but I will defend to the death your right to say it' (attributed) captured his spirit: tolerance, reason, combat. He lived to 84 and entered Paris to a triumphant welcome — the Enlightenment's victory happened in his lifetime.

representativeWorks.title: 《哲学通信》
representativeWorks.content: 英国流亡期间写给法国同胞的二十五封信：介绍牛顿科学、洛克经验论、英国的政治制度与宗教宽容，对比法国的专制与教权。这本书被巴黎高等法院下令焚毁，却成为启蒙运动的思想动员书——「把英国的自由带给法国」。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Twenty-five letters from English exile introducing Newton, Locke, English institutions, and religious toleration, contrasting them with French absolutism. Burned by the Paris parlement, yet the Enlightenment's manifesto — bringing English liberty to France.

representativeWorks.title: 《老实人》
representativeWorks.content: 讽刺莱布尼茨「一切皆善」的哲理小说：老实人历经地震、战争、酷刑与欺骗，终于得出「我们必须耕种我们的花园」的结论。公认的启蒙文学杰作与法国文学经典。
representativeWorks.contentEn: A philosophical novel satirizing Leibniz's 'all is for the best': Candide suffers earthquake, war, torture, and fraud before concluding 'we must cultivate our garden'. A masterpiece of Enlightenment literature.

representativeWorks.title: 《哲学辞典》
representativeWorks.content: 以辞典词条形式展开的启蒙批判：从「上帝」「灵魂」到「宽容」「自由」，逐条拆解教条与迷信。笔锋辛辣，是伏尔泰「理性法庭」的最终呈现。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Enlightenment critique in dictionary form: from God and soul to toleration and liberty, dismantling dogma and superstition entry by entry — the razor wit of Voltaire's court of reason.

coreThoughts.desc: 伏尔泰一生都在为「宽容」辩护：宽容不是软弱，而是理性的必然——既然理性无法证明唯一的真理，禁止别人思考就是最大的非理性。他在著名的卡拉斯案（1762）中为一个被宗教偏执冤杀的商人家庭奔走六年，最终平反，也把「宗教宽容」从一个道德愿望变成了一项公共事业。宽容不等于什么都信，而是「我不同意你，但你有权说出来」——这是现代自由主义的第一课。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：伏尔泰说谁都没有资格垄断真理，所以谁都无权堵别人的嘴——宽容不是软弱，是理性。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像开灯的房间：一盏灯照不亮所有角落，多几盏灯大家才都看得清——伏尔泰让思想也多点几盏灯。
coreThoughts.l3: 伏尔泰的宽容论是洛克《论宗教宽容》的激进实践化：从「政府不应干涉信仰」推进到「社会不应迫害异见」。卡拉斯案（Calas affair）是其理论的社会实验场。其「我不同意你的观点，但誓死捍卫你说话的权利」成为自由主义的核心格言（实际出处存疑，通常归于其门徒）。
coreThoughts.descEn: Toleration is not weakness but rational necessity: since reason cannot prove a single truth, forbidding others to think is the greatest irrationality. His six-year campaign for the Calas family (1762), victims of religious bigotry, made toleration a public cause. Tolerance is not believing everything — it is 'I disagree, but you have the right to speak'.
coreThoughts.l1En: No one holds a monopoly on truth, so no one has the right to silence others. Tolerance is not weakness; it is reason.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a room with lamps: one lamp leaves corners dark; more lamps let everyone see.
coreThoughts.l3En: Voltaire radicalized Locke's toleration: from 'the state must not dictate belief' to 'society must not persecute dissent'. The Calas affair was his social laboratory. 'I disapprove of what you say but defend to the death your right to say it' became liberalism's core slogan (attribution debated).

coreThoughts.desc: 伏尔泰是「进步观念」的旗手：历史不是神意的剧本，而是人类理性与愚昧斗争的过程；科学（牛顿）、哲学（洛克）与自由制度每前进一寸，人类的苦难就减少一分。他写作《风俗论》——第一部真正意义上的世界文明史，把目光从欧洲帝王转向各民族的风俗、技艺与思想。他相信的进步不是盲目的乐观（《老实人》恰恰讽刺乐观主义），而是「看清世界之后仍然行动」的清醒理性主义。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：伏尔泰认为历史不是神写好的剧本，而是理性和愚昧拔河——科学、宽容、自由每进一步，人就少受一分苦。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像拔河：绳子中间的红布条（文明的成果）会来回移动，但只要你这边多一个人用力（理性），它迟早会滑向这边。
coreThoughts.l3: 《风俗论》（Essai sur les mœurs）是西方史学从「帝王编年」转向「文明史」的里程碑：以文化、经济、风俗为纲，把中国、印度、伊斯兰纳入欧洲视野。其「进步」观念经孔多塞、孔德发展为历史哲学主流，也埋下后来「历史进步主义」的争论。
coreThoughts.descEn: History is not a divine script but the struggle of reason against ignorance: every inch gained by science, toleration, and liberty reduces human suffering. His Essay on the Manners of Nations was the first true world history of civilization, shifting the gaze from kings to customs, arts, and ideas. His progressivism is not blind optimism (Candide satirizes that) but lucid rationalism that acts after seeing clearly.
coreThoughts.l1En: History is a tug-of-war between reason and ignorance — every step of science, tolerance, and freedom lessens suffering.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a tug-of-war: the marker sways, but each extra rational hand pulls it eventually to your side.
coreThoughts.l3En: The Essai sur les mœurs turned historiography from dynastic chronicle to civilization history, including China, India, and Islam in the European gaze. Progress became the mainstream of philosophy of history via Condorcet and Comte — and a permanent controversy.

famousEvents.title: 卡拉斯案
famousEvents.desc: 图卢兹新教徒让·卡拉斯被诬杀子而处以磔刑。伏尔泰调查后认定冤案，发表《论宽容》并奔走六年，1765 年卡拉斯平反。宗教宽容从口号变成制度性胜利的转折点。
famousEvents.descEn: Protestant Jean Calas was broken on the wheel on false charges of murdering his son. Voltaire investigated, published Treatise on Toleration, and campaigned for six years; Calas was exonerated in 1765 — toleration turned from slogan into institutional victory.

famousEvents.title: 巴士底狱与流亡
famousEvents.desc: 因讽刺摄政王的诗作被关入巴士底狱十一个月，出狱后与骑士罗昂发生冲突再次入狱，随后流亡英国三年——正是这次流亡催生了《哲学通信》。
famousEvents.descEn: Imprisoned in the Bastille for eleven months for a satirical poem, later jailed again after a quarrel with a noble, then exiled to England for three years — the exile that produced the Philosophical Letters.

famousEvents.title: 巴黎的凯旋
famousEvents.desc: 84 岁高龄重返巴黎，万人空巷迎接；法兰西学院为他塑像。两个月后他在巴黎逝世——启蒙哲学家以胜利者的姿态完成了人生谢幕。
famousEvents.descEn: Returning to Paris at 84, he received a hero's welcome; the Académie française honored him. He died two months later — the Enlightenment philosopher's triumphant exit.

philosophers.scientificEval: 伏尔泰是牛顿科学在法国的首席传播者：他亲自主持法国的牛顿实验复现（光学实验、万有引力解释），其《牛顿哲学原理》一书把微积分与万有引力引入法语世界，被视为法国科学现代化的催化剂。他参与「地球形状之争」（支持牛顿的扁球说，反对笛卡尔的椭球说），并以实验数据支持，堪称科学传播与科学辩论的先驱。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: Voltaire was Newton's chief apostle in France: he arranged French replications of Newtonian experiments and his Elements of the Philosophy of Newton brought calculus and gravitation to the French-speaking world, catalyzing French scientific modernization. In the Earth-shape dispute he championed Newton's oblate spheroid with experimental data — a pioneer of science communication and debate.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 伏尔泰的启蒙之路是一条「从文学天才到公共知识分子」的路：早年以悲剧诗人在巴黎成名，巴士底狱的打击与英国流亡（1726-1729）成为转折——他亲眼看到牛顿科学、洛克哲学与英国自由制度的组合如何让一个民族强盛。此后六十年的写作只有一个主题的变奏：用理性拆掉专制与教权的墙。越到晚年，他越把重心从建设性论证转向破坏性批判——但《老实人》告诉我们，他的批判从不指向虚无，而是指向「我们必须耕种自己的花园」的行动主义。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: His arc runs 'from literary genius to public intellectual': fame in Paris as a tragedian, then the Bastille and English exile (1726-29) as the turning point — seeing how Newton, Locke, and English liberty made a nation strong. Sixty years of writing ring variations on one theme: dismantling the walls of despotism and clerical power with reason. In old age critique grew more destructive — yet Candide shows it never points at nothingness but at action: 'we must cultivate our garden'.
philosophers.aiReview: 伏尔泰是启蒙运动的人格化：他把哲学从书斋搬到了广场，用戏剧、小说、辞典和诉讼把「理性」变成了一场全民运动。他的伟大和局限同样明显：对非欧洲文明的兴趣带着居高临下的目光，对「进步」的信念在 20 世纪遭到沉重打击，他那句名言（其实他大概没说过）被滥用成「什么都可以说的许可证」——伏尔泰本人一定会反对这种用法，他从不认为胡说八道值得捍卫。但有一点无可争议：在他之前，「宽容」是弱者的美德；在他之后，「宽容」是文明的基本条件。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Voltaire is the Enlightenment personified: he moved philosophy from the study to the public square, making 'reason' a mass movement through plays, novels, dictionaries, and lawsuits. His greatness and limits are equally visible: a condescending gaze at non-European civilizations; a faith in progress shattered in the 20th century; his famous slogan (probably never said) abused as a license to say anything — which Voltaire, who never defended nonsense, would have opposed. Yet one thing is beyond dispute: before him toleration was a virtue of the weak; after him, a basic condition of civilization.

furtherReading.title: 《伏尔泰文集》（中译本）
furtherReading.desc: 《哲学通信》《老实人》《论宽容》均为核心篇目

philosophers.anecdote: 伏尔泰一生与权贵周旋，也不忘捉弄他们。普鲁士国王腓特烈大帝请他赴宴，他当面吐槽国王的诗「像用脏袜子织的」；腓特烈回敬说「我拥有全欧洲最好的医生，可你连感冒都要自己治」。二人吵架到绝交，又和好到通信。他 84 岁病重时，神父劝他皈依，他说：「让我安静地死去，我已经给上帝写了那么多信，他欠我一封回信。」
philosophers.anecdoteEn: A lifetime sparring with the mighty: he told Frederick the Great his poetry was 'like socks knit from dirty yarn'; Frederick retorted he had Europe's best doctors while Voltaire insisted on curing his own colds. They quarreled to enmity and reconciled to correspondence. Dying at 84, pressed by a priest to convert, he said: 'Let me die in peace — I have written God so many letters, He owes me a reply.'

philosophers.name: 孟德斯鸠
philosophers.role: 启蒙运动政治哲学家，「三权分立」学说的奠基人
philosophers.summary: 法国启蒙运动的政治哲学巨匠。他的《论法的精神》在二十年间震撼了整个欧洲：法律不是凭空颁布的命令，而是民族精神、气候、地理、习俗的产物；权力必须用权力来制衡——「三权分立」（立法、行政、司法）从此成为现代宪政的通用语法。他还是一位游记作家，用二十年游历欧洲，写下辛辣的《波斯人信札》，以波斯人视角反观欧洲文明的荒谬。美国的国父们、法国的制宪者们、乃至今天绝大多数国家的宪法，都流淌着他的思想。
philosophers.summaryEn: The political-philosophical giant of the French Enlightenment. The Spirit of the Laws shook Europe for two decades: law is not arbitrary command but the product of national spirit, climate, geography, and custom; power must check power — the separation of powers (legislative, executive, judicial) became the universal grammar of modern constitutionalism. Also a travel writer, he spent twenty years touring Europe and wrote the satirical Persian Letters, viewing European absurdity through Persian eyes. The American Founders, the French constitutionalists, and most constitutions today flow from his thought.

representativeWorks.title: 《论法的精神》
representativeWorks.content: 二十年的巨著，共 31 卷。提出法律的本质是「事物的本性所产生的关系」；区分共和、君主、专制三种政体及其原则；论证气候与地理对法律的影响；提出三权分立与「中间权力」。近代政治科学的奠基之作。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Twenty years in the making, 31 books. Law is 'the relations necessarily derived from the nature of things'; three forms of government (republic, monarchy, despotism) with their principles; the influence of climate and geography; the separation of powers and intermediary bodies. The founding work of modern political science.

representativeWorks.title: 《波斯人信札》
representativeWorks.content: 两个波斯人游历法国的通信：以「异乡人的眼睛」审视法国的宗教、宫廷、习俗与法律。伏尔泰读了拍案叫绝，启蒙文学的里程碑，也是比较文化的先驱之作。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Letters of two Persians touring France: viewing French religion, court, customs, and law through foreign eyes. Voltaire was delighted; a milestone of Enlightenment literature and a pioneer of comparative culture.

coreThoughts.desc: 孟德斯鸠政治学的核心命题：任何拥有权力的人都倾向滥用权力，直到遇到边界。所以必须用权力制衡权力——立法权、行政权、司法权分属不同机构，彼此独立又互相制约。他不是第一个提出分权的人（洛克已区分立法与行政），但他第一个把司法权独立出来，并把它从「理论建议」变成了「宪政配方」。美国宪法对三权分立的实践，直接源于《论法的精神》第十一卷。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：孟德斯鸠说「权力会自己膨胀，所以不能把权力都交给一个人」——立法、行政、司法三把钥匙，分开保管。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像银行的保险库需要三把不同的钥匙、三个不同的人保管——谁都不能单独打开，才能互相看着。
coreThoughts.l3: 三权分立（séparation des pouvoirs）：立法（人民/代议）、行政（君主/政府）、司法（法院）。「只有权力才能阻止权力」（le pouvoir arrête le pouvoir）。与洛克的二权分立相比，孟德斯鸠的司法独立是原创贡献，直接塑造了 1787 年美国宪法与 1789 年法国《人权宣言》的制度设计。
coreThoughts.descEn: Anyone with power tends to abuse it until it meets a limit. Therefore power must check power: legislative, executive, and judicial powers belong to distinct bodies, independent yet mutually restraining. Locke separated powers; Montesquieu made the judiciary independent and turned a suggestion into a constitutional recipe — the direct source of the U.S. Constitution's design.
coreThoughts.l1En: Power grows by itself, so don't give it all to one person — three keys to the vault, held by three different hands.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a bank vault requiring three different keys held by three different people: no one can open it alone.
coreThoughts.l3En: Legislative, executive, judicial — 'power must stop power'. His innovation over Locke is judicial independence, directly shaping the U.S. Constitution (1787) and the French Declaration of Rights (1789).

coreThoughts.desc: 孟德斯鸠的法学革命：法律不是抽象的正义公式，而是「与事物本性相关的关系」——政体是共和还是君主，领土是大是小，气候是寒是热，宗教、习俗、商业发达与否，都会影响该国的法律应该长什么样。由此他开创了「比较法学」和「历史法学」：没有放之四海皆准的最优法律，只有与国情匹配的合适法律。这个相对主义结论既是近代社会科学的起点，也埋下了「普遍人权 vs 文化差异」的持久争论。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：孟德斯鸠说法律不是天上掉下来的标准答案——热带的共和国和寒冷的君主国，需要的法律不一样，得看国情。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像裁衣：同样一块布，给瘦子和胖子做衣服要量体裁衣——法律也得量着民族的「身材」来做。
coreThoughts.l3: 「法的精神」= 法律与政体性质、原则、气候、土壤、民情、商业、宗教等一切因素的总关系。他把法律从道德哲学拉进经验科学：以跨文明比较（希腊、罗马、英国、中国）取代先验演绎。其「气候决定论」后世备受批评，但「制度与国情匹配」的思路仍是政治学的基本方法。
coreThoughts.descEn: Law is not an abstract formula of justice but a relation to the nature of things: government form, territory, climate, religion, custom, commerce all shape what law a people needs. No single best law for all — only fitting laws. This relativism founded comparative and historical jurisprudence, opening the enduring debate between universal rights and cultural difference.
coreThoughts.l1En: Law is not a standard answer from heaven: a hot republic and a cold monarchy need different laws, fitted to their situations.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like tailoring: the same cloth must be cut to different bodies — law must be cut to a people's measure.
coreThoughts.l3En: The 'spirit of the laws' = the total relation of law to government nature, principles, climate, soil, mores, commerce, religion. He moved law from moral philosophy into empirical science via cross-civilizational comparison. His climate determinism is criticized, but institutional fit remains basic political science.

famousEvents.title: 英国考察
famousEvents.desc: 流亡英国两年，旁听议会辩论、研究英国宪制，回国后把英国的「平衡政体」融入自己的制度设计——三权分立的灵感正是来自他对英国体制的观察。
famousEvents.descEn: Two years in England, attending parliamentary debates and studying the English constitution; his separation of powers was distilled from observing the English balance of institutions.

famousEvents.title: 《论法的精神》的出版风波
famousEvents.desc: 《论法的精神》在日内瓦匿名出版，随即风靡欧洲，两年内再版 22 次；同时被罗马教廷列入禁书目录，被法国索邦大学批判——越禁越流行，成为启蒙时代的现象级著作。
famousEvents.titleEn: The Spirit of the Laws Controversy
famousEvents.descEn: Published anonymously in Geneva, it swept Europe (22 reprints in two years) while being placed on the Index and attacked by the Sorbonne — the more it was banned, the more it sold.

philosophers.scientificEval: 孟德斯鸠把法律研究从伦理学带入经验科学：他采用的跨文明比较法、类型学方法（政体分类）和对「制度-环境」关系的系统考察，被公认为现代社会科学（政治学、社会学、法学）的方法论起点之一。涂尔干视其为「社会学的先驱」；他的气候-社会理论虽被现代科学证伪，却是环境决定论与人文地理学的早期模板。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: Montesquieu moved the study of law from ethics into empirical science: cross-civilizational comparison, typology of governments, and systematic study of institution-environment relations mark the methodological origin of modern social science. Durkheim called him a forerunner of sociology; his climate theory, though falsified, is an early template of environmental determinism and human geography.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 孟德斯鸠的思想轨迹是一位法官走向政治科学的历程：他出身法官世家，本人任波尔多法院院长，亲身体验了法国司法制度的僵化与贵族的特权——这解释了他对「中间权力」和分权的执念。他游历欧洲二十年（维也纳、匈牙利、意大利、德意志、荷兰、英国），把见闻转化为《波斯人信札》的讽刺与《论法的精神》的比较。他是启蒙阵营里最「保守」的激进者：不追求抽象人权，而追求制度平衡；不推翻君主制，而给君主制装上刹车。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: His arc is a judge's road to political science: born into a legal dynasty, himself president of the Bordeaux parlement, he tasted firsthand the rigidity and privilege of French justice — explaining his obsession with intermediary powers and balance. Twenty years of European travel became the satire of the Persian Letters and the comparison of the Spirit of the Laws. He was the most 'conservative' radical of the Enlightenment: not abstract rights but institutional balance; not abolishing monarchy but braking it.
philosophers.aiReview: 孟德斯鸠是那种「你可能没读过，但活在每部宪法里」的哲学家。三权分立如今已经是宪政常识，以至于人们忘了它曾经是一个石破天惊的发明：把权力交给互相牵制的机构，而不是交给最好的人。他对「法的精神」的相对主义至今仍是政治学的核心张力：既要普遍人权，又要尊重国情——两百年了，这个问题没有答案，只有更好的平衡。批评者说他为气候决定论背书、为贵族「中间权力」辩护（有人称他是「穿长袍的贵族在给特权找理论」）；但美国宪法的设计者、法国大革命的制宪者都从他的书里找钥匙，这本身就是对他最好的辩护。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Montesquieu is a philosopher you may never have read yet live inside every constitution. Separation of powers is now constitutional common sense, so easily forgotten as a stunning invention: give power to mutually restraining institutions, not to the best men. His relativism of legal spirit remains political science's core tension: universal rights and national particularity — two centuries, no answer, only better balances. Critics call him an apologist for aristocratic intermediary powers; but the American Founders and French constitution-makers all took their keys from his book — the best defense.

furtherReading.title: 《论法的精神》（张雁深中译本）
furtherReading.desc: 重点读第 11 卷（三权分立）与第 19 卷（法的精神）

philosophers.anecdote: 孟德斯鸠写《波斯人信札》时才 32 岁，匿名出版后红遍巴黎，人人都猜作者是谁。他后来承认时说：「我像孔雀一样炫耀了一下。」他晚年视力几乎失明，仍坚持写作；1755 年他在巴黎病逝，临终前说：「我一辈子都在努力工作，现在可以休息了。」伏尔泰为他写下悼词：「人类的损失。」
philosophers.anecdoteEn: He published the Persian Letters anonymously at 32; when Paris buzzed guessing the author, he confessed: 'I preened like a peacock.' Nearly blind in old age, he wrote on; dying in Paris in 1755, he said, 'I have worked all my life; now I may rest.' Voltaire's epitaph: 'The loss of humankind.'

relationships.description: 分权思想承自洛克并发展为三权分立
同为启蒙双璧，互相欣赏又彼此疏远
与卢梭的人民主权论形成「制衡 vs 主权」之争
其共和主义政体论影响康德《永久和平论》
黑格尔《法哲学原理》的「具体普遍性」吸收其制度思想

goldenQuotes.text: 任何拥有权力的人都倾向滥用权力，直到遇到边界。要防止滥用权力，就必须以权力制约权力。
goldenQuotes.textEn: Every man who has power is led to abuse it, until he finds limits. To prevent this abuse, power must check power.

goldenQuotes.text: 自由不是做你想做的事，而是有权做法律允许做的事。
goldenQuotes.textEn: Liberty is not doing what one wishes, but having the right to do what the laws permit.

philosophers.name: 费希特
philosophers.role: 德国古典哲学承上启下者，「自我」哲学的奠基人
philosophers.summary: 康德与黑格尔之间的枢纽人物。他出身贫寒的织带匠家庭，靠给人做家教自学成才，因一篇论文被康德赏识而踏入哲学界。他嫌康德的「物自体」是个多余的黑洞，把哲学重建为「自我」的体系：自我不是被动反映世界，而是主动设定世界——「自我设定自身，并设定非我」。这个激进的主体哲学影响了整个德国浪漫派、青年黑格尔派与马克思的实践哲学。他还是著名的爱国演说家，在拿破仑占领柏林时发表了《对德意志民族的演讲》。
philosophers.summaryEn: The hinge between Kant and Hegel. Born into a poor ribbon-weaver's family, he educated himself as a private tutor and entered philosophy on a thesis Kant admired. Finding Kant's thing-in-itself a redundant black hole, he rebuilt philosophy as the system of the 'I': the self does not passively mirror the world but posits it — 'the I posits itself, and posits the not-I'. This radical philosophy of subjectivity shaped German Romanticism, the Young Hegelians, and Marx's practical philosophy. He was also the patriotic orator of the Addresses to the German Nation under Napoleonic occupation of Berlin.

representativeWorks.title: 《全部知识学的基础》
representativeWorks.content: 费希特的核心著作：以「自我设定自身」为第一原理，演绎出自我、非我、有限自我三个命题及其综合，建立了一个彻底的主体唯心论体系——「知识学」（Wissenschaftslehre）成为德国唯心论中最纯粹的行动哲学。
representativeWorks.contentEn: His central work: deriving from 'the I posits itself' the three propositions of the I, the not-I, and the finite I, constructing a radical subjective idealism — the Wissenschaftslehre, the purest philosophy of action in German idealism.

representativeWorks.title: 《对德意志民族的演讲》
representativeWorks.desc: 拿破仑占领柏林期间发表的十四篇演讲，呼吁德意志民族通过教育实现精神新生。既是民族主义思想史上的名篇，也常被视为近代民族意识觉醒的标志性文献。

representativeWorks.title: 《人的使命》
representativeWorks.content: 通俗哲学代表作：以「怀疑、知识、信仰」三卷对话体，论证人不是自然的旁观者而是自由的行动者，世界的意义由人的行动赋予。
representativeWorks.contentEn: A popular philosophical work in dialogues (doubt, knowledge, faith): man is not a spectator of nature but an agent of freedom; the world's meaning is constituted by action.

coreThoughts.desc: 费希特把康德哲学推到底：康德说知识需要先天形式（时间、空间、范畴），那这些形式又来自哪里？费希特的回答：来自「自我」的活动本身——自我不是被动地接受材料，而是主动地设定对象。「自我设定自身」是第一原理：我一活动，就意识到自己；我一意识到自己，就同时设定了一个「非我」（对象）与自己对立。意识不是镜子，而是光源。这个转向使哲学从「认识世界」变成「构造世界」。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：费希特说别问「世界是什么样」，要问「谁在看」——不是眼睛反映世界，而是心灵在照亮世界。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像探照灯：黑暗不是灯照出来的，但你能看见的东西全是灯照出来的——费希特的「自我」就是那盏灯。
coreThoughts.l3: 知识学三命题：①自我设定自身（同一性）；②自我设定非我（对立）；③自我在自我之中设定可分的自我与非我（综合）。康德的「哥白尼革命」被费希特彻底主体化：物自体被取消，「设定」（Setzen）取代「接受」。这为谢林、黑格尔铺路，也直接启发了马克思「实践构造对象」的命题。
coreThoughts.descEn: Pushing Kant to the limit: if knowledge requires a priori forms, where do the forms come from? From the activity of the I itself — the self is not a passive receiver but an active positer. 'The I posits itself': in acting I become aware of myself; in being aware I simultaneously posit a not-I opposed to me. Consciousness is a light-source, not a mirror.
coreThoughts.l1En: Don't ask 'what is the world like' — ask 'who is seeing'. It is not the eye reflecting the world but the mind illuminating it.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a searchlight: darkness is not made by the lamp, but everything you can see is lit by it — the I is that lamp.
coreThoughts.l3En: Three propositions: (1) the I posits itself; (2) the I posits the not-I; (3) the I posits a divisible I and not-I within itself. Kant's Copernican turn is radicalized into pure positing; the thing-in-itself is abolished. This paves the way for Schelling and Hegel and anticipates Marx's thesis that practice constitutes its object.

coreThoughts.desc: 费希特的哲学有一个伦理内核：自我不是现成的东西，而是要做出来的东西——「我是我所应当成为的」。知识服务于行动，哲学最终是实践学。他区分「自然的人」（被欲望牵着走）与「道德的人」（自我立法、自我超越）；世界是「我的行动的原材料」，而行动的目标是把理性实现于世界。这套「自我即使命」的伦理学，是后来存在主义「自我创造」命题的先声。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：费希特说「你是什么」不重要，「你要成为什么」才重要——人是自己要做出来的作品，不是天生的。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像雕塑：大理石不是雕像，雕像要靠雕琢——费希特说，你自己就是那块大理石，也是那个雕刻家。
coreThoughts.l3: 费希特的伦理学：自我是「Tathandlung」（事实行动）——在行动中自我被生产。道德法则（绝对命令的费希特版）：「永远按照你的使命行动」。这套「自我即自由的活动」的学说经谢林转手，深刻影响黑格尔的「实体即主体」与马克思的实践唯物主义。
coreThoughts.descEn: The self is not a given thing but something to be made — 'I am what I ought to become'. Knowledge serves action; philosophy is ultimately practical. The natural man is driven by desire; the moral man self-legislates and self-surpasses. The world is the raw material of my action, whose goal is realizing reason in the world. A direct prelude to existentialist self-creation.
coreThoughts.l1En: What you are doesn't matter; what you become does. A person is a work to be made, not a given.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like sculpture: marble is not a statue until carved — you are both the marble and the sculptor.
coreThoughts.l3En: The self is Tathandlung — fact-act, produced in acting. His moral law: 'always act according to your vocation.' Via Schelling this shapes Hegel's 'substance is subject' and Marx's practical materialism.

famousEvents.title: 「费希特危机」与《论知识学的概念》
famousEvents.desc: 1791 年，费希特带着手稿去见康德，康德虽未全力推荐，却被其才能折服。次年他匿名发表《试评一切天启》，被误认为康德新作，康德澄清后费希特一举成名——哲学史上著名的「误认事件」。
famousEvents.descEn: In 1792 he anonymously published an essay on revelation so Kantian it was mistaken for Kant's own; after Kant clarified, Fichte became famous overnight — philosophy's most famous case of mistaken attribution.

famousEvents.title: 无神论之争
famousEvents.desc: 费希特在论文中把上帝解释为「道德世界秩序」，被指控无神论，被迫辞去耶拿大学教授职位——魏玛公国在舆论压力下解雇了他。此事震动全德，也让他转向更强调实践与民族的思想。
famousEvents.descEn: His thesis that God is the moral world-order drew charges of atheism; he was dismissed from Jena under political pressure. The affair shook Germany and pushed him toward practice and the nation.

famousEvents.title: 《对德意志民族的演讲》
famousEvents.desc: 拿破仑占领柏林，柏林大学停办。费希特在德军占领下的柏林发表十四篇演讲，主张以新教育实现民族精神复兴——成为德意志民族主义的思想源头之一。
famousEvents.descEn: Under French occupation of Berlin he delivered fourteen addresses calling for national spiritual rebirth through education — a founding text of German nationalism.

philosophers.scientificEval: 费希特对科学的直接影响有限，但其「主体构造对象」的认识论立场被后来的认知科学（建构主义认知观）、现象学（胡塞尔）与哲学诠释学部分继承。他在耶拿时期推动了「自我意识」问题的现代讨论，这个讨论经由胡塞尔、萨特延续至当代意识哲学；其「设定」概念也启发了结构主义对「结构先于要素」的分析。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: Fichte's direct scientific influence is limited, but his constructivist epistemology is partly inherited by cognitive science, Husserl's phenomenology, and philosophical hermeneutics. His Jena treatment of self-consciousness feeds the modern debate continuing through Husserl and Sartre into contemporary philosophy of mind; his 'positing' also inspired structuralist analysis of structure before elements.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 费希特的思想分三阶段：耶拿时期（1794-1799）建立知识学体系，从「自我」推出全部哲学；柏林时期（1799-1810）转向宗教与法权哲学，写作《人的使命》《对德意志民族的演讲》；晚期（1810-1814）在柏林大学任校长，回归更成熟的「知识学」新版本。贯穿始终的主线只有一个：自我是自由的活动，哲学的使命是唤醒人对自己自由的意识。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: Three phases: Jena (1794-99) founding the Wissenschaftslehre from the I; Berlin (1799-1810) turning to religion and legal philosophy (Vocation of Man, Addresses); late (1810-14) as Berlin University's first rector, returning to a mature new Wissenschaftslehre. One thread runs through all: the self is free activity, and philosophy's mission is awakening consciousness of one's freedom.
philosophers.aiReview: 费希特是被低估的「激进康德」：他把康德体系里最别扭的部分（物自体）果断砍掉，换来一个纯净到近乎炫目的主体哲学。他的「自我设定」后来被嘲笑为「唯心主义的独白」，但换个角度看，这正是现代主体性思想最纯粹的标本——存在主义说「存在先于本质」，费希特早一百年说「自我先于自我」。他对民族教育的热情让他成了某种民族主义源头，这层遗产是双刃剑：既催生了教育救国的理想，也被后世民族主义滥用。但若回到哲学本身，他值得被记住的是一句朴素而有力的话：人是自己行动的作品。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Fichte is the underrated radical Kantian: he cut away the thing-in-itself for a subjectivism so pure it verges on dazzling. His 'the I posits' was mocked as idealist monologue, yet it is the purest specimen of modern subjectivity — existentialism says existence precedes essence; Fichte said a century earlier that the self precedes itself. His national-education enthusiasm made him a source of nationalism, a double-edged legacy. But philosophically, remember him for one plain strong sentence: a person is the work of their own action.

philosophers.anecdote: 费希特成名前给人当家庭教师，曾受雇于瑞士一个贵族家庭。他的教学方法激进到让东家抗议——他拒绝教孩子「顺从」，而要教他们「思考」。后来他回信说：「教育要么培养自由人，要么就是训练奴隶，没有中间道路。」这话让他丢了饭碗，却预示了他一生的哲学立场。
philosophers.anecdoteEn: Before fame he tutored a Swiss noble family; his methods were so radical the employer protested — he refused to teach obedience, insisting on teaching thought. He replied: 'Education either cultivates free people or trains slaves; there is no middle way.' He lost the job but kept the position for life.
