philosophers.name: 谢林
philosophers.role: 德国古典哲学奇才，同一哲学与自由哲学的开创者
philosophers.summary: 德国古典哲学的天才少年：15 岁入图宾根神学院，与黑格尔、荷尔德林同窗；23 岁即任耶拿大学教授，被歌德、席勒等奉为哲学界新星。他的一生横跨观念论从巅峰到解体的全过程：早年创建「同一哲学」，主张自然与精神、主体与客体本是同一整体；中期转向艺术哲学（《先验唯心论体系》）；晚期提出「自由哲学」与「启示哲学」，直面恶的根源与存在的深渊。他的自然哲学直接启发了浪漫派的自然观与谢林-黑格尔之争，也通过海德格尔重新进入 20 世纪哲学。
philosophers.summaryEn: The boy genius of German idealism: into the Tübingen seminary at 15 alongside Hegel and Hölderlin; professor at Jena at 23, celebrated by Goethe and Schiller. His career spans idealism's peak and dissolution: early Identity Philosophy (nature and spirit, subject and object as one whole); middle philosophy of art (System of Transcendental Idealism); late philosophy of freedom and revelation confronting the origin of evil and the abyss of being. His philosophy of nature inspired the Romantics; his later thought re-entered 20th-century philosophy through Heidegger.

representativeWorks.title: 《先验唯心论体系》
representativeWorks.content: 谢林中期代表作：以艺术为哲学的最高器官——艺术作品是无意识与有意识活动的统一，是「哲学的唯一真正工具」。此书深刻影响了浪漫派美学与黑格尔的艺术哲学。
representativeWorks.contentEn: His middle masterpiece: art as the highest organon of philosophy — the artwork unifies conscious and unconscious activity, 'the only true instrument of philosophy'. It deeply shaped Romantic aesthetics and Hegel's philosophy of art.

representativeWorks.title: 《论人类自由的本质》
representativeWorks.content: 晚期哲学的标志：如果一切源于上帝，恶从何来？谢林提出「存在的深渊」——上帝内部存在一个不可化的基底（Ungrund），自由正是从深渊中的决断诞生。被海德格尔称为「西方形而上学最伟大的著作之一」。
representativeWorks.titleEn: Philosophical Investigations into the Essence of Human Freedom
representativeWorks.contentEn: The landmark of his late philosophy: if all comes from God, whence evil? Schelling posits the 'ground' of being — an ungroundable basis within God from which freedom's decision emerges. Heidegger called it 'one of the greatest works of Western metaphysics'.

coreThoughts.desc: 谢林年轻时的口号：绝对者不是主体也不是客体，而是主体与客体的「无差别同一」。自然不是精神的异乡，而是「可见的精神」；精神也不是自然的对立面，而是「不可见的自然」。这条思路治愈了康德-费希特留下的主客裂缝：世界是一个自我展开的整体，自然哲学（研究自然中的精神）与先验哲学（研究精神中的自然）是同一个绝对者的两面。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：谢林说别把「我」和「世界」分成两边——它们是同一个东西的两面，就像硬币的正反面。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像一棵树：你看到树冠和树根是两样东西，但它们是同一棵树——谢林说自然和精神就是同一棵树的树冠和树根。
coreThoughts.l3: 同一哲学（Identitätsphilosophie）：绝对者 = 主体与客体的无差别点（Indifferenzpunkt）。自然哲学发现自然中的精神性（磁、电、化学中的「两极对立」），先验哲学发现精神中的自然性（无意识→意识）。这套图式经黑格尔改造为「绝对精神」的辩证展开，但谢林坚持同一性先于差别，与黑格尔的「差别优先」形成著名的谢林-黑格尔之争。
coreThoughts.descEn: The Absolute is neither subject nor object but their undifferentiated identity. Nature is not spirit's foreign land but 'visible spirit'; spirit is 'invisible nature'. This heals the Cartesian-Kantian split: philosophy of nature (spirit in nature) and transcendental philosophy (nature in spirit) are two faces of one Absolute unfolding.
coreThoughts.l1En: Don't split 'me' and 'the world' — they are two faces of one thing, like the two sides of a coin.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a tree: crown and root look like two things but are one tree — nature and spirit are the crown and root of one tree.
coreThoughts.l3En: The Absolute is the point of indifference of subject and object. Nature-philosophy finds spirituality in nature (polarity in magnetism, electricity, chemistry); transcendental philosophy finds nature in spirit (unconscious to conscious). Hegel absorbs the schema but insists on the priority of difference — the famous Schelling-Hegel dispute.

coreThoughts.desc: 晚期谢林面对一个恶的问题：若一切都是上帝（绝对者）的展开，恶从何而来？他的回答惊世骇俗：上帝不是无差别的完满，其内部有一个「深渊」（Grund）——一种非理性的、黑暗的基底，像大地之于光明。自由不是「选择善恶的能力」那么简单，而是从深渊中自我奠基的决断。人之所以能作恶，恰恰因为他有自由；而自由的可能性本身就预设了存在的黑暗面。这套「存在论的恶论」打破了启蒙以来「恶=无知」的乐观，预示了 20 世纪对「根本恶」的思考。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：谢林说世界不只由光明构成——光明背后有一片深渊，自由就是人从这片深渊里自己做出决断的能力，包括作恶。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像黑夜与白昼：没有黑夜就没有白昼的对比，没有「深渊」这个基底，自由和善恶根本无法存在。
coreThoughts.l3: 《论人类自由的本质》：存在（Existenz）与基底（Grund）的区分；上帝中的「自然」面（黑暗）是光明面的条件。自由 = 善与恶的可实现性（das Gute und Böse zu realisieren）。海德格尔、蒂利希、阿伦特均深受此论影响；其「根本恶」概念先于康德与阿伦特的同名讨论。
coreThoughts.descEn: If all follows from God, whence evil? Schelling's shocking answer: God is not undifferentiated perfection; within Him lies a Grund — a dark, irrational ground, like earth beneath light. Freedom is the decision that grounds itself out of this abyss. Evil is possible precisely because freedom is real; freedom's possibility presupposes being's dark side. This ontological account of evil breaks the Enlightenment's 'evil = ignorance' optimism, anticipating 20th-century thinking on radical evil.
coreThoughts.l1En: The world is not made of light alone — behind light lies an abyss; freedom is the decision a person makes from that abyss, including the decision to do evil.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like night and day: without night, day has no contrast; without the 'ground', freedom and good-and-evil could not exist.
coreThoughts.l3En: The distinction of existence and ground; the dark 'nature' in God as the condition of light; freedom as the realizability of good and evil. Heidegger, Tillich, and Arendt are all heirs; his radical evil precedes Kant's and Arendt's homonymous discussions.

famousEvents.title: 图宾根三杰
famousEvents.desc: 15 岁的谢林与黑格尔、荷尔德林同窗于图宾根神学院，三人一起研读康德与法国大革命，传为哲学史佳话——「三个青年在果园里种下了一棵自由树」。
famousEvents.descEn: At 15 Schelling entered the Tübingen seminary with Hegel and Hölderlin; together they read Kant and celebrated the French Revolution — the famous story of three youths planting a tree of liberty.

famousEvents.title: 与黑格尔的分道扬镳
famousEvents.desc: 黑格尔出版《精神现象学》后，两人由挚友变论敌。谢林指责黑格尔剽窃其思想，黑格尔讥讽谢林哲学是「黑夜里的牛」（一切皆黑）。此后谢林沉寂数十年，晚年方重出江湖。
famousEvents.descEn: After Hegel's Phenomenology (1807) the friends became rivals: Schelling accused Hegel of plagiarism; Hegel mocked Schelling's absolute as 'the night in which all cows are black'. Schelling fell silent for decades before a late comeback.

famousEvents.title: 柏林讲席之争
famousEvents.desc: 66 岁高龄的谢林应普鲁士国王之邀赴柏林大学讲学，与青年黑格尔派（包括恩格斯、克尔凯郭尔）正面交锋，他的「启示哲学」讲座吸引全欧瞩目——德国哲学王座的最后一次交接。
famousEvents.descEn: At 66, invited by the Prussian king to Berlin, he clashed head-on with the Young Hegelians (including Engels and Kierkegaard) in his lectures on positive philosophy — the last handover of Germany's philosophical throne.

philosophers.scientificEval: 谢林的自然哲学把磁、电、化学等现象解释为「自然中的精神活动」，虽带有思辨色彩，却直接启发了浪漫派科学（如奥肯的生物哲学）与德国大学体系的建立。其「自然是有机整体」的纲领被看作有机论科学观的重要源头；他对「极性」和「发展」的强调间接影响了黑格尔辩证法和 19 世纪进化观念的氛围。现代科学哲学（如怀特海的过程哲学）也吸收其有机论遗产。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: Schelling's nature-philosophy read magnetism, electricity, and chemistry as spirit in nature; speculative as it was, it inspired Romantic science (Oken's biology) and the founding of the German university system. His organicist program is a major source of organicist science; his polarity and development themes indirectly fed Hegelian dialectics and 19th-century evolutionism. Whitehead's process philosophy absorbs this organicist legacy.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 谢林一生四次转向，每次都推翻自己：同一哲学（1794-1800）→ 艺术哲学（1800-1804）→ 自由哲学（1804-1815）→ 启示哲学/实存哲学（1815-1854）。他自称「不辍的自我否定者」，黑格尔揶揄他「在公众面前举办哲学进修班」。但正是这种不断自我推翻，使他的晚期思想带着罕见的诚实直面理性的极限——理性无法推出「为什么存在者存在」，只能面对存在的事实。这个「实证哲学」的转向预告了存在主义与后观念论哲学。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: Four self-overthrowings: identity (1794-1800), art (1800-04), freedom (1804-15), positive/revelation philosophy (1815-54). Hegel mocked his public 'philosophical refresher courses'; yet this relentless self-negation gave his late thought an unusual honesty before reason's limits — reason cannot derive 'why anything exists'; it must confront the fact of existence. The turn to positive philosophy heralds existentialism and post-idealist philosophy.
philosophers.aiReview: 谢林是被黑格尔的光芒遮蔽得太久的哲学天才。他 23 岁就建成体系，一生都在拆掉重来——这在哲学史上罕见，也让他成为最难「读完」的经典作家：你刚熟悉他的同一哲学，他已经转向艺术哲学，等你跟上，他又跳进了深渊。晚期谢林对「恶的根源」「存在的深渊」的思考，在两百年后显得格外前瞻：启蒙理性无法解释奥斯维辛，而谢林早已断言理性的根基处有非理性。他输给了黑格尔的历史地位之争，但赢回了后世的重新发现——从海德格尔到蒂利希，从浪漫派到当代存在哲学，谢林的名字一直在暗中发光。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Schelling is the genius too long overshadowed by Hegel. A system at 23, then a lifetime of demolition and rebuilding — rare in philosophy, which is why he is the hardest classic to 'finish': by the time you master the identity philosophy he has moved to art, then plunged into the abyss. His late thinking on the origin of evil and the ground of being looks prescient across two centuries: Enlightenment reason cannot explain Auschwitz, and Schelling already insisted reason's ground is non-rational. He lost the battle of reputations to Hegel but won posterity's rediscovery — from Heidegger to Tillich, from the Romantics to existential philosophy.

furtherReading.desc: 晚期谢林的代表作，恶与自由的形而上学

philosophers.anecdote: 谢林 23 岁到耶拿时，歌德亲自去听他的课，席勒与他频繁通信。传说歌德问他：「你的体系什么时候才能写完？」谢林答：「我的体系不在书里，在我心里，我随时可以重写。」歌德赞他「天生的哲学家」。而他晚年对克尔凯郭尔的评价更是传神——听完这位丹麦人的硕士论文答辩，他说：「我从未见过这么有哲学天赋的年轻人，可惜他选择了神学。」
philosophers.anecdoteEn: At Jena at 23, Goethe attended his lectures and Schiller corresponded with him. Asked when his system would be finished, Schelling answered: 'My system lives in my heart, not in my books; I can rewrite it at any time.' Goethe called him a born philosopher. After hearing the young Kierkegaard defend his thesis, Schelling said: 'I have never met a youth of such philosophical talent — pity he chose theology.'

philosophers.name: 费尔巴哈
philosophers.role: 青年黑格尔派旗手，「人本学唯物主义」的创立者
philosophers.summary: 德国古典哲学向唯物主义转向的枢纽人物。他是青年黑格尔派中最激进的一员：把黑格尔的「绝对精神」从天上拽回人间——不是神创造了人，而是人按照自己的形象创造了神。「上帝是人的本质的对象化」这句命题引爆了整个 19 世纪的思想界。马克思和恩格斯正是在批判费尔巴哈的过程中走向历史唯物主义（《关于费尔巴哈的提纲》第一条就是「从前的一切唯物主义的主要缺点是：对对象……只是从客体的形式去理解」）。他的一生像他的哲学一样朴素：被大学除名后，隐居乡间小镇写作，靠妻子的遗产度日，却影响了整整一代人。
philosophers.summaryEn: The pivotal figure of German idealism's turn to materialism. The most radical of the Young Hegelians, he dragged Hegel's absolute spirit down to earth: not God who created man in His image, but man who created God in his own. 'God is the objectified essence of man' detonated 19th-century thought. Marx and Engels reached historical materialism precisely by criticizing Feuerbach (the first thesis On Feuerbach: 'the chief defect of all previous materialism is that it grasps things only in the form of the object'). His life was as plain as his philosophy: expelled from the university, he wrote in a country town on his wife's inheritance — and influenced a generation.

representativeWorks.title: 《基督教的本质》
representativeWorks.content: 费尔巴哈的核弹：基督教神学的秘密是人本学——上帝的一切属性（全知、全能、至善）都是人的本质属性的无限化投射。「人把自己对象化又把自己当作对象」：宗教是人的自我异化，哲学的使命是把人从神的阴影下解放出来。此书使他一夜之间成为欧洲思想界的风暴中心。
representativeWorks.contentEn: His detonation: the secret of Christian theology is anthropology — every divine attribute (omniscience, omnipotence, goodness) is the infinite projection of human essence. Religion is man's self-alienation; philosophy's task is to liberate man from God's shadow. It made him the storm center of European thought overnight.

representativeWorks.title: 《宗教的本质》
representativeWorks.content: 把《基督教的本质》的投射论推广到一切宗教：自然宗教把自然神化，基督教把人的本质神化，二者都是人的依赖感与幻想能力的产物。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Extending the projection thesis to all religion: natural religion divinizes nature, Christianity divinizes human essence — both are products of human dependence-feelings and fantasy.

coreThoughts.concept: 上帝是人的本质的对象化
coreThoughts.desc: 费尔巴哈的命题：不是神按自己的形象造人，而是人按自己的形象造神。人所崇拜的上帝的全知、全能、无限，正是人自己的有限能力在想象中的无限放大——「人把自己的本质对象化出去，然后跪拜这个对象」。神学因此变成人学：研究上帝，就是研究人；对神的崇拜，是对人的本质（但被扭曲为外在于人的形式）的崇拜。这个「投射论」是近代无神论最有力的武器之一，直接启发了马克思的异化论、弗洛伊德的宗教心理学。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：费尔巴哈说上帝是人的镜子——你崇拜的神的每一种能力，都是你自己的能力被放大了无数倍。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像对着哈哈镜：镜子里的人又高又壮，其实是真实的人被放大变形了——费尔巴哈说神就是那面哈哈镜里的「放大版自己」。
coreThoughts.l3: 投射论（Projektionstheorie）：神学还原为人学（Theologie = Anthropologie）。上帝的本质 = 类本质（Gattungswesen）的无限化。费尔巴哈的宗教批判不是取消宗教，而是「宗教的真理是人」——把爱、理性、意志（人的三位一体）从彼岸收回此岸。马克思的《关于费尔巴哈的提纲》肯定其批判，但指出「人的本质不是单个人所固有的抽象物，而是一切社会关系的总和」。
coreThoughts.conceptEn: God as the Objectified Essence of Man
coreThoughts.descEn: Not God who made man in His image, but man who made God in his own. Every divine attribute is the infinite magnification of a human capacity; theology is anthropology. Worship of God is worship of man's own essence in alienated form — the most powerful weapon of modern atheism, inspiring Marx's alienation theory and Freud's psychology of religion.
coreThoughts.l1En: God is a mirror of man: every capacity you worship in God is your own capacity, magnified infinitely.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a funhouse mirror: the tall strong figure is really you, distorted — God is the magnified self in the mirror.
coreThoughts.l3En: Projection theory: theology reduces to anthropology. The divine essence is the infinitized species-essence. Feuerbach does not abolish religion but reveals its truth as human — recovering love, reason, and will from the beyond. Marx praises the critique but adds: 'the essence of man is the ensemble of social relations'.

coreThoughts.desc: 费尔巴哈对黑格尔的批判：黑格尔的「绝对精神」是「思辨的神学」，把活生生的人变成了精神自我运动的工具。费尔巴哈的纲领：「我欲，故我在」——人首先是感性存在（身体、欲望、情感），理性只是感性的延伸。「哲学必须重新把人当作感性的、有需要的、有身体的存在来理解。」这套人本学（Anthropologie）为「人」恢复了身体的尊严，也被马克思批评为「只从客体的形式理解，而没有从实践的、人的感性活动去理解」。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：费尔巴哈说哲学家别光谈精神——人有身体、有欲望、会饿会爱，哲学得先承认这个「血肉的人」。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像一座房子：你光说「设计图很完美」没用，房子住人的——哲学要服务的是住在身体里的人，不是图纸上的精神。
coreThoughts.l3: 感性（Sinnlichkeit）是费尔巴哈哲学的基石：存在 = 感性存在；真理的法庭是感觉与爱。他提出「我欲故我在」（volo, ergo sum）对抗笛卡尔。此立场构成马克思主义「实践」概念的直接对话对象（《关于费尔巴哈的提纲》第 1、5、9 条）。
coreThoughts.descEn: Against Hegel's 'speculative theology' that turns living humans into tools of spirit's self-movement, Feuerbach declares: man is first a sensuous being — body, desire, feeling — and reason is its extension. Philosophy must recover man as flesh-and-blood, needy, embodied. This restores bodily dignity and becomes the direct dialogue-partner of Marx's concept of practice.
coreThoughts.l1En: Stop talking about pure spirit — humans have bodies, desires, hunger, love. Philosophy must first accept the flesh-and-blood person.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a house: the blueprint isn't enough; houses are for living in. Philosophy must serve the person in the body, not the spirit on paper.
coreThoughts.l3En: Sensuousness is his foundation: being is sensuous being; the court of truth is feeling and love. 'Volo, ergo sum' against Descartes. Marx's Theses on Feuerbach (1, 5, 9) are a direct dialogue with this position.

famousEvents.title: 《基督教的本质》的爆炸
famousEvents.desc: 1841 年此书出版，立即被翻译成多种语言。恩格斯后来回忆说：「那时我们都成了费尔巴哈派了。」——这本书让一代青年知识分子第一次看到「没有神的哲学」的可能。
famousEvents.descEn: Published in 1841 and immediately translated, Engels later recalled: 'Then we all became Feuerbachians.' The book showed a generation of young intellectuals philosophy without God for the first time.

famousEvents.title: 被大学除名
famousEvents.desc: 因匿名发表的《论死与不朽》否定个体不朽，被确认身份后遭埃尔朗根大学解聘，从此未再获得教职，隐居乡间 25 年。
famousEvents.descEn: His anonymous Thoughts on Death and Immortality denying personal immortality cost him his Erlangen post once identified; he never held a chair again, retiring to the country for 25 years.

philosophers.scientificEval: 费尔巴哈对自然科学的直接贡献有限，但他「人是感性存在」的唯物主义纲领为 19 世纪自然科学与哲学的联盟提供了哲学地基；其人类学转向影响了后来的实证科学观（反对思辨，主张观察）。马克思主义与恩格斯《自然辩证法》吸收其唯物立场；20 世纪法兰克福学派（马尔库塞）又通过其「感性解放」观念回望这条线索。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: Feuerbach's direct contribution to science is limited, but his sensuous-materialist program grounded the 19th-century alliance of natural science and philosophy; his anthropological turn influenced positivist attitudes (observation over speculation). Marxism and Engels' dialectics of nature absorbed his materialism; the Frankfurt School (Marcuse) later returned to his idea of sensuous liberation.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 费尔巴哈的轨迹是「从神学走向人学」：他本是海德堡的神学生，因仰慕黑格尔转赴柏林，成为青年黑格尔派最激进者之一；但很快连黑格尔也成了他要清算的对象——「黑格尔哲学是神学的理性化」。1830 年他被逐出大学，此后 25 年隐居乡间，从神学批判推进到哲学批判，从宗教异化推进到思辨哲学批判。他思想的终点是人本学：神是人的投射，哲学必须回到人。而马克思正是在这个终点上再次出发——把「人」进一步落实为「社会关系」与「实践」。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: His arc runs 'from theology to anthropology': theology student at Heidelberg, drawn to Berlin by Hegel, radical Young Hegelian, then Hegel himself became his target — 'Hegelian philosophy is rationalized theology'. Expelled in 1830, he retired to the countryside for 25 years, moving from critique of religion to critique of speculative philosophy, from religious alienation to its philosophical form. His terminus is anthropology; Marx departs from that very terminus toward social relations and practice.
philosophers.aiReview: 费尔巴哈在哲学史上常被贴上「过渡人物」的标签——他是马克思的垫脚石，似乎只有被超越的价值。这是不公平的：他的「上帝是人的本质的对象化」是人类思想史上一枚真正的炸弹，其穿透力至今未减（当代认知科学对宗教的投射式解释仍是这条路线的变体）。他隐居乡间、被大学遗忘的 25 年，恰恰象征了他的处境：一个把「神圣」从天上拽下来的人，注定要在人间孤独。他的局限也是清晰的：对「人」的理解停留在抽象的感性个体，忽略了社会与历史——这正是马克思超越他的地方。但若没有他先把「神学」翻译成「人学」，马克思的异化论未必能找到那条捷径。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Feuerbach is usually tagged as transitional — Marx's stepping stone, valuable only as something surpassed. Unfair: 'God is the objectified essence of man' is a genuine bomb in intellectual history, undimmed today (cognitive-science accounts of religion are variants of his projection thesis). His 25 lonely years in the country symbolize his position: whoever pulls the divine down to earth is condemned to solitude among humans. His limits are clear: 'man' remained an abstract sensuous individual without society and history — exactly where Marx surpasses him. But without Feuerbach's translation of theology into anthropology, Marx's theory of alienation might not have found its shortcut.

furtherReading.title: 《基督教的本质》（荣震华中译本）
furtherReading.desc: 费尔巴哈代表作，近代无神论经典

philosophers.anecdote: 费尔巴哈一生最大的讽刺是「被哲学遗忘」：他在乡间隐居时，一位访客问他如何打发漫长的乡村岁月，他指着窗外的苹果树说：「我看它开花，看它结果，看它落叶——哲学的问题，树上都写着。」他 68 岁在纽伦堡去世时，葬礼冷清，但马克思在《关于费尔巴哈的提纲》里给他留了一席之地，让他的名字永远刻在了哲学的教科书上。
philosophers.anecdoteEn: His life's great irony was being forgotten by philosophy: visited in his country retreat, he gestured at an apple tree — 'I watch it blossom, fruit, and shed its leaves; all philosophy's questions are written on the tree.' He died at 68 in Nuremberg with a quiet funeral — but Marx's Theses on Feuerbach gave him an eternal place in the textbooks.

goldenQuotes.textEn: The mystery of theology is anthropology: man's knowledge of God is man's knowledge of himself.

philosophers.name: 克尔凯郭尔
philosophers.role: 存在主义之父，个体与信仰的哲学辩护者
philosophers.summary: 丹麦哥本哈根的富家子，存在主义哲学的开创者。他毕生对抗两样东西：黑格尔那套吞没个体的宏大体系，和丹麦教会那种安然舒适的「官方基督教」。他以假名写作大量著作（《非此即彼》《恐惧与战栗》《致死的疾病》），主张：真理不在体系里，而在个体「如何生活」的选择里——「主体性即真理」。他终身未娶（与蕾吉娜的婚约解除是他最大的伤口和灵感），45 岁猝死街头。一百年后，海德格尔、萨特、加缪、卡夫卡全都站在他的影子里。
philosophers.summaryEn: The wealthy Copenhagen son who founded existentialism. He fought two things all his life: Hegel's grand system swallowing the individual, and the Danish church's cozy official Christianity. Writing pseudonymously (Either/Or, Fear and Trembling, The Sickness unto Death), he held: truth is not in systems but in the individual's how — 'subjectivity is truth'. He never married (the broken engagement with Regine Olsen was his greatest wound and inspiration) and died suddenly at 45. A century later Heidegger, Sartre, Camus, and Kafka all stand in his shadow.

representativeWorks.title: 《非此即彼》
representativeWorks.content: 假名著作，上下卷：审美者（追求感官愉悦，最终厌倦）与伦理者（承担选择与责任）两种生活方式的对话。书中「人生三种阶段」的框架成为存在主义经典命题：审美阶段→伦理阶段→宗教阶段。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Pseudonymous, two volumes: a dialogue between the aesthete (sensuous pleasure ending in boredom) and the ethicist (choice and responsibility). The famous framework of life's stages: aesthetic, ethical, religious.

representativeWorks.title: 《恐惧与战栗》
representativeWorks.content: 以亚伯拉罕献以撒的故事追问：信仰是否高于伦理？当上帝命令亚伯拉罕杀死儿子，亚伯拉罕凭借「信念的悖论」行动——这超越了普遍伦理，是「个体对绝对者的绝对关系」。存在主义对「荒谬」「信仰跳跃」的经典论述。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Through Abraham's sacrifice of Isaac: is faith higher than ethics? Under God's command to kill his son, Abraham acts on 'the paradox of faith' — beyond universal ethics, 'the individual's absolute relation to the absolute'. The classic existential account of absurdity and the leap of faith.

representativeWorks.title: 《致死的疾病》
representativeWorks.content: 分析「绝望」的现象学：绝望是「致死的疾病」——不是因为绝望会杀死你，而是因为绝望的人无法死去，他被困在自我的分裂中。书中对「成为自我」的分析深刻影响了海德格尔的《存在与时间》。
representativeWorks.contentEn: A phenomenology of despair: despair is the sickness unto death — not because it kills you, but because the despairing person cannot die, trapped in self-division. Its analysis of 'becoming a self' deeply shaped Heidegger's Being and Time.

coreThoughts.desc: 克尔凯郭尔对黑格尔的致命反击：真理不是客观体系，而是「个体在热情中无限投入地选择的东西」。他举了个著名的例子：一个祈祷者真诚地向着偶像祈祷，与一个「正确地」向真神却心不在焉地祈祷的人——谁更接近真理？他的回答：真诚者。因为「真理」不是「相信正确命题」，而是「成为一个真实的人」。这个转向把哲学的重心从「世界是什么」移到「我该如何存在」——存在主义的根本姿态。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：克尔凯郭尔说别管「真理是什么」，要问「我怎么活」——真诚地活出自己的选择，比正确地说出教条更重要。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像学游泳和看游泳书：书上写的都对，但你跳下水才知道自己会不会——克尔凯郭尔说真理得跳进水里才算数。
coreThoughts.l3: 「主体性即真理」（Subjectivity is Truth）：真理 = 客观不确定 + 内在热情的无限投入。克尔凯郭尔区分「客观反思」（寻求确定性）与「主观反思」（寻求意义）；黑格尔的体系恰恰是客观反思的极致，而它无法回答「我应该如何存在」。此命题是萨特「存在先于本质」与整个存在主义传统的源头。
coreThoughts.descEn: The fatal counter to Hegel: truth is not objective system but what the individual chooses with infinite passionate commitment. A man praying sincerely to an idol vs. one praying correctly but absent-mindedly to the true God — who is closer to truth? The sincere one. Truth is not believing right propositions but becoming a real person.
coreThoughts.l1En: Don't ask 'what is truth' but 'how do I live' — sincerely living your choice matters more than correctly reciting doctrine.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like swimming versus reading about swimming: the book is all correct, but you only know in the water. Truth must be jumped into.
coreThoughts.l3En: Truth = objective uncertainty held in the most passionate inwardness. Objective reflection seeks certainty; subjective reflection seeks meaning. Hegel's system is objective reflection at its extreme — and it cannot answer 'how should I exist'. This is the source of Sartre's existence precedes essence.

coreThoughts.desc: 克尔凯郭尔的信仰不是「相信上帝存在」的理智判断，而是在荒谬面前的「跳跃」（leap）：亚伯拉罕无法用理性解释为什么应该杀子献祭，但信仰者就在这荒谬的张力中把一切押上去。「信仰始于理性穷尽之处」——不是反理性，而是理性的界限处，人必须用「决断」补上理性给不了的确定性。这正是他与启蒙理性主义的分水岭：理性给不了你活着的意义，意义的给出者只有选择本身。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：克尔凯郭尔说信仰没法论证，也没法靠证据——它是在理性能证明的和不能证明的边界上，自己跳过去的那一下。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像跳悬崖：你站在岸边算不出对面有多远（理性），但要么跳（信仰），要么回去——人生的大问题都在这悬崖边。
coreThoughts.l3: 「信念的悖论」：信仰 = 荒谬（absurdum）中的跳跃；亚伯拉罕是「信念的骑士」（knight of faith）。与黑格尔「扬弃」相反，跳跃是断裂不是连续。此概念经雅斯贝尔斯、蒂利希进入 20 世纪神学；无神论存在主义（萨特、加缪）则把同一结构用在「无上帝的荒谬」上。
coreThoughts.descEn: Faith is not an intellectual judgment that God exists but a leap in the face of the absurd: Abraham cannot rationally justify sacrificing Isaac, yet the believer stakes everything in that absurd tension. Faith begins where reason ends — not against reason, but at its limit, where decision must supply the certainty reason cannot.
coreThoughts.l1En: Faith cannot be argued or evidenced — it is the jump made at the boundary where proof ends.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like standing at a cliff: you cannot measure the far side (reason), but either you jump (faith) or you go back — life's great questions stand at such cliffs.
coreThoughts.l3En: The paradox of faith: the leap in the absurd; Abraham the knight of faith. Against Hegel's sublation, the leap is rupture, not continuity. Via Jaspers and Tillich into 20th-century theology; atheist existentialists (Sartre, Camus) apply the same structure to absurdity without God.

famousEvents.title: 解除婚约
famousEvents.desc: 与蕾吉娜·奥尔森订婚一年后，克尔凯郭尔解除了婚约——他认为是自己的「忧郁」让她无法承受，也认为自己的使命不容婚姻。这个伤口成了他一生的写作燃料，《非此即彼》等书里处处可见蕾吉娜的影子。
famousEvents.descEn: A year after his engagement to Regine Olsen he broke it off — convinced his melancholy would crush her and that his vocation forbade marriage. The wound fueled a lifetime of writing; Regine's shadow lies over Either/Or and more.

famousEvents.title: 《海盗报》论战
famousEvents.desc: 丹麦最著名的讽刺周刊《海盗报》攻击他，他反手与之论战，结果成为哥本哈根街头被嘲讽的对象——这次经历加深了他对「群众/公众」的蔑视，强化了「个体对抗群体」的主题。
famousEvents.descEn: Attacked by Denmark's most famous satirical weekly, he counterattacked and ended up the laughingstock of Copenhagen streets — deepening his contempt for 'the crowd' and sharpening the theme of the individual against the public.

famousEvents.title: 教堂大罢工与猝死
famousEvents.desc: 生命最后一年，他发动对丹麦国教的公开攻击（「基督教的官方化是最大的亵渎」），宣布不再进教堂。同年 10 月他晕倒在街头，几周后去世，年仅 42 岁。
famousEvents.titleEn: The Church Attack and Sudden Death
famousEvents.descEn: In his final year he publicly attacked the Danish state church ('official Christianity is the greatest blasphemy') and refused to attend. He collapsed in the street that October and died weeks later at 42.

philosophers.scientificEval: 克尔凯郭尔对科学的直接影响有限，但其「个体性」「主观性」「焦虑」的现象学分析在 20 世纪被心理学（存在主义心理学、罗洛·梅、欧文·亚隆）、精神病学（宾斯万格的存在分析）与神学（巴特、蒂利希）广泛吸收。《致死的疾病》的绝望分析被视为现代焦虑/抑郁研究的思想先驱之一。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: Kierkegaard's direct scientific influence is limited, but his phenomenology of individuality, subjectivity, and anxiety was absorbed by existential psychology (Rollo May, Irvin Yalom), psychiatry (Binswanger's Daseinsanalyse), and theology (Barth, Tillich). The Sickness unto Death's analysis of despair is a recognized forerunner of modern anxiety and depression studies.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 克尔凯郭尔的思想谱系清晰：早年受苏格拉底「认识你自己」与浪漫派影响，青年时期经历婚约解除与《海盗报》事件的双重打击，使他确认了「个体 vs 群体」的立场；1843-1846 年是假名著作期（审美/伦理/宗教三阶段、恐惧与战栗、致死的疾病）；1846 年后转向直接署名的「基督教著作」，最终以对国教的正面进攻结束生命。他的哲学不是体系——他故意拒绝体系，因为「体系是给体系者的，存在是给存在者的」。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: His lineage is clear: Socrates' know-thyself and Romanticism early; the broken engagement and Corsair affair confirmed the individual-vs-crowd stance; 1843-46 the pseudonymous works (stages, Fear and Trembling, Sickness unto Death); after 1846 signed Christian writings, ending in open assault on the state church. He refused system deliberately: 'systems are for systematizers; existence is for existers.'
philosophers.aiReview: 克尔凯郭尔是那种「用生命写哲学」的人：他的一切命题——焦虑、绝望、跳跃、个体——都是自己先活过的。解约的伤口、被嘲笑的街头、对国教的怒火，全是第一手的材料。这也是他的哲学至今仍有杀伤力的原因：当你在深夜面对「我到底是谁、为什么活着」时，黑格尔帮不了你，而克尔凯郭尔会说：这正是你该独自面对的时刻。他当然有争议：对「群体」的蔑视可以滑向精英主义；「信仰的跳跃」也可以被解释为反智主义。但他说得最重的那句话至今有效：人群（公众）不是真理的载体，每个人必须自己回答自己的问题——在信息爆炸的今天，这句话比 1840 年代更需要被听见。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Kierkegaard wrote philosophy with his life: anxiety, despair, the leap, the individual — all lived first. The broken engagement, the mocked streets, the fury at the church: all first-hand material. That is why he still cuts deep: when you face at midnight 'who am I, why live', Hegel cannot help — Kierkegaard says: this is precisely the moment you must face alone. Controversial, of course: contempt for the crowd can slide into elitism; the leap can read as anti-intellectualism. But his heaviest sentence still holds: the public is not the bearer of truth; each must answer their own question — in today's information flood, this needs hearing more than in the 1840s.

furtherReading.title: 《恐惧与战栗》（一谌中译本）
furtherReading.desc: 存在主义信仰哲学代表作

philosophers.anecdote: 克尔凯郭尔一生都生活在哥本哈根，他的「散步」是这座城市的著名景观：每天下午准时出现在街道上，身后跟着一群孩子模仿他。他一边走一边想，回家就把思考写成书。他终生保持父亲留下的巨额遗产而生活简朴，唯一的大手笔是包下一家戏院的包厢——为了气他的情敌。他死后，人们在他的书桌里发现一封没写完的信，收信人是蕾吉娜。
philosophers.anecdoteEn: He lived all his life in Copenhagen; his daily afternoon walk was a famous sight, with children trailing to imitate him. He thought while walking and wrote when home. Living plainly on his father's fortune, his one extravagance was renting a theater box to annoy a rival. After his death, an unfinished letter to Regine was found in his desk.

philosophers.name: 孔德
philosophers.role: 实证主义创始人，「社会学」一词的发明者
philosophers.summary: 法国思想家，实证主义哲学的创始人，也是「社会学」（sociologie）这个词的发明者。他提出的「三阶段规律」：人类思想从神学阶段（神话解释）经形而上学阶段（抽象本质解释）走向实证阶段（科学规律解释）——历史是理性不断胜利的过程。他的《实证哲学教程》六卷巨著试图把自然科学的方法推广到人类社会，让「社会物理学」像牛顿力学一样精确。晚年他更创立了「人道教」，把自己奉为实证主义的大祭司——这个荒唐的尾巴常常让人忘记他思想的严肃内核：科学可以，也应该指导人类生活。
philosophers.summaryEn: French thinker, founder of positivism, and inventor of the word 'sociology' (sociologie). His law of three stages: human thought moves from the theological (myth), through the metaphysical (abstract essences), to the positive (scientific laws) — history as the victory march of reason. His six-volume Course of Positive Philosophy sought to extend natural-scientific method to society, making 'social physics' as precise as Newtonian mechanics. Late in life he founded the Religion of Humanity, installing himself as high priest — an absurd tail that often hides the serious core: science can and should guide human life.

representativeWorks.title: 《实证哲学教程》
representativeWorks.content: 六卷巨著：从天文学、物理学、化学、生物学到「社会物理学」（社会学），逐门科学考察其实证方法的发展。全书的高潮是断言：社会科学终将像自然科学一样建立在观察与规律之上。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Six volumes surveying astronomy, physics, chemistry, biology, and 'social physics' (sociology), tracing the development of positive method in each. The climax: social science will become as empirical and law-governed as natural science.

representativeWorks.title: 《实证政治体系》
representativeWorks.content: 四卷本：把实证主义扩展到政治、伦理与宗教，提出「人道教」与「实证伦理」——社会的组织原则应以科学知识为基础，以利他主义（altruism，孔德造的词）为道德核心。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Four volumes extending positivism to politics, ethics, and religion: the Religion of Humanity and a positive ethics founded on scientific knowledge with altruism (a word Comte coined) at its moral core.

coreThoughts.desc: 孔德的历史哲学：每一种知识体系都要经历三个阶段——神学阶段（用神和灵魂解释世界）、形而上学阶段（用本质和实体解释世界）、实证阶段（只研究现象之间的规律，不问「为什么」而问「如何」）。物理学和化学已经到达实证阶段，生物学正在路上，而社会科学（他发明的「社会学」）将最终完成这个进程。这个规律是进步观念最系统化的版本：历史不是循环，不是退步，而是理性的凯旋。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：孔德说人类思想像一个人成长：先信神话（童年），再信抽象理论（青年），最后只看事实和规律（成年）。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像学物理：小学生问「为什么苹果会掉」，初中生背「万有引力定律」，物理学家说「我来算它的轨迹」——孔德说整个人类都在走这条路。
coreThoughts.l3: 三阶段规律（loi des trois états）：神学（fictif）→ 形而上学（abstrait）→ 实证（scientifique）。每门科学按顺序成熟（数学最早，社会学最晚）。此规律是历史哲学的里程碑，但也因其决定论色彩受到批评：历史真的有这种必然秩序吗？
coreThoughts.descEn: Every body of knowledge passes through three stages: theological (gods and souls), metaphysical (essences and substances), positive (regularities among phenomena — asking how, not why). Physics and chemistry have arrived; biology is en route; social science will complete the march. The most systematic version of progress: history as the triumph of reason.
coreThoughts.l1En: Human thought grows like a person: myth-believing childhood, theory-loving youth, fact-facing adulthood.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like learning physics: children ask why apples fall, students memorize gravity, physicists calculate trajectories — humanity is walking that road.
coreThoughts.l3En: The law of three states: theological, metaphysical, positive. Each science matures in order (math first, sociology last). A milestone of philosophy of history, criticized for its determinism: is history really that orderly?

coreThoughts.desc: 孔德的纲领：社会现象和自然现象一样受规律支配，可以用观察、实验、比较的方法来研究。「社会学」要像物理学研究物质那样研究社会——发现社会静力学（秩序，社会各部分如何协同）与社会动力学（进步，社会如何发展）。这个计划把「社会」变成了科学对象，直接奠基了现代社会科学；而「科学家治国」（实证政治）的结论——由掌握科学知识的人来组织社会——则成为后来的技术官僚主义与科学主义争论的源头。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：孔德说社会和人其实也像物理现象一样有规律——研究社会的科学就是「社会学」，可以像物理学一样精确。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像研究天气：没有人能「命令」天气，但气象学家能预测它——孔德说社会也一样，可以被科学地理解。
coreThoughts.l3: 社会静力学（statique）研究社会秩序的条件，社会动力学（dynamique）研究社会进步（三阶段规律即动力学核心）。孔德创造了 sociologie 与 altruisme 两个词。其「实证政治」主张科学精英治理，被密尔质疑、被波普尔批判为「历史主义」，但其科学化社会的理想深刻塑造了 19-20 世纪的社会工程传统。
coreThoughts.descEn: Social phenomena obey laws like natural ones and can be studied by observation, experiment, and comparison. Sociology must study society as physics studies matter — statics (order, how parts cohere) and dynamics (progress, how it develops). This made 'society' an object of science and founded the modern social sciences; 'scientist rulers' became the seed of technocracy debates.
coreThoughts.l1En: Society has regularities like physical phenomena — the science of society can be as precise as physics.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like weather: no one commands it, but meteorologists can predict it — society too can be scientifically understood.
coreThoughts.l3En: Social statics (conditions of order) and dynamics (progress). He coined 'sociology' and 'altruism'. His positive polity of scientific elites was questioned by Mill and attacked by Popper as historicism, yet the ideal of a scientific society shaped modern social engineering.

famousEvents.title: 精神崩溃与再起
famousEvents.desc: 1826 年孔德因工作过劳与婚姻不幸精神崩溃，次年恢复后重整旗鼓，开始系统的《实证哲学教程》写作，并在巴黎开设免费的实证哲学讲座，听众中包括密尔等后来者。
famousEvents.descEn: A collapse from overwork and unhappy marriage in 1826; recovered the next year, he relaunched with the Course and free lectures in Paris, attracting hearers including John Stuart Mill.

famousEvents.title: 与人道教
famousEvents.desc: 晚期孔德创立「人道教」：以人类（Grand-Être）为崇拜对象，设计了实证历法、圣殿与祭仪，自任大祭司。科学主义走向了它最奇特的宗教形态——知识分子被科学理想鼓舞却无法安放情感需求的寓言。
famousEvents.descEn: Late Comte founded the Religion of Humanity, worshipping Humanity (Grand-Être) with calendars, temples, and rituals, himself as high priest. Science's most curious religious form — a parable of intellectuals inspired by science yet needing somewhere to put their feelings.

philosophers.scientificEval: 孔德是「科学主义」与「实证方法」的奠基性倡导者：他明确划定科学与形而上学的界限（科学只研究现象与规律）、主张观察与实验优先，为 19 世纪科学方法论提供了纲领。他创立的「社会学」学科规划、社会静力学/动力学框架，直接影响了涂尔干（自认继承孔德事业）与整个法国社会学学派。波普尔将其历史规律论批判为「历史主义」的错误，但其「社会科学可以像自然科学一样严谨」的理想至今仍是社会科学的自我期许。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: Comte is the foundational advocate of positivism and empirical method: science studies only phenomena and their laws, observation and experiment first. His plan for sociology and the statics/dynamics frame directly shaped Durkheim (his self-declared heir) and the French school. Popper attacked his laws of history as historicism, yet the ideal of rigorous social science remains social science's own aspiration.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 孔德的思想轨迹是「从数学到社会学再到宗教」：他早年就读巴黎综合理工学院，数学出身，做过圣西门（空想社会主义者）的秘书七年，从圣西门那里继承了「科学改造社会」的信念；1826 年后他独立发展出三阶段规律与实证哲学；1830-1842 年出版《实证哲学教程》；1845 年他遇到克洛蒂尔德·德·沃——一场柏拉图式的爱情（她次年病逝）——此后他的思想转向「情感」与「人道教」，把「爱」放在实证主义的核心（「爱为原则，秩序为基础，进步为目标」）。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: His arc runs 'from mathematics to sociology to religion': trained at the École Polytechnique, seven years as Saint-Simon's secretary (inheriting science-for-society), independent development of the three stages, the Course (1830-42), then in 1845 Clotilde de Vaux — a platonic love cut short by her death next year — turning his thought toward feeling and the Religion of Humanity: 'Love as principle, order as basis, progress as goal.'
philosophers.aiReview: 孔德是现代科学主义的正负极：他正确地看到科学方法可以照亮社会领域（这个洞见催生了整个社会科学），又荒谬地把它推向极端（自封实证主义大祭司，设计拜「人类」的宗教）。他的三阶段规律读起来像人类思想的成长小说，但历史并没有按他的剧本走——20 世纪的科学危机与两次大战让「科学必然带来进步」成为可疑命题。不过，若把孔德放在他的时代：他是在法国大革命的血泊和复辟的混乱中，寻找一种能安顿社会的理性秩序——这个动机本身值得尊重。今天每个说「要用数据说话」「让科学指导决策」的人，都在无意中站在他的肩膀上。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Comte is the positive and negative pole of modern scientism: right that scientific method can illuminate society (the insight that birthed social science), absurd in pushing it to extremes (high priest of the Religion of Humanity). His three stages read like a bildungsroman of thought, but history ignored the script — the 20th century's crises made 'science guarantees progress' doubtful. Yet place him in his time: amid revolutionary blood and restored chaos, he sought a rational order to settle society — a motive worth respect. Everyone saying 'let the data speak' stands on his shoulders.

furtherReading.desc: 重点读第一卷序论与三阶段规律

philosophers.anecdote: 孔德晚年过着一贫如洗却仪式感极强的日子：他每天早睡早起，饮食定量，给克洛蒂尔德·德·沃的亡灵写「三年之约」的晨祷。他把自己的哲学称作「主观综合」，并宣称「我欠科学与艺术的一切，我将以爱来偿还」。他死后，追随者们真把「人道教」办成了有圣殿、历法和节日的组织——在巴黎至今还有「人道教教堂」的遗迹。
philosophers.anecdoteEn: Late Comte lived in poverty yet with intense ritual: fixed sleep and diet, morning prayers to Clotilde de Vaux's memory ('the three-year pact'). He called his system 'subjective synthesis' and declared 'I owe science and art everything; I will repay with love.' After his death followers actually built the Religion of Humanity with temples, calendars, and festivals — traces survive in Paris.

philosophers.name: 皮尔士
philosophers.role: 实用主义创始人，美国最伟大的逻辑学家与符号学之父
philosophers.summary: 美国本土哲学实用主义的真正创始人（詹姆斯后来把「pragmatism」一词发扬光大），也是美国有史以来最伟大的逻辑学家、现代符号学（semiotics）之父。他提出了「皮尔士原则」：一个概念的意义，就在于它可能产生的可感效果的总和——「真理」不过是研究者共同体在无限探索中最终会一致同意的意见。他一生被学术体制排斥（唯一教职被撤），晚年穷困潦倒，靠给辞典撰稿度日，留下十万页手稿，死后半个世纪才被重新发现，被誉为「美国的康德」与「美国的亚里士多德」。
philosophers.summaryEn: The true founder of pragmatism (James later popularized the word) and America's greatest logician, father of modern semiotics. His Peirce principle: the meaning of a concept is the totality of its conceivable sensible effects; 'truth' is the opinion the community of inquirers would ultimately agree on. Excluded from academia (his only chair revoked), impoverished in old age, writing dictionary entries, he left 100,000 pages of manuscripts, rediscovered half a century after death — 'America's Kant' and 'America's Aristotle'.

representativeWorks.title: 《如何使我们的观念清晰》
representativeWorks.content: 实用主义原则的原始表述：「考虑一下我们概念的对象可能具有什么可想象的实际效果——那么，我们对这些效果的概念，就是我们对该对象的全部概念。」发表于《通俗科学月刊》，是实用主义哲学的开篇文献。
representativeWorks.titleEn: How to Make Our Ideas Clear
representativeWorks.contentEn: The original statement of the pragmatic maxim: 'Consider what effects, which might conceivably have practical bearings, we conceive the object of our conception to have. Then, our conception of these effects is the whole of our conception of the object.' Pragmatism's founding document.

representativeWorks.title: 《信念的确定》
representativeWorks.content: 认识论的经典论文：思想的功能是消除怀疑、确立信念；确立信念有四种方法——固执、权威、先验、科学（实验）。科学方法是唯一尊重事实与他者的方法，因为它把信念交给共同体检验。
representativeWorks.contentEn: A classic of epistemology: thought functions to relieve doubt and fix belief; four methods — tenacity, authority, a priori, and science (experiment). Scientific method alone respects fact and others, submitting belief to communal testing.

coreThoughts.concept: 皮尔士原则（实用主义准则）
coreThoughts.desc: 皮尔士给「意义」下的定义：一个概念的意义，等于它可能产生的一切实际效果的集合。说「这个药是甜的」= 如果你尝它，会得到某种味觉；说「这个物体是硬的」= 如果你压它，它不会变形。「一个模糊的概念没有效果，也就没有意义。」这个准则不是「有用即真理」的粗俗版（那是后人误读），而是一种意义理论：两个概念若在所有可想象的情境中产生相同的效果，它们就是同一个概念。它把哲学从字面争论中解放出来——别再吵「上帝存在吗」这种空转的问题，先问「相信他存在 vs 不相信，会有哪些可观察的不同」。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：皮尔士说一个词有没有意义，看它能不能带来「可以观察到的不同」——说和不说它没区别，那这个词就是空的。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像「这把椅子结实」：这句话的意义不在字典里，而在你坐上去它没塌——意义就在「你坐上去」这个效果里。
coreThoughts.l3: 皮尔士原则（pragmatic maxim）：概念的清楚观念 = 其可感效果的集合（1878）。注意与詹姆斯「有用即真理」的区分：皮尔士关心的是意义标准（meaning criterion），不是真理论。此原则后来被逻辑实证主义的「可验证性原则」继承（经詹姆斯、席勒→维也纳学派），是 20 世纪意义理论的重要源头。
coreThoughts.descEn: The meaning of a concept is the totality of its conceivable practical effects. 'This pill is sweet' = if you taste it, you get such-and-such sensation. A vague concept with no effects has no meaning. Not the vulgar 'useful = true' (a misreading), but a theory of meaning: concepts identical in all conceivable effects are identical. Philosophy stops spinning: don't argue empty questions — ask what observable difference the answer makes.
coreThoughts.l1En: A word is meaningful if it makes an observable difference — if saying it changes nothing, it's empty.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like 'this chair is sturdy': the meaning isn't in the dictionary but in sitting down without collapse.
coreThoughts.l3En: The meaning of a concept is the sum of its sensible effects (1878). Distinct from James' 'useful is true': Peirce's maxim is a meaning criterion. Inherited by logical positivism's verifiability principle — a major source of 20th-century meaning theory.

coreThoughts.concept: 可错论与真理的共同体
coreThoughts.desc: 皮尔士的认识论是「可错论」（fallibilism）：任何信念都可能错，科学没有绝对可靠的起点——但这不是怀疑主义，因为真理不是某个人的发现，而是研究者共同体长期探究的最终意见。「真理是探究最终会迫使共同体同意的意见；现实是独立于你我意见的某种东西。」科学之所以可靠，不是因为科学家不会错，而是因为错误会被共同体的实验与批评不断纠正。这个观点同时驳斥了独断论（我有绝对真理）和相对主义（谁都可以有他的真理）。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：皮尔士说科学不是「不会错的圣旨」，而是「不断纠错的合作」——单个科学家会错，但大家一起较真，真理会慢慢浮出来。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像拼图：没有一个人知道全图，但每个人手里的拼图块合在一起，图就越来越完整——真理是共同体拼出来的。
coreThoughts.l3: 可错论（fallibilism）：所有信念皆可修正；真理 = 探究的极限意见（limit of inquiry）。「现实」独立于任何个人意见但可由共同体趋近。这个立场调和了客观主义与怀疑论，被波普尔（猜想-反驳）、科学实在论与社会科学哲学广泛继承。
coreThoughts.conceptEn: Fallibilism and the Community of Inquiry
coreThoughts.descEn: Any belief may be wrong; science has no absolute foundations — but this is not skepticism, because truth is not one person's discovery but the final opinion of the community of inquirers. Science is reliable not because scientists are infallible but because errors are corrected by communal experiment and criticism. This refutes both dogmatism and relativism.
coreThoughts.l1En: Science is not an infallible decree but cooperative error-correction: individuals err; the community's rigor surfaces truth.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a jigsaw: no one holds the full picture, but everyone's pieces combined complete it — truth is assembled by the community.
coreThoughts.l3En: Fallibilism: all beliefs revisable; truth = the limit opinion of inquiry; reality independent of any individual's opinion yet approachable by the community. Harmonizing objectivism and skepticism, inherited by Popper's conjecture-refutation and scientific realism.

famousEvents.title: 唯一教职被撤
famousEvents.desc: 皮尔士在约翰·霍普金斯大学任逻辑学讲师——当时美国唯一的逻辑教席——因性格孤傲与离婚风波，校方未续聘。此后他终生未获正式学术职位。
famousEvents.descEn: At Johns Hopkins he held America's only logic lectureship; his difficult personality and divorce scandal led the university not to renew. He never held an academic post again.

famousEvents.title: 皮尔士-詹姆斯之争
famousEvents.desc: 詹姆斯在加州大学演讲《哲学概念与实际效果》，把皮尔士的准则推向「有用即真理」，皮尔士大为不满，从此改称自己的学说为「实用主义」（pragmaticism）以示区别——「这个词丑得没人会偷」。
famousEvents.descEn: James' 1898 lecture pushed the maxim toward 'useful is true'; Peirce, displeased, renamed his doctrine 'pragmaticism' — 'ugly enough to be safe from kidnappers'.

philosophers.scientificEval: 皮尔士在逻辑学上几乎每一项都领先时代：他独立于弗雷格发展了量化逻辑（1870 年代的成果早于《概念文字》发表时间或同时）、发明了存在图（existential graphs）、提出「溯因推理」（abduction）——发现假设的逻辑，被当代科学哲学（汉森、科斯特）视为科学发现逻辑的先驱。他在概率论（伯努利试验的严格分析）、测地学（光的波长测量）上也有实际贡献。符号学三分类（图像/指示/象征）更是现代语言学与传播学的基石。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: In logic Peirce was ahead of his time on nearly every front: quantification theory independent of (or concurrent with) Frege, existential graphs, and abduction — the logic of hypothesis discovery, recognized as a forerunner of discovery logic. He contributed to probability (strict analysis of Bernoulli trials) and geodesy (measuring the wavelength of light). His icon/index/symbol triad is foundational for linguistics and communication studies.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 皮尔士的思想生涯以「探究」为核心：青年时代（1859-1870）主攻化学与哲学，受康德（他终生自认「康德的信徒」）与经验主义双重影响；中年（1870-1884）完成逻辑与符号学的主要创见，发表《信念的确定》《如何使我们的观念清晰》；此后三十年被学术界遗忘，却写下数十万页手稿，把实用主义细化为符号学、宇宙论与形而上学（「偶成论」tychism）。他始终相信：哲学不靠天才的顿悟，而靠研究者共同体的长期协作——连他自己的命运都是这个信念的注脚。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: His career centered on inquiry: youth (1859-70) chemistry and philosophy, Kantian (he called himself Kant's disciple) and empiricist; middle years (1870-84) the great work in logic and semiotics; then thirty years of academic oblivion producing hundreds of thousands of manuscript pages refining pragmatism into semiotics, cosmology, and tychism. He always believed philosophy advances not by genius flashes but by communal collaboration — his own fate is a footnote to that belief.
philosophers.aiReview: 皮尔士是哲学史上最典型的「死后封神」案例：活着时被体制放逐，死后被重新抬进神殿。他的实用主义准则至今被无数人挂在嘴边，但多半挂在詹姆斯的通俗版本上——那个「有用即真理」的版本。真正的皮尔士其实更冷静：他关心的是意义的标准，不是真理的捷径；他强调可错论，拒绝一切独断；他的符号学和逻辑学领先时代半个世纪。他的孤傲与坎坷既是性格问题也是体制问题——一个不肯迎合的头脑，在 19 世纪的美国大学里注定无处安放。今天，当我们说「科学是自我纠正的过程」「让事实说话」时，说的都是皮尔士的常识。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Peirce is philosophy's textbook case of posthumous canonization: exiled by the system alive, enthroned after death. His maxim is quoted everywhere, usually in James' vulgar version — 'useful is true'. The real Peirce was cooler: meaning criteria, not truth shortcuts; fallibilism against all dogmatism; semiotics and logic half a century ahead. His pride and hardship were both character and system: a mind that would not flatter had no home in 19th-century American academia. When we say 'science is self-correcting' or 'let the facts speak', we are quoting Peirce.

furtherReading.desc: 含《信念的确定》《如何使我们的观念清晰》

philosophers.anecdote: 皮尔士晚年穷困到靠约翰·杜威等后辈接济，他却依旧醉心于实验——他把自家谷仓改造成化学实验室，用妻子的嫁妆买仪器。他唯一的教席被撤后，曾试图在天文台找份测地工作，面试时滔滔不绝讲了三个小时的逻辑学，把考官们讲得目瞪口呆，最后没被录用。他在日记里写道：「我这一生都在为人们做事，人们却认为我一事无成。」
philosophers.anecdoteEn: In poverty, supported by Dewey and younger admirers, he converted his barn into a chemical lab funded by his wife's dowry. After losing his chair he sought a geodesy post; at the interview he lectured three hours on logic, stunning the examiners — and was not hired. His diary: 'I have spent my life serving people who thought I accomplished nothing.'

philosophers.name: 威廉·詹姆斯
philosophers.role: 实用主义旗手，美国心理学之父
philosophers.summary: 美国哲学的黄金人物：既是「美国心理学之父」（《心理学原理》1890），又是实用主义哲学的代表（《实用主义》1907）。他出身富有的知识分子家庭（弟弟是小说家亨利·詹姆斯），本人一度体弱多病、饱受抑郁折磨，正是与疾病的搏斗让他的哲学充满对「心灵如何运作」的切身关怀。他的「意识流」概念、情绪理论（詹姆斯-兰格理论）、真理的实用主义理论，横跨心理学与哲学两个领域，影响遍及 20 世纪美国思想。
philosophers.summaryEn: The golden man of American philosophy: father of American psychology (Principles of Psychology, 1890) and standard-bearer of pragmatism (Pragmatism, 1907). Born into a wealthy intellectual family (brother novelist Henry James), plagued by illness and depression, his struggle with disease gave his philosophy a lived concern with how minds actually work. His stream of consciousness, the James-Lange theory of emotion, and the pragmatic theory of truth span psychology and philosophy, shaping American thought for a century.

representativeWorks.title: 《心理学原理》
representativeWorks.content: 两卷本巨著，奠定美国心理学：提出「意识流」（stream of consciousness）、习惯与情绪的躯体理论（詹姆斯-兰格理论）、自我分析（经验的自我/社会自我/精神自我）。文笔优美，至今仍是心理学与哲学交叉的经典。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Two volumes founding American psychology: the stream of consciousness, habit, the James-Lange theory of emotion, and the analysis of the self (material, social, spiritual). Beautifully written, still a classic at the psychology-philosophy interface.

representativeWorks.title: 《实用主义》
representativeWorks.content: 八次演讲集：实用主义作为「哲学之间的调解人」——真理不是静止的复制，而是「行之有效的观念」；概念是「经验之舟的桨」。此书使实用主义成为 20 世纪初最具影响力的美国哲学运动。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Eight lectures: pragmatism as 'mediator between philosophies' — truth not a static copy but 'what works in the way of belief'; concepts are 'oars of the boat of experience'. It made pragmatism the most influential American movement of the early 20th century.

representativeWorks.title: 《宗教经验之种种》
representativeWorks.content: 对宗教经验的心理学研究：神秘经验、皈依经验、圣徒生活的实证考察。「宗教是真实的，因为它有效果」——用实用主义方法为宗教经验辩护，被誉为宗教心理学的奠基之作。
representativeWorks.contentEn: A psychological study of religious experience: mysticism, conversion, saintliness, examined empirically. Religion is real because it works — defending religious experience by pragmatic method. The founding text of the psychology of religion.

coreThoughts.desc: 詹姆斯对心理学最重要的贡献：意识不是一串断开的珠子，而是一条流动的河——「意识流」。没有静止的「感觉原子」，只有持续的、有选择性的流动；「自我」也不是一个稳定的实体，而是这条流中被注意的中心。这个观念打破了 19 世纪心理学的原子主义（把意识拆成元素），直接启发了意识研究、意识流文学（乔伊斯、伍尔夫）与现代认知科学。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：詹姆斯说你的意识不是一张张静止的照片，而是一条停不下来的河——没有「现在的我」，只有「正在流动的我」。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像河水：你没法把河切成一段段摆进瓶子，它永远是流动的整体——你的念头也是这么流动的。
coreThoughts.l3: 意识流（stream of consciousness, 1890）：意识是连续的、变化的、有选择性的、有边缘的（边缘意识/焦点意识）。「自我」= 经验自我（物质的/社会的/精神的）+ 纯粹自我。此概念深刻影响意识研究（丹尼特的多重草稿模型与之呼应）、意识流文学与临床心理学。
coreThoughts.descEn: Consciousness is not a string of beads but a flowing river: no static atoms of sensation, only continuous selective flow; the self is not a fixed entity but the attended center of the stream. This broke the atomism of 19th-century psychology, inspiring consciousness research, stream-of-consciousness literature (Joyce, Woolf), and cognitive science.
coreThoughts.l1En: Your consciousness is not a series of still photographs but a river that never stops — there is no 'now-me', only 'me-in-flow'.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a river: you cannot bottle it in sections; it is always a flowing whole — so are your thoughts.
coreThoughts.l3En: Consciousness is continuous, changing, selective, with fringes (focus and margin). The self: empirical (material/social/spiritual) and pure. Echoed by Dennett's multiple drafts, stream-of-consciousness literature, and clinical psychology.

coreThoughts.desc: 詹姆斯的实用主义真理观：真理不是一个躺着等你发现的现成图景，而是「观念在经验中起作用」的过程——一个观念如果引导我们成功应对世界、让经验协调一致，它就是真的。「真理是在经验之河中造船的桨」。这个理论被批评为「有用即真理」的粗俗版，但詹姆斯本人的表述更微妙：他反对的是「真理=永恒不变的副本」，主张真理是「在经验中兑现的承诺」。它最激进的含义：真理可以有未来时态——一个现在还没被证实的观念，可能因为未来的成功而成为真理。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：詹姆斯说真理不是天上挂好的成品，而是「经得起检验的想法」——它让你过得顺、想得通、世界对得上，就是真的。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像一把钥匙：你说它是「真的钥匙」还是「假的钥匙」？——看它能不能打开门。真理也一样，得看它能不能打开经验的锁。
coreThoughts.l3: 詹姆斯的真理论：真理 = 观念的「现金价值」（cash value）在经验中的兑现；「真理是制造出来的」（truth happens to an idea）。此说与其弟亨利·詹姆斯的小说、与杜威的工具主义一脉相承，但被罗素、摩尔批评为混淆「真」与「有用」；罗蒂后来以「真理没有本质」继承其精神。
coreThoughts.descEn: Truth is not a ready-made picture awaiting discovery but the process of ideas working in experience: an idea is true if it guides us successfully, making experience coherent. 'Truth is an oar built in the river of experience.' Against truth as eternal copy, truth as a promise cashed out in experience — radically, truth can have a future tense.
coreThoughts.l1En: Truth is not a finished product hanging in heaven but an idea that passes the test — it lets you cope, makes things cohere, so it's true.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a key: is it 'truly' a key? — see whether it opens the door. Truth must open experience's locks.
coreThoughts.l3En: Truth is the cash value of an idea in experience; 'truth happens to an idea'. Continuous with Dewey's instrumentalism, criticized by Russell and Moore for conflating true and useful; Rorty later inherits the spirit in 'truth has no essence'.

famousEvents.title: 抑郁危机与「自由意志的第一次选择」
famousEvents.desc: 28 岁的詹姆斯陷入严重的抑郁，被「自由意志是否存在」的形而上学问题折磨。他在日记里写道，他决定「相信自由意志是真实的，并看它是否改变我的生活」——这个实用主义式的决断让他走出低谷，也成了他哲学的个人起源。
famousEvents.titleEn: The Crisis and the First Pragmatic Choice
famousEvents.descEn: At 28, deep in depression over whether free will exists, he wrote in his diary his decision to 'believe free will is real and see if it changes my life' — a pragmatic resolve that saved him and became the personal origin of his philosophy.

famousEvents.title: 与罗素论战
famousEvents.desc: 罗素与摩尔在英国抨击实用主义「混淆真与有用」，詹姆斯赴英答辩，双方论战成为 20 世纪初英美学界最著名的哲学交锋之一——分析哲学与实用主义的第一次正面碰撞。
famousEvents.descEn: Russell and Moore attacked pragmatism in Britain for conflating truth and utility; James defended it in person — one of the early 20th century's most famous philosophical clashes, the first collision of analytic philosophy and pragmatism.

philosophers.scientificEval: 詹姆斯是实验心理学制度化的重要推手：他于 1875 年在哈佛建立了美国第一个心理学教学实验室（早于冯特莱比锡实验室的教学功能）；《心理学原理》综合了当时的生理心理学成果并加以批判整合。詹姆斯-兰格情绪理论（情绪=对身体反应的知觉）虽后被修正，却是情绪研究史上第一个可检验的躯体理论，至今仍是情绪认知研究绕不开的参照。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: James institutionalized experimental psychology: the first American psychology teaching laboratory at Harvard (1875); the Principles synthesized and criticized physiological psychology. The James-Lange theory (emotion = perception of bodily changes), though later revised, was the first testable bodily theory of emotion and remains a reference point.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 詹姆斯的道路是「从医学到心理学再到哲学」：他先学医（哈佛医学院），随亚马逊考察队远行，后转向生理学与心理学；1872 年起在哈佛任教，从解剖学教到心理学再到哲学。他的哲学从个人危机中生长：对自由意志的「选择」、对宗教经验的「验证」、对多元论的坚持（「多元宇宙」pluriverse），都带着体温。晚年他转向彻底经验主义与形而上学的多元论，反对一切一元论的「大体系」——「相信存在一个整体宇宙的人，和相信宇宙由许多部分组成的人，过的是不同的生活」。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: His road runs 'medicine to psychology to philosophy': medical school, an Amazon expedition, then physiology and psychology; at Harvard from 1872, teaching anatomy, then psychology, then philosophy. His philosophy grew from personal crisis: the choice of free will, the verification of religious experience, the pluralism of the 'pluriverse' — all warm with lived temperature. Late James turned to radical empiricism and metaphysical pluralism against every monistic grand system: believers in one universe and believers in many live different lives.
philosophers.aiReview: 詹姆斯是美国哲学里最「像人」的哲学家：他不端架子，不造体系，把哲学写成了对心灵困境的诚实记录。他的「真理即行之有效」常被漫画化，但他真正的立场其实是：观念应该为人生服务，而不是反过来——在绝对主义与虚无主义之间，他坚持走那条「以效果检验」的中间路。批评者（罗素等）说他混淆了真与有用，这个批评有道理，但詹姆斯早有回应：他关心的从来不是逻辑学家的「真」，而是活人的「真」。今天，当认知科学讨论意识流、当心理治疗强调「检验信念」、当「多元宇宙」成为流行词，我们都在与詹姆斯对话。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: James is the most human of American philosophers: no airs, no system, philosophy as honest record of mental struggle. His 'truth as what works' is often caricatured; his real position: ideas should serve life, not vice versa — between absolutism and nihilism, the middle way of testing by effects. Russell's critique (conflating true and useful) has force; James answered in advance: he never meant the logician's truth but the living person's. When cognitive science discusses the stream of consciousness, therapy tests beliefs, and 'multiverse' goes viral, we are talking with James.

furtherReading.title: 《实用主义》（陈羽纶/孙瑞禾中译本）
furtherReading.desc: 詹姆斯代表作，通俗而深刻

philosophers.anecdote: 詹姆斯以「在路上」闻名：他是美国哲学史上最爱远行的哲学家之一，多次往返欧洲，在柏林拜访过赫尔姆霍茨，在法国与柏格森会面并深受震动（「柏格森是唯一真正拒绝了康德-黑格尔框架的人」）。他讲课也「在路上」——一边散步一边授课，学生要跟着他在校园里转圈。他 68 岁去世时，哈佛的挽联写着：「他教过我们如何思考，更教过我们如何生活。」
philosophers.anecdoteEn: James was famous for being on the road: among philosophy's great travelers, visiting Helmholtz in Berlin, meeting Bergson in France and shaken by him ('the only thinker who really breaks with the Kant-Hegel frame'). He lectured while walking, students circling campus behind him. At his death at 68, Harvard's tribute: 'He taught us how to think, and more, how to live.'

relationships.description: 推广皮尔士的实用主义准则，虽然后来分歧
柏格森的时间与直觉观令其深受震动
杜威继承实用主义并将其工具主义化
与罗素论战「真理是否等于有用」

goldenQuotes.text: 行动看似跟随情感，其实行动与情感并行；行动调节情感，情感又被行动调节。
goldenQuotes.textEn: Action seems to follow feeling, but really action and feeling go together; and by regulating the action, which is under the more direct control of the will, we can indirectly regulate the feeling.

goldenQuotes.text: 相信的意志：我们的激情本性不仅合法地、而且必然地决定一些哲学问题的取舍。
goldenQuotes.textEn: Our passional nature not only lawfully may, but must, decide an option between propositions, whenever it is a genuine option that cannot by its nature be decided on intellectual grounds.

philosophers.name: 柏格森
philosophers.role: 生命哲学大师，直觉主义与绵延哲学的创立者
philosophers.summary: 20 世纪初法国乃至整个欧洲最耀眼的哲学家：1927 年诺贝尔文学奖得主（史上唯一获此奖的纯粹哲学家），其巴黎讲座一票难求，连普鲁斯特、詹姆斯、丘吉尔都是听众。他的核心命题：科学用「空间化的时间」理解世界，但真实的生命时间（绵延）是连续的、不可分割的流动——理解生命不能靠分析（理智），只能靠直觉。他的《创造进化论》提出「生命冲动」（élan vital），直接影响文学（意识流）、心理学（记忆研究）与哲学（怀特海、德勒兹）。晚年他拒绝接受纳粹统治下的「犹太人豁免」，在巴黎街头排队登记时感染肺炎去世。
philosophers.summaryEn: The most dazzling philosopher of early 20th-century Europe: Nobel Prize in Literature 1927 (the only pure philosopher so honored), his Paris lectures oversold with Proust, James, and Churchill among the audience. His core thesis: science understands the world through spatialized time, but real lived time (durée) is continuous, indivisible flow — life is grasped not by analysis (intellect) but by intuition. Creative Evolution's élan vital shaped literature (stream of consciousness), psychology (memory research), and philosophy (Whitehead, Deleuze). In 1941 he refused the 'Jew exemption' under Nazi rule, stood in line in Paris to register, caught pneumonia, and died.

representativeWorks.title: 《时间与自由意志》
representativeWorks.content: 柏格森的成名作：区分「空间化的时间」（被科学量化为钟表刻度的同质时间）与「绵延」（被体验的、流动的、质性的时间）。自由意志之谜源于我们把后者误当成前者。
representativeWorks.contentEn: His breakthrough: distinguishing spatialized time (homogeneous clock time quantified by science) from durée (lived, flowing, qualitative time). The mystery of free will arises from mistaking the latter for the former.

representativeWorks.title: 《创造进化论》
representativeWorks.content: 提出「生命冲动」（élan vital）：生命不是机械因果的产物，而是一股持续创造、自我分化的冲动，在进化中分出植物、节肢动物与脊椎动物三条路；理智（intelligence）是脊椎动物路线的工具，而直觉（intuition）能通达生命的绵延本身。此书让柏格森名满全球。
representativeWorks.contentEn: The élan vital: life is not mechanical causation but a continuous creative impulse that differentiates into plants, arthropods, and vertebrates; intellect is the tool of the vertebrate line, while intuition reaches duration itself. The book made him world-famous.

representativeWorks.title: 《物质与记忆》
representativeWorks.content: 身心关系与记忆哲学：记忆不是大脑中的「仓库」，而是绵延在当下对过去的持续介入；大脑只是「过滤器」，删减记忆以服务行动。此书影响了神经科学与意识研究对记忆的理解。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Mind-body and memory: memory is not a storehouse in the brain but duration's continuous intervention of the past into the present; the brain is a filter, deleting memory to serve action. Influential for neuroscience and consciousness studies.

coreThoughts.desc: 柏格森最核心的概念：真实的时间不是钟表上的刻度（那是空间化的、可以切割的），而是绵延（durée）——一种连续的、不可分割的流动，像一支旋律，你不能把它切成音符而不杀死它。钟表时间把「时间」变成了空间（刻度排成一排），这是科学和日常语言的习惯，却不是生命的真相。记忆、意识、自由意志都只在绵延中存在：当你犹豫不决时，你的过去正整体地渗入当下——这才是自由。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：柏格森说钟表量出来的不是真正的时间——真正的时间像一段旋律，只能被体验，不能被切成刻度。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像听歌：把一首歌切成 100 个瞬间，你还是没听到那首歌——歌在音符与音符之间的流动里，时间也一样。
coreThoughts.l3: 绵延（durée）vs 空间化时间（temps spatialisé）：前者是质性的、不可分的、创造的；后者是同质的、可分的、量的。自由 = 自我在绵延中的自我决定，而非被因果链决定。此概念深刻影响：意识流文学（乔伊斯、伍尔夫）、现象学（海德格尔的时间性）、德勒兹的「差异哲学」、当代时间哲学。
coreThoughts.descEn: Real time is not the clock's ticks (spatialized, divisible) but durée — continuous, indivisible flow, like a melody that dies when cut into notes. Clock time turns time into space; science and language habituate us to this, but life's truth is flow. Memory, consciousness, free will exist only in duration: in hesitation, your whole past permeates the present — that is freedom.
coreThoughts.l1En: The clock does not measure real time — real time is like a melody: experienced, never divisible into ticks.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like listening to music: cutting a song into 100 instants still fails to give you the song — the song lives in the flow between notes, and so does time.
coreThoughts.l3En: Durée vs spatialized time: the first qualitative, indivisible, creative; the second homogeneous, divisible, quantitative. Freedom = the self's self-determination in duration. Influences: stream-of-consciousness literature, Heidegger's temporality, Deleuze's philosophy of difference, contemporary philosophy of time.

coreThoughts.desc: 《创造进化论》的纲领：进化不是达尔文式的偶然变异+自然选择那么简单，背后有一股「生命冲动」（élan vital）——一股持续的创造冲动，自我分化出不同的生命路线。理智（intelligence）是这条冲动发展出来应对无生命物质的工具（善于分析、空间化），但面对生命本身（绵延、创造、整体）却力不从心——就像用尺子量音乐。要理解生命，需要另一种能力：直觉（intuition）——置身于对象内部、与绵延合一的认知方式。理智给科学，直觉给哲学。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：柏格森说生命的本质是「创造」，不是机械拼装——分析只能拆机器，想懂生命得靠「直觉」，直接融进它的流动里。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像理解一个人：解剖学能告诉你他由什么组成（理智），但「懂他」是另一种知——你和他一起生活过才知道（直觉）。
coreThoughts.l3: élan vital 与达尔文进化论的关系：柏格森接受变异与选择，但质疑其充分性（「创造」维度）；理智/直觉二分；「时间不是进化的剧场，而是进化的作者」。怀特海、德勒兹（《柏格森主义》）、普鲁斯特均深受影响；「生命冲动」在科学上被批评为不可检验，但其对机械论还原的批判至今有价值。
coreThoughts.descEn: Evolution is not merely chance variation plus selection but is driven by an élan vital — a continuous creative impulse differentiating into life's many lines. Intellect, the tool evolved for dealing with inert matter (good at analysis and spatialization), fails before life itself (duration, creation, whole) — like measuring music with a ruler. To understand life we need intuition: cognition from within, coinciding with duration. Intellect for science, intuition for philosophy.
coreThoughts.l1En: Life's essence is creation, not mechanical assembly — analysis only dismantles machines; to understand life, use intuition, merging with its flow.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like knowing a person: anatomy tells you what they're made of (intellect); 'getting them' is another kind of knowing, from living together (intuition).
coreThoughts.l3En: Élan vital accepts variation and selection but questions their sufficiency (the creative dimension). Intellect/intuition dichotomy; time is not evolution's theater but its author. Whitehead, Deleuze (Bergsonism), and Proust are heirs; the élan vital was criticized as untestable, but its critique of mechanistic reduction remains valuable.

famousEvents.title: 巴黎讲座的万人空巷
famousEvents.desc: 柏格森在法兰西学院的讲座成为巴黎的文化事件：绅士淑女们提前数小时排队，会场站满听众，连门廊都挤满人。当时的报纸说「整个巴黎都在读柏格森」。
famousEvents.descEn: His Collège de France lectures became a Parisian cultural event: queues hours early, standing-room-only crowds spilling into the corridors. The papers said 'all Paris reads Bergson'.

famousEvents.title: 诺贝尔文学奖
famousEvents.desc: 因「丰富而生气勃勃的思想和卓越的表达技巧」获诺贝尔文学奖——唯一获此奖的纯粹哲学家。获奖演说中他仍不忘提醒：「诺贝尔奖是一项国家间的礼物，提醒我们世界比国家更大。」
famousEvents.descEn: Awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for 'rich and vitalizing ideas and brilliant presentation' — the only pure philosopher so honored. In his speech he reminded: 'The Nobel Prize is an international gift reminding us that the world is larger than nations.'

famousEvents.title: 拒绝豁免，排队赴死
famousEvents.desc: 纳粹占领巴黎后颁布针对犹太人的登记令，教会愿为这位大哲学家申请豁免，82 岁的柏格森拒绝：「我不愿和我的同胞分开。」他在寒冬清晨排队数小时，感染肺炎，不久后去世。
famousEvents.descEn: Under Nazi occupation the Church offered the great philosopher an exemption from Jewish registration; the 82-year-old refused: 'I will not be separated from my brothers.' He stood in line for hours in the winter cold, caught pneumonia, and died.

philosophers.scientificEval: 柏格森与同时代科学的互动深度惊人：《物质与记忆》与神经科学对话（其记忆观与当代「记忆的建构性」共识高度契合）；《创造进化论》正面回应达尔文；他在 1922 年与爱因斯坦就时间问题进行著名论战——他认为相对论处理的仍是「空间化的时间」，绵延仍是物理时间未触及的维度。当代时间哲学（时间之箭、现在主义/永恒主义之争）仍在回应他的问题；其记忆理论被神经科学界重新发现（如记忆的重构性、背景依赖）。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: Bergson engaged science intensely: Matter and Memory dialogues with neuroscience (his constructive memory view matches modern consensus); Creative Evolution confronts Darwin head-on; his 1922 debate with Einstein held that relativity still treats spatialized time, duration remaining beyond physics. Contemporary philosophy of time (the arrow, presentism vs eternalism) still answers his questions; neuroscience rediscovers his memory theory.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 柏格森的四部代表作构成一条清晰的递进线：《时间与自由意志》（1889）确立绵延概念，回答自由意志问题；《物质与记忆》（1896）以记忆为桥梁处理身心关系；《创造进化论》（1907）把绵延推向宇宙论，提出生命冲动；《道德与宗教的两个来源》（1932）把生命冲动应用于社会——「开放社会」vs「封闭社会」的区分成为其晚年政治哲学。他始终如一的立场：生命高于机械，创造高于重复，直觉补足理智。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: Four masterworks in a clear progression: Time and Free Will (1889) establishes duration and answers free will; Matter and Memory (1896) bridges mind and body via memory; Creative Evolution (1907) extends duration to cosmology with the élan vital; The Two Sources of Morality and Religion (1932) applies it to society — open vs closed society. One constant: life over mechanism, creation over repetition, intuition completing intellect.
philosophers.aiReview: 柏格森是 20 世纪哲学最大的「流星」之一：1910-1920 年代他是全球哲学偶像，1940 年代后几乎被分析哲学运动扫进角落，1980 年代后又被德勒兹等人重新激活——他的命运本身就是他关于「时间」理论的寓言：思想也会在绵延中被重新评价。他的洞见在今天看来依然锋利：人工智能与计算主义越是把一切都还原为「可计算的信息」，柏格森那句「理智面对生命力不从心」就越显得像一个提前说出的警告。当然，他的「生命冲动」确实缺乏可检验性，这也是他被科学主义时代冷落的原因。但把「直觉」完全逐出认识论，同样是一种狭隘。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Bergson is one of the 20th century's great meteors: a global philosophical idol in 1910-20, swept into a corner by the analytic movement after 1940, reactivated by Deleuze in the 1980s — his fate is itself a fable of his theory of time: ideas are re-evaluated in duration. His insight cuts sharper today: the more AI and computationalism reduce everything to computable information, the more his warning that intellect fails before life looks like prophecy. Granted, the élan vital lacks testability — the reason scientism shelved him. But banishing intuition from epistemology entirely is its own narrowness.

philosophers.anecdote: 1922 年柏格森与爱因斯坦在巴黎论战：爱因斯坦说「没有哲学家的时间，只有物理的时间」，柏格森反诘「物理时间正是你们把绵延空间化的结果」。据在场者回忆，爱因斯坦私下承认柏格森「聪明得危险」。另一个轶闻：柏格森晚年皈依天主教（并未受洗），但他解释理由时带着他一贯的时间哲学——「我考虑了五十年，现在终于到了决定的时刻。而这个时刻，就是永恒。」
philosophers.anecdoteEn: In 1922 he debated Einstein in Paris: Einstein — 'there is no philosopher's time, only physical time'; Bergson — 'physical time is precisely your spatialization of duration'. Witnesses say Einstein privately called Bergson 'dangerously clever'. Another story: late in life he leaned toward Catholicism (unbaptized), explaining with his own philosophy of time: 'I have considered for fifty years; now the moment of decision has come. And the moment is eternity.'

philosophers.name: 弗雷格
philosophers.role: 分析哲学之父，现代逻辑学的奠基人
philosophers.summary: 现代逻辑学的奠基人、分析哲学的精神之父——一个生前几乎无人知晓、死后被尊为「哲学家的哲学家」的人。他在 1879 年出版的《概念文字》中发明了现代数理逻辑：量词、变项、函数-自变元分析，一举超越了亚里士多德逻辑两千年的统治。他毕生的事业是证明算术可以还原为逻辑（逻辑主义），这项工作虽未完成（罗素悖论击碎了它），却开创了数理逻辑的整个世纪。他的意义理论（涵义/指称区分）是 20 世纪语言哲学的原点。晚年他寂寞地住在乡村，手稿几乎无人读，只有罗素、维特根斯坦等少数人读懂了他的分量。
philosophers.summaryEn: Founder of modern logic and the spiritual father of analytic philosophy — a philosopher's philosopher, unknown in life, canonized after death. His Begriffsschrift (1879) invented modern mathematical logic: quantifiers, variables, function-argument analysis, surpassing two millennia of Aristotelian logic. His life's project — reducing arithmetic to logic (logicism) — failed (Russell's paradox shattered it) but founded a century of mathematical logic. His theory of meaning (sense/reference) is the origin of 20th-century philosophy of language. He died lonely in a village; only Russell, Wittgenstein, and a few others grasped his weight.

representativeWorks.title: 《概念文字》
representativeWorks.content: 现代逻辑的诞生证书：第一套完整的量化逻辑系统（量词、变项、真值函项），把「所有/存在」的形式结构第一次精确表达出来。弗雷格在此把逻辑从「关于思想形式的三段论」改造成「数学式的形式演算」——人类推理从此有了精确的语言。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Modern logic's birth certificate: the first complete system of quantification (quantifiers, variables, truth-functions), giving precise formal expression to 'all' and 'some' for the first time. Logic transformed from syllogistic forms of thought into a mathematical calculus — human reasoning acquired an exact language.

representativeWorks.title: 《算术基础》
representativeWorks.content: 逻辑主义的宣言：证明算术概念（数、相等、后继）可以只用逻辑概念定义。提出著名的「语境原则」：绝不孤立地询问一个词的意义，而只在命题的语境中询问。这本书也是分析哲学的奠基文献之一。
representativeWorks.contentEn: The logicist manifesto: arithmetic concepts (number, equality, successor) definable in purely logical terms. The famous context principle: never ask for the meaning of a word in isolation, only in the context of a proposition. A founding text of analytic philosophy.

representativeWorks.title: 《论涵义与指称》
representativeWorks.content: 语言哲学的原子弹：区分「晨星/暮星」（同一对象两种涵义）——语词有涵义（Sinn，其被给予的方式）与指称（Bedeutung，其对象）。「晨星=暮星」因指称相同而真，因涵义不同而有信息量。这条区分开启了整个 20 世纪意义理论。
representativeWorks.contentEn: The atom bomb of philosophy of language: morning star/evening star (one object, two senses) — expressions have sense (how the object is given) and reference (the object). 'Morning star = evening star' is true by reference, informative by sense. The distinction opened a century of meaning theory.

coreThoughts.concept: 逻辑主义：算术还原为逻辑
coreThoughts.desc: 弗雷格的毕生计划：数学（尤其算术）不是靠直觉或经验，而是逻辑的延伸——数、加法、归纳都能只用逻辑概念和逻辑定律定义和推导。为此他发明了现代逻辑作为工具。这个计划在 1902 年遭遇致命一击：罗素写信告诉他，他构造的「数集」体系里出现了悖论（罗素悖论：包含所有不含自身的集合的集合是否包含自身？）。弗雷格在《算术基本法则》第二卷付印前写下著名的补遗：「对一个科学家来说，最糟糕的事莫过于在他的工作完成之际，地基却被抽掉了。」逻辑主义虽失败，但它逼出了公理化集合论（策梅洛、罗素-怀特海《数学原理》），现代数学的逻辑基础正是从这里长出来的。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：弗雷格想证明「数学=逻辑」，他造出了现代逻辑这把精密工具，却在完工时发现地基有条裂缝（罗素悖论）——但他留下的工具成了整个 20 世纪思想的标准语言。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像建筑师想用「逻辑」这一种材料盖出数学这座大楼，图纸画到最后一层时发现地基公式有矛盾——但地基的施工方法（现代逻辑）却成了此后所有大楼的标准工艺。
coreThoughts.l3: 逻辑主义（logicism）：数学可还原为逻辑。工具：量化逻辑（1879）。崩塌：罗素悖论（1902）针对《算术基本法则》第五公理（外延原则）——「罗素类」R={x|x∉x}，R∈R ⟺ R∉R。后果：策梅洛-弗兰克尔公理集合论（ZFC）、罗素-怀特海《数学原理》（1910-13）——现代数学基础的真正起点。
coreThoughts.descEn: His life's project: mathematics — especially arithmetic — is not grounded in intuition or experience but is logic's extension; numbers, addition, induction definable and derivable from logical concepts and laws alone. For this he invented modern logic. The project collapsed in 1902 when Russell's paradox struck his system: the set of all sets not containing themselves — does it contain itself? Frege appended a famous note before publishing: 'What a scientist can do worst is to have the ground pulled from under him just as his work is completed.' Yet logicism forced axiomatic set theory into being: the real foundation of modern mathematics.
coreThoughts.l1En: Frege aimed to prove mathematics is logic. He built the precise instrument (modern logic), but at completion found a crack in the foundation (Russell's paradox) — yet the instrument became the standard language of 20th-century thought.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like an architect building the tower of mathematics from a single material, logic, only to find a contradiction in the foundation formulas at the last floor — but the construction method (modern logic) became standard for every later building.
coreThoughts.l3En: Logicism: mathematics reducible to logic. Tool: quantification (1879). Collapse: Russell's paradox (1902) on the axiom of extension — R={x|x∉x}, R∈R ⟺ R∉R. Consequence: Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory and Principia Mathematica (1910-13) — the true foundation of modern mathematics.

coreThoughts.desc: 弗雷格用「晨星与暮星」这个例子开启了语言哲学：两个短语指称同一个天体（金星），但涵义不同——一个是「清晨出现的星」，一个是「黄昏出现的星」。「晨星=暮星」这句话之所以不是废话，正因为指称相同而涵义不同。同理，「亚里士多德」与「亚历山大的老师」指称同一个人，却有不同涵义。这条区分的重要性：它说明意义不是简单的「词=物」的对应，语言通过「涵义」这个中间层与世界相连——20 世纪的意义理论（罗素、维特根斯坦、卡尔纳普、克里普克）全部从这里出发。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：弗雷格说「晨星」和「暮星」是同一颗星（金星），但意思不一样——一个词除了「指什么」还有「怎么指」，语言靠这层「怎么指」才有信息量。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像「你的妈妈」和「你爸爸的妻子」是同一个人——两个说法指向同一人，但一个是「从你出发」的指法，一个是「从你爸爸出发」的指法。
coreThoughts.l3: 涵义（Sinn）/指称（Bedeutung）：Sinn 是「被给予的方式」（mode of presentation），Bedeutung 是对象本身。同名语句的认知价值差异由此解释。弗雷格还区分：命题的指称 = 真值；专名有涵义与指称；「关于涵义的涵义」（引号语境）。此框架是罗素摹状词理论、卡尔纳普内包/外延、克里普克因果命名论的原点。
coreThoughts.descEn: The morning star and evening star: two expressions, one object (Venus), two senses. 'Morning star = evening star' is informative precisely because reference coincides while sense differs. Meaning is not simple word-object correspondence: language reaches the world through the mediating layer of sense. All 20th-century meaning theory — Russell, Wittgenstein, Carnap, Kripke — starts here.
coreThoughts.l1En: 'Morning star' and 'evening star' are one star (Venus) but two meanings — a word has both what it points to and how it points; the 'how' carries information.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like 'your mother' and 'your father's wife': one person, two routes — one via you, one via your father.
coreThoughts.l3En: Sense is the mode of presentation; reference the object. Informative identity statements explained. Proposition's reference = truth value; sense/reference for names; oblique contexts. The origin of Russell's theory of descriptions, Carnap's intension/extension, Kripke's causal theory of naming.

famousEvents.title: 罗素悖论来信
famousEvents.desc: 罗素致信弗雷格，指出其《算术基本法则》体系中的矛盾（罗素悖论）。弗雷格立即回信：「你的发现使我喜出望外，它摧毁的不仅是我的算术基础，恐怕还有全部逻辑。」他在第二卷补遗中承认失败——这是 20 世纪数学基础论最著名的时刻之一。
famousEvents.descEn: Russell wrote to Frege exposing the contradiction in his system. Frege replied immediately: 'Your discovery has delighted me — it destroys not only my arithmetic foundation but, I fear, all of logic.' His published appendix admitted defeat — one of the most famous moments in 20th-century foundations of mathematics.

famousEvents.title: 被忽视的一生
famousEvents.desc: 弗雷格 1918 年退休后回到乡村，孤身一人（妻子早逝、无子女），继续写作却几乎无人问津。《概念文字》出版后十年只卖出寥寥数册；晚年他一度觉得自己一生的劳作「毫无用处」。直到 1950 年代，他的全集才被系统整理出版——「一位天才为未来准备的礼物」。
famousEvents.descEn: Retired to his village in 1918, alone (wife dead, no children), he wrote on largely unread. Begriffsschrift sold only a few copies in ten years; late in life he feared his life's work was 'useless'. Only in the 1950s was his corpus systematically edited — 'a genius's gift prepared for the future'.

philosophers.scientificEval: 弗雷格是「逻辑学中的欧几里得」：他发明的量化逻辑是现代逻辑的基准框架，也是计算机科学（类型论、程序语义、形式验证）、语言学（形式语义学、蒙塔古语法）与数学基础（公理集合论、证明论）的公共语言。其「函数-自变元」分析与「语境原则」被 20 世纪分析哲学全面继承。计算机科学家、逻辑学家与语言学家至今仍在他的概念上工作——几乎每一门形式科学都欠他一份工钱。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: Frege is the Euclid of logic: his quantification theory is the benchmark framework of modern logic and the common language of computer science (type theory, program semantics, formal verification), linguistics (formal semantics, Montague grammar), and the foundations of mathematics (axiomatic set theory, proof theory). His function-argument analysis and context principle were inherited wholesale by analytic philosophy. Nearly every formal science works on his concepts today.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 弗雷格的学术生涯分三段：早年（1873-1879）以数学博士身份转向逻辑基础，写出《概念文字》；中年（1884-1903）实施逻辑主义计划，《算术基础》《算术基本法则》相继问世，同时产出语言哲学三篇名文（《论概念与对象》《论涵义与指称》1892）；晚年（1903-1925）在罗素悖论之后转向「逻辑」概念的重新检讨与后期未刊论文（《思想》《否定》等，为其「逻辑对象」与意义理论做最后的辩护）。他的一生是典型的「完成者的孤独」：每一个伟大的发现都超前于时代，又都被时代遗忘，直到时代终于追上来。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: Three phases: early (1873-79) from mathematics doctorate to logical foundations, the Begriffsschrift; middle (1884-1903) the logicist program (Foundations, Basic Laws) plus the three great language papers (1892); late (1903-25) after the paradox, rethinking logic and meaning in unpublished essays (Thought, Negation). A life of the finisher's solitude: every great discovery ahead of its time, forgotten, until the time finally caught up.
philosophers.aiReview: 弗雷格是「思想家的思想家」——他发明了让其他思想家得以思考的工具。如果不理解他的量词逻辑，你无法真正读懂罗素、维特根斯坦、卡尔纳普乃至今天任何一篇形式语义学论文；他的涵义/指称区分至今仍是语言哲学第一课。他的一生是一个关于「超前」的悲剧：最聪明的人往往等不到自己的时代。罗素悖论击碎了他的体系，但那恰恰证明了另一件事——他的体系足够精确，精确到能被证明是错的。模糊的思想不会出错，只会被遗忘。弗雷格的思想精确到足以出错，这是对他最高的赞美。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Frege is the thinker's thinker — he invented the tools that let other thinkers think. Without his quantifier logic you cannot truly read Russell, Wittgenstein, Carnap, or any formal-semantics paper today; his sense/reference distinction remains the first lesson of philosophy of language. His life is a tragedy of being ahead: the cleverest often wait in vain for their time. Russell's paradox shattered his system — which proves precisely that it was precise enough to be shown wrong. Vague thoughts make no errors; they are only forgotten. Frege's thought was precise enough to err: the highest praise.

philosophers.anecdote: 弗雷格晚年曾给一位年轻的英国学生（维特根斯坦）寄去自己刚出版的《算术基本法则》第一卷，维特根斯坦读后致信说「您的著作让我爱不释手」，弗雷格回信时却抱怨说「您太客气了，大多数人连第一页都读不下去」。据罗素回忆，他在与弗雷格通信前甚至没听说过这个名字——但正是这位「没听说过的人」，改变了他和整个哲学的未来。
philosophers.anecdoteEn: Late in life Frege sent his newly printed Basic Laws vol. 1 to a young English student, Wittgenstein, who wrote that he was 'enthralled'; Frege complained in reply: 'You are too kind — most people cannot get past page one.' Russell recalled never having heard the name before their correspondence — yet this unheard-of man changed his future and philosophy's.
