philosophers.name: 阿伯拉尔
philosophers.role: 中世纪辩证法大师，唯名论先驱，理性与信仰之争的主角
philosophers.summary: 12 世纪法国最耀眼也最悲剧的哲学家：布列塔尼贵族出身，因超凡辩才名动巴黎，「阿伯拉尔 vs 香浦的威廉」「阿伯拉尔 vs 安瑟伦信徒」的公开辩论场场爆满。他确立「理解为了信仰」（与安瑟伦相反）的立场，主张用辩证法检验教义；提出「概念论」的共相观；还以《伦理学》分析「意向」在道德中的核心地位。他与爱洛伊丝的爱情悲剧（师生恋、私生子、被阉割、双双出家）成为中世纪最著名的罗曼史。晚年被指控异端，著作被焚，流放中去世——「中世纪第一个现代知识分子」。
philosophers.summaryEn: The most dazzling and tragic philosopher of 12th-century France: a Breton noble with unmatched dialectical brilliance, his public debates (vs. William of Champeaux, vs. Anselm's disciples) packed Paris. He inverted Anselm — understanding in order to believe — testing dogma with dialectic; held a 'conceptualist' view of universals; and made intention central to ethics. His love tragedy with Héloïse (teacher-student, secret child, castration, double monastic vows) is the Middle Ages' most famous romance. Condemned for heresy in old age, works burned, he died in exile — 'the Middle Ages' first modern intellectual'.

representativeWorks.title: 《是与否》
representativeWorks.content: 158 个神学问题，每个问题下列出教父们互相矛盾的言论——不是亵渎，而是证明：信仰也必须经得起辩证法的检验。这部「矛盾清单」是中世纪理性主义的宣言书，也是经院方法（quaestio）的原型。
representativeWorks.contentEn: 158 theological questions, each listing contradictory patristic sayings — not blasphemy but proof that faith too must pass dialectical scrutiny. The manifesto of medieval rationalism and the prototype of the scholastic quaestio.

representativeWorks.title: 《伦理学》（认识你自己）
representativeWorks.content: 中世纪第一部系统伦理学：道德判断的核心不是行为本身，而是「意向」（intentio）——「罪不在于做了什么事，而在于对那事的同意」。这个意向论伦理学比阿奎那早一百年触及「道德主体性」问题。
representativeWorks.contentEn: The first systematic ethics of the Middle Ages: the core of moral judgment is not the act but the intention — 'sin consists not in what is done, but in consent to it.' His intentionalism touches moral subjectivity a century before Aquinas.

coreThoughts.desc: 阿伯拉尔对安瑟伦「信仰寻求理解」的倒转：不是先信后理解，而是先理解后信——「只有理解了才能相信」（intellectum ut credam）。他并不否定信仰，而是坚持：信仰的对象也必须在理性面前经受检验，经不起检验的「信仰」只是盲从。这个立场让他成为中世纪最早的系统理性主义者：《是与否》把教父的矛盾言论公开陈列，呼吁用逻辑（辩证法）裁定神学争议。他为「怀疑」正名：「通过怀疑我们开始探究，通过探究我们认识真理。」
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：安瑟伦说「先信再懂」，阿伯拉尔反过来说「先弄懂再信」——盲目的信不是真信，是偷懒。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像学数学：老师让你先背公式再理解（先信后懂），阿伯拉尔说要先搞懂推导再接受公式——不懂就接受，那不是学问是迷信。
coreThoughts.l3: 「理解为了信仰」（intellectum ut credam）与安瑟伦「信仰寻求理解」（fides quaerens intellectum）构成中世纪认识论的两极。阿伯拉尔名言：「通过怀疑我们探究，通过探究我们认识真理。」（Dubitando enim ad inquisitionem venimus; inquirendo veritatem percipimus）——被视为笛卡尔式方法论的遥远先声。
coreThoughts.descEn: The inversion of Anselm: not believe-then-understand but understand-then-believe — intellectum ut credam. He does not deny faith but insists its objects must face rational scrutiny; unexamined faith is mere credulity. The first systematic rationalist of the Middle Ages: Sic et Non displays contradictory patristic sayings, urging dialectic to adjudicate theology. He rehabilitates doubt: 'by doubting we come to inquiry; by inquiry we perceive truth.'
coreThoughts.l1En: Anselm says believe first, then understand; Abelard says understand first, then believe — blind belief is not faith but laziness.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like math: a teacher makes you memorize formulas before understanding (believe first); Abelard says understand the derivation before accepting the formula.
coreThoughts.l3En: Intellectum ut credam vs fides quaerens intellectum: the two poles of medieval epistemology. 'By doubting we come to inquiry; by inquiry we perceive truth' — read as a distant prelude to Cartesian method.

coreThoughts.desc: 阿伯拉尔《伦理学》的洞见：上帝审判的不是行为的外在结果，而是行为者的内在意向。同样的行为（如杀死一个人），可能是谋杀、可能是误杀、可能是正当防卫——道德性质完全取决于意向。他甚至提出著名的例子：迫害基督的刽子手在「不知情」中行事，其罪过不同于明知故犯。这个「意向论」（intentionalism）把道德的重心从「做了什么」移到「为什么做」，是西方伦理史上对「道德主体性」最早的系统论述之一——它预告了后来康德「善良意志」的方向。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：阿伯拉尔说「做没做」不是关键，「心里怎么想」才是——同样杀一个人，谋杀和正当防卫的道德完全不同。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像医生给病人用药：同样的药，救人时是善、害人时是恶——差别不在药（行为），在医生的心（意向）。
coreThoughts.l3: 意向论（intentionalism）：罪 = 对恶行的「同意」（consensus）。阿伯拉尔区分行为（actus）与同意（consensus），强调无意的行为无罪。此说引发同时代神学家的反弹（彼得·隆巴德《箴言录》反驳之），但其「道德判断应关注意向」的洞见后经奥卡姆、至康德《道德形而上学奠基》的「善良意志」而成为近代义务论的核心。
coreThoughts.descEn: God judges not the outward act but the inward intention: the same act (killing a man) is murder, manslaughter, or self-defense depending entirely on intention. Even the persecutor of Christ, acting in ignorance, sins less than the knowing wrongdoer. This intentionalism moves morality from 'what was done' to 'why' — an early systematic account of moral subjectivity, prefiguring Kant's good will.
coreThoughts.l1En: What you did isn't the point; what you meant is — killing is murder, accident, or defense depending on intention.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a doctor's prescription: the same drug saves or kills — the difference is not the drug (the act) but the doctor's intent.
coreThoughts.l3En: Sin = consent to evil. He distinguishes the act from consent; unintentional acts are not sinful. His critics (Peter Lombard) pushed back, but intention-centered morality flows through Ockham to Kant's good will and modern deontology.

famousEvents.title: 与爱洛伊丝的爱情悲剧
famousEvents.desc: 阿伯拉尔任巴黎圣母院学院教师时，与神学家富尔贝尔的侄女爱洛伊丝相恋并秘密结婚。富尔贝尔雇人阉割了阿伯拉尔，两人被迫双双出家——爱洛伊丝的信件成为中世纪最深刻的情书与神学对话。
famousEvents.descEn: Teaching at Notre-Dame, he loved and secretly married Héloïse, niece of Canon Fulbert; Fulbert had him castrated. Both entered monasteries — her letters became the Middle Ages' deepest love-letters and theological dialogue.

famousEvents.title: 桑斯会议：异端审判
famousEvents.desc: 经伯尔纳·克莱沃（明谷的伯尔纳）策划，桑斯宗教会议将阿伯拉尔的命题（三位一体的辩证法分析等）定为异端。他上诉罗马未果，著作被焚，流放至克吕尼修道院，在伯尔纳的政敌保护下度过余生。
famousEvents.descEn: Orchestrated by Bernard of Clairvaux, the 1141 council condemned Abelard's theses (including his dialectical analysis of the Trinity). His appeal to Rome failed, books were burned, and he died in exile at Cluny under the protection of Bernard's opponents.

philosophers.scientificEval: 阿伯拉尔对中世纪学术制度的影响深远：他的论辩教学（公开辩论、矛盾裁定）直接塑造了经院方法（quaestio-disputatio），为后来的大学体系（巴黎大学的前身巴黎圣母院学派）奠定教学模式。他对「共相问题」的概念论立场（共相存在于心灵中但基于实在的相似性）为唯名论与实在论的争论提供了中间方案。其意向论伦理学被当代道德心理学（意图在道德判断中的作用实验）重新关注。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: Abelard shaped medieval academic institutions: his public disputation became the scholastic method (quaestio-disputatio) and the teaching model of the university (the Paris school). His conceptualism on universals (universals in the mind, grounded in real similarities) offered the middle path between nominalism and realism. Contemporary moral psychology on the role of intention echoes his ethics.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 阿伯拉尔的轨迹是「天才的自我毁灭与重建」：早年以辩才征服巴黎学界（曾让老师香浦的威廉颜面扫地）；1118 年与爱洛伊丝的悲剧让他转向伦理学与忏悔（《伦理学》）；此后他反复在荣誉与打击间沉浮——《是与否》被焚后仍坚持写作，桑斯会议定罪后仍在克吕尼讲学。他的一生论证了一个命题：在中世纪，理性与制度权威的冲突没有赢家，但理性本身不会因此停止提问。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: His arc: genius's self-destruction and rebuilding — early dialectical conquest of Paris (humbling his teacher William); the Héloïse tragedy (1118) turning him to ethics; perpetual oscillation between fame and condemnation — books burned, condemned at Sens, yet still lecturing at Cluny. His life proves: in the Middle Ages, reason vs institutional authority had no winner — but reason never stopped asking.
philosophers.aiReview: 阿伯拉尔是「天才与制度冲突」的千年标本：他的每一次胜利（辩论、著作、爱情）都招来更重的打击，直到被烧书、定罪、流放。他错了吗？他质疑三位一体的表述确实越界，但他为「怀疑」和「理性检验」正名本身没有错——没有他和伯尔纳的冲突，就不会有后来阿奎那「哲学与神学分工」的成熟解决方案。他的爱情故事常被拍成传奇，但他的思想遗产更值得记住：一个在 12 世纪就坚持「信仰必须经过理性检验」的人，一个把道德判断的重心从行为移到心意的人——这两点都让他比他的时代早了几百年。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Abelard is the millennium's specimen of genius vs institution: every victory (debates, works, love) drew heavier blows, ending in burned books, condemnation, exile. Was he wrong? His Trinitarian formulations overstepped; but vindicating doubt and rational scrutiny was right — without his clash with Bernard, Aquinas' mature division of philosophy and theology would not exist. His romance is legend; his intellectual legacy matters more: insisting in the 12th century that faith face reason, and moving moral judgment from act to intention — both centuries ahead of his time.

philosophers.anecdote: 阿伯拉尔与爱洛伊丝葬在一起。传说他们的遗骸被多次迁徙，最后一次在拉雪兹神父公墓合葬——墓碑上是两人相拥的雕像。每次迁葬，人们都会打开棺椁，发现两人的遗骨仍然并排躺着。这对被世俗拆散的爱人，在死后八百年里不断被重新合葬——现代人把他们当作「真爱」的象征，而他们自己留下的，是更深刻的东西：爱洛伊丝在信中对阿伯拉尔说，「上帝知道，我寻求的不是你的身体，而是你的灵魂」。
philosophers.anecdoteEn: Abelard and Héloïse are buried together. Legend says their remains were moved repeatedly, finally side by side at Père Lachaise under embracing statues; each reburial found their bones still aligned. The lovers separated by the world have been continually reunited in death — moderns take them as true love's symbol; they themselves left something deeper: 'God knows,' Héloïse wrote, 'I sought not your body but your soul.'

philosophers.name: 托马斯·莫尔
philosophers.role: 《乌托邦》作者，人文主义者，殉道的政治家
philosophers.summary: 英国文艺复兴人文主义的代表，亨利八世的大法官——一个把「理想国」写进小说、又把理想活进现实的罕见人物。他的《乌托邦》（1516）创造了「乌托邦」（Utopia，无何有之乡）一词，描绘了一个废除私有制、实行公有制、人人劳动、宗教宽容的理想社会——既是讽刺当时英国圈地运动与穷困的批判书，也是社会主义思想的最早蓝图。他与亨利八世决裂（拒绝承认国王为教会最高首脑），1535 年以叛国罪被处决。他死后四百年被天主教会封圣——「一个为良心而死的人」。
philosophers.summaryEn: The representative of English Renaissance humanism and Henry VIII's Lord Chancellor — rare in writing the ideal republic into a novel and living an ideal into reality. His Utopia (1516) coined the word: a society without private property, with common labor and religious toleration — satire of English enclosures and poverty, and socialism's earliest blueprint. He broke with Henry VIII over the royal supremacy and was executed for treason in 1535; canonized four centuries later — a man who died for conscience.

representativeWorks.title: 《乌托邦》
representativeWorks.content: 以拉斐尔·希斯拉德航海见闻的形式描绘「无何有之乡」：废除私有财产、六小时工作制、全民教育、宗教宽容、选举制官员。第一部分的对话尖锐批判英国圈地运动——「羊吃人」。政治哲学的永恒经典与社会主义思想的源头之一。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Raphael Hythloday's traveler's tale of 'nowhere': no private property, six-hour workdays, universal education, religious toleration, elected officials. Part I's dialogue savages English enclosure — 'sheep that eat men'. A permanent classic of political philosophy and a fountainhead of socialist thought.

representativeWorks.title: 《理查三世史》
representativeWorks.content: 用拉丁文写作的英国历史，是莎士比亚《理查三世》的直接素材。莫尔以人文主义史学家的眼光描绘暴君的形象，此书的叙述艺术被后世史家推崇。
representativeWorks.titleEn: The History of King Richard III
representativeWorks.contentEn: Latin history of England, the direct source of Shakespeare's Richard III. More's portrait of the tyrant is a masterpiece of humanist historiography.

coreThoughts.concept: 乌托邦：理想社会的蓝图
coreThoughts.desc: 《乌托邦》的伟大不在于描绘了一个完美社会，而在于它提出了一种新的思考方式：把「理想社会应该是什么样」当作一个可以认真设计的问题。莫尔的方案：废除私有制（私有制是罪恶与不平等的根源）、公有制生产、按需分配、六小时工作、全民教育与医疗、宗教宽容、官员民选、战争为最后手段。其中许多设计（教育平等、宗教宽容、人道刑罚）在 16 世纪是惊人的超前。乌托邦的反面是当时的英国：圈地运动让农民失去土地——「你们的羊，一向那么温顺，如今却变得如此贪婪凶残，以至于开始吃人了」。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：莫尔画了一张「理想社会」的设计图：没有私有财产、人人劳动六小时、教育医疗免费、信仰自由——并拿它对比当时「羊吃人」的英国。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像先画理想房子的图纸再对比老破屋：图纸（乌托邦）不是为了立刻住进去，而是为了让你知道现在的房子差在哪、值得往哪改。
coreThoughts.l3: 乌托邦（Utopia）= ou（无）+ topos（地方）=「无何有之乡」，兼有「好地方」（eutopia）的双关。思想史意义：①社会主义/公有制的第一个系统蓝图（马克思、恩格斯的直接先驱）；②「乌托邦主义」批判的靶子（「乌托邦」后来成为空想的代名词——但莫尔本人清醒地区分理想与方案）；③西方反乌托邦文学（《1984》《美丽新世界》）的潜在对话对象。
coreThoughts.conceptEn: Utopia: Blueprint of the Ideal Society
coreThoughts.descEn: Utopia's greatness: not a perfect society depicted, but a new way of thinking — that 'what should an ideal society be' is a serious design question. More's plan: abolish private property (root of vice and inequality), common production, distribution by need, six-hour days, universal education and healthcare, religious toleration, elected officials, war as last resort. Many designs were astonishingly ahead of 1516. The mirror: enclosure England — 'your sheep, once so meek, have become so greedy and fierce as to devour men.'
coreThoughts.l1En: More drew a blueprint of the ideal society: no private property, six-hour workdays, free education and healthcare, freedom of belief — contrasted with the sheep-eating England of his day.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like drawing the blueprint of an ideal house to compare with a crumbling one: the blueprint isn't for moving in tomorrow, it shows where the old house fails and where to improve.
coreThoughts.l3En: Utopia (ou+topos, 'nowhere', punning on eutopia) — the first systematic blueprint of common ownership (direct precursor of Marx and Engels), the target of later 'utopianism' critique, and the hidden dialogue partner of dystopian literature (1984, Brave New World).

coreThoughts.desc: 莫尔之死的哲学意义：当世俗权力与个人良心冲突时，谁说了算？亨利八世要求全体臣民宣誓承认国王为教会最高首脑，莫尔拒绝——不是因为他反对改革本身，而是因为他不能违背自己对「教会合一」的信念。他宁可死也不在违背良心的誓词上签字。他临终名言：「我是国王的忠实仆人，但首先是上帝的仆人。」这不是宗教狂热，而是对「权力边界」的声明：国家可以要求公民服从法律，但不能要求公民放弃良心——这个原则后来成为公民不服从理论与良心自由的法律基础。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：国王逼他签字违背良心，他宁可掉脑袋也不签——莫尔说：国家的权力管得到我的行为，管不到我的良心。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像合同：你可以强迫我履行合同（法律），但不能强迫我相信这合同是公正的（良心）——莫尔为「良心不签字」付出了生命。
coreThoughts.l3: 莫尔的良心论：行为可被强迫，同意（consent）不可被强迫。他区分「法律义务」与「道德义务」，认为违背良心的宣誓无效。此立场被后世承继：洛克《论宗教宽容》、梭罗《公民不服从》、罗尔斯《正义论》中的公民不服从理论、以及现代「良心拒服兵役」制度——都可视为莫尔遗产的制度化。
coreThoughts.descEn: The philosophical meaning of More's death: when secular power clashes with personal conscience, who decides? Henry VIII demanded an oath of royal supremacy; More refused — not from anti-reform conviction but because he could not swear against his belief in church unity. He chose death over a conscience-violating oath: 'the king's good servant, but God's first.' Not religious zeal but a statement of power's limits: the state may command obedience to law, but cannot command the surrender of conscience — the root of civil disobedience and freedom of conscience.
coreThoughts.l1En: The king forced an oath against his conscience; he chose death over signing. State power governs my acts, not my conscience.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a contract: you can force performance (law), not belief in its justice (conscience) — More died for not signing with his conscience.
coreThoughts.l3En: Acts may be compelled, consent may not. He distinguishes legal from moral duty; an oath against conscience is void. His legacy institutionalized: Locke's toleration, Thoreau's civil disobedience, Rawls' civil disobedience theory, conscientious objection — all heirs of More.

famousEvents.title: 《乌托邦》的出版
famousEvents.desc: 《乌托邦》在鲁汶出版（莫尔 38 岁），立即成为欧洲人文主义者的必读书。伊拉斯谟称它是「值得放在柏拉图的《理想国》旁边的书」——一个词「乌托邦」从此进入所有欧洲语言。
famousEvents.descEn: Published at Louvain in 1516 (More at 38), it became the humanists' must-read. Erasmus called it worthy to sit beside Plato's Republic — the word 'utopia' entered every European language.

famousEvents.title: 与亨利八世的决裂与殉道
famousEvents.desc: 亨利八世离婚案后，莫尔辞去大法官，拒绝宣誓承认国王为教会最高首脑，被囚伦敦塔十五个月后以叛国罪处决。行刑前他说：「我在国王的臣仆中死得其所，但首先是上帝的仆人。」临刑玩笑：「请帮我上去，下来我自己来。」
famousEvents.descEn: After the divorce, More resigned the chancellorship, refused the oath of royal supremacy, was imprisoned in the Tower for fifteen months and executed for treason in 1535. On the scaffold: 'the king's good servant, but God's first.' His last joke: 'See me safe up; for my coming down I can shift for myself.'

philosophers.scientificEval: 《乌托邦》的社会设计（公有制、按需分配、全民教育、六小时工作日）被视为社会主义思想史上第一个系统文本，马克思、恩格斯在《共产党宣言》中明确将其列入「批判的空想的社会主义」谱系。其「羊吃人」的圈地批判是政治经济学对资本原始积累最早的文学控诉。当代「乌托邦/反乌托邦」研究、理想社会实验（合作社、基布兹）以及「设计社会」的讨论都从这里出发。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: Utopia's social design is the first systematic text of socialist thought — Marx and Engels placed it in the lineage of critical-utopian socialism in the Communist Manifesto. The 'sheep eat men' passage is among the earliest literary indictments of primitive accumulation. Contemporary utopia/dystopia studies, intentional communities, and 'designing society' discussions all start here.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 莫尔的轨迹是「人文主义者→政治家→殉道者」的三幕剧：早年作为伦敦律师与人文主义者，与伊拉斯谟共同翻译希腊经典、批判教会腐败；中年受亨利八世赏识，从下议院议长升至大法官（1529），此时《乌托邦》已为他赢得全欧声誉；1532 年因国王离婚案辞职，此后三年从「国事」退入「良心」，直至赴死。他从未改变立场，变的只是权力对他的态度——这本身就是一种哲学。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: Three acts: humanist (London lawyer, co-translating Greek classics with Erasmus, attacking church corruption), politician (Speaker, then Lord Chancellor 1529), martyr (resigned 1532, three years from affairs of state to affairs of conscience, then death). He never changed his position; power's attitude to him changed — that itself is a philosophy.
philosophers.aiReview: 莫尔常被简化为「乌托邦之父」或「殉道圣人」，但这两顶帽子都太小。他是第一个把「理想社会」当作严肃设计课题的人，也是第一个用行动示范「良心高于权力」的人——前者开创了社会主义思想传统，后者开创了公民不服从传统，两者在 16 世纪同一个人身上出现，堪称奇迹。当然，他有他的时代局限：他的乌托邦容忍奴隶制，他的宗教宽容不包括异端——今天的读者不必因此否定他，只需记住：没有完美的乌托邦，只有不断追问「好社会长什么样」的勇气。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: More is usually shrunk into 'father of Utopia' or 'martyr saint' — both too small. He was the first to treat the ideal society as a serious design problem and the first to demonstrate by action that conscience outranks power — the former founding socialism, the latter founding civil disobedience, both in one 16th-century man. His limits: his Utopia tolerates slavery, his toleration excludes heretics. No perfect utopia; only the courage to keep asking what a good society looks like.

furtherReading.desc: 莫尔代表作，社会主义思想源头

philosophers.anecdote: 莫尔以机智闻名朝野，临死也不例外。走上绞刑架时，他对刽子手说：「请务必帮我把头放正，别让我的名誉受损。」（传说还有一版：「我的脖子很短，请瞄准点，别坏了你的手艺。」）行刑前夜他给女儿玛格丽特写信：「明天我将见到上帝——如果我们有缘重逢，记得带一枝花来。」这位写「乌托邦」的人，用玩笑和温柔走完了现实世界的最后一程。
philosophers.anecdoteEn: Famous for wit to the last. On the scaffold he told the executioner: 'Pray, see me safe up, and for my coming down let me shift for myself.' The night before, he wrote his daughter Margaret: 'Tomorrow I shall see God — if we meet again, bring a flower.' The man who wrote Utopia walked the real world's final steps with jokes and tenderness.

philosophers.name: 狄德罗
philosophers.role: 《百科全书》主编，启蒙运动的总设计师
philosophers.summary: 法国启蒙运动的核心人物，主持编纂《百科全书》（28 卷，1751-1772）——人类历史上第一部系统的现代知识总集，也是启蒙运动的「作战机器」：以词条形式把科学、工艺、哲学、宗教批判熔于一炉，把「知识」从教会与王权的垄断中解放出来。他本人是哲学家、小说家、戏剧理论家、艺术批评家，作品之杂与思想之锐使他成为「哲学家中的百科全书」。晚年他写下《拉摩的侄儿》《宿命论者雅克》等哲理小说，超前地触及唯物主义、生理决定论与辩证法的主题，被马克思称为「辩证法的精神之父」。
philosophers.summaryEn: The organizing mind of the French Enlightenment, editor of the Encyclopédie (28 volumes, 1751-72) — history's first systematic modern compendium of knowledge and the Enlightenment's war machine, liberating knowledge from church and crown. Philosopher, novelist, dramatist, art critic — his range and edge made him the encyclopedia among philosophers. Late works (Rameau's Nephew, Jacques the Fatalist) prefigure materialism, physiological determinism, and dialectics; Marx called him the spiritual father of dialectics.

representativeWorks.title: 《百科全书》（主编）
representativeWorks.content: 28 卷 71818 个词条，历时 21 年完成。以字母顺序组织人类全部知识，把工艺与技术（plate 卷）与哲学、宗教批判并列。伏尔泰、孟德斯鸠、卢梭、达朗贝尔均参与撰稿。启蒙运动的标志性工程。
representativeWorks.contentEn: 28 volumes, 71,818 articles, completed over 21 years. Alphabetically organized all human knowledge, putting crafts and technology beside philosophy and religious critique; Voltaire, Montesquieu, Rousseau, and d'Alembert contributed. The signature project of the Enlightenment.

representativeWorks.title: 《拉摩的侄儿》
representativeWorks.content: 对话体哲理小说：「我」与天才音乐家拉摩的侄儿对谈——一个愤世嫉俗的寄生虫用冷酷的逻辑剖析社会与道德的虚伪。马克思与黑格尔都为之着迷，黑格尔在《精神现象学》中称之为「分裂意识的杰作」。
representativeWorks.contentEn: A philosophical dialogue: 'I' converses with the nephew of composer Rameau, a cynical parasite dissecting society's and morality's hypocrisy with cold logic. Marx and Hegel were fascinated; Hegel called it 'the masterpiece of the divided consciousness' in the Phenomenology.

representativeWorks.title: 《宿命论者雅克》
representativeWorks.content: 雅克与主人的旅行故事：雅克相信「一切皆为命定」，却在行动中不断自由选择——以戏谑的方式讨论决定论与自由意志。「天上写着……」成为书中的口头禅，也是 18 世纪决定论争论的小说化表达。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Jacques and his master travel, Jacques professing 'all is written above' while freely choosing at every turn — a playful treatment of determinism and free will. A novelized 18th-century debate on fatalism.

coreThoughts.desc: 狄德罗的百科全书不是一部辞书，而是一场认识论革命：知识不是神的启示的注脚，而是人通过感官、经验与技艺积累的成果；「知识树」的根不是神学而是「理解力」本身。他坚持把「工艺」（工匠的技艺）与「哲学」并列词条——因为知识的价值在于改善生活，而工匠正是知识作用于生活的通道。他还坚持词条之间的「参照」（renvoi）体系：让读者自己沿着线索发现教条之间的矛盾——一种文本层面的解构。《百科全书》因此既是知识的集大成，也是权威的掘墓人。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：狄德罗说知识不是神给的，是人用眼睛、双手和头脑攒出来的——他让工匠的手艺和哲学家的思想写进同一本书。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像把全城所有的菜谱、地图、配方、传说装进一个大柜子，还配了索引——狄德罗给全人类的知识做了一个「总柜子」，从此谁都能查、谁都能质疑。
coreThoughts.l3: 《百科全书》的知识树（système figuré des connaissances humaines）以「理解力」（entendement）为根，分记忆/理性/想象三枝——取代了以神学为根的传统分类。参照系统（renvoi）让词条互相指涉、暴露矛盾（如「权威」词条下让读者自见其虚）。理念史意义：知识民主化（education for all）、世俗化、以及「技术作为知识」的现代观念。
coreThoughts.descEn: The Encyclopédie is not a dictionary but an epistemological revolution: knowledge is humanity's accumulation through senses, experience, and craft, not a footnote to revelation; the tree of knowledge roots in understanding, not theology. He placed artisan crafts beside philosophy — knowledge's value is improving life, and artisans are knowledge's conduit to life. The cross-reference (renvoi) system let readers trace contradictions among dogmas — a textual deconstruction. Compendium and grave-digger of authority at once.
coreThoughts.l1En: Knowledge isn't given by God but accumulated by human eyes, hands, and minds — Diderot put craftsmen's skills in the same book as philosophers' ideas.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like collecting every recipe, map, formula, and legend of a city into one indexed cabinet: humanity's knowledge got a master cabinet anyone could consult — and question.
coreThoughts.l3En: The tree of knowledge roots in understanding (memory/reason/imagination), replacing theology as root. The renvoi system lets articles cross-reference and expose contradictions. Historical import: democratization of knowledge, secularization, and craft as knowledge.

coreThoughts.desc: 狄德罗的《达朗贝尔之梦》《生理学原理》发展了一套激进的唯物主义：心灵不是独立的实体，而是物质组织（神经系统）的功能；「感觉」是一切认识的基础，而感觉本身是物质运动的结果。他甚至提出「惰性物质可能具有感觉能力」的假说（物活论），并猜测生物是自我组织的物质系统——在没有显微镜和 DNA 的 18 世纪，这几乎是凭思辨预演了生命科学的唯物主义方向。他的唯物论不是冷冰冰的机械论：他承认生命、感受、欲望的丰富性，马克思因此称他为「辩证法的精神之父」——因为他看到对立面（物质与意识、必然与自由）在运动中的统一。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：狄德罗说「人的思想不是天上的火花，是身体这台机器算出来的」——但他不是把人当机器，而是把机器当成了能长出灵魂的东西。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像鸡蛋变鸡：一团「没思想」的物质，在合适的组织下会长出会思考的鸟——狄德罗说人和思想就是这么从物质里长出来的。
coreThoughts.l3: 狄德罗的唯物主义：感觉主义（sensationalism，一切知识源于感觉）→ 物质的功能主义（思想=神经系统的功能）→ 物活论（pansensism：物质可能普遍有感觉能力）→ 自组织的生命观（生物=自我组织系统）。马克思《神圣家族》称其为「辩证法的精神之父」；当代意识哲学（涌现论、物理主义）与其「低阶物质长出新性质」的直觉高度同构。
coreThoughts.descEn: D'Alembert's Dream and Elements of Physiology develop a radical materialism: mind is not a separate substance but a function of organized matter (the nervous system); sensation is the basis of all knowledge and itself a product of material motion. He hypothesized that 'inert matter might have sensation' (pansensism) and that organisms are self-organizing material systems — a speculative rehearsal of the materialist direction of life science before microscopy and DNA. His materialism is not cold mechanism: he affirms life, feeling, desire — why Marx called him the spiritual father of dialectics: opposites (matter and mind, necessity and freedom) unified in motion.
coreThoughts.l1En: Thought is not a spark from heaven but the calculation of the body-machine — yet he didn't reduce man to machine; he saw machines as capable of growing a soul.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like an egg becoming a chicken: 'thoughtless' matter, properly organized, grows a thinking bird — thought grows out of matter.
coreThoughts.l3En: Sensationalism → functionalism (thought as nervous function) → pansensism (matter may feel) → self-organizing life. Marx called him the spiritual father of dialectics. Contemporary emergence-theories of consciousness echo his intuition that higher properties arise from lower matter.

famousEvents.title: 《百科全书》的围攻与坚持
famousEvents.desc: 《百科全书》出版后被教会查禁、耶稣会攻击、政府一度吊销出版许可，达朗贝尔退出主编。狄德罗独自扛下全部编纂工作，在秘密工场里完成了后十卷——「他们把火炬熄了，我就摸黑继续写」。
famousEvents.descEn: Condemned by the Church, attacked by Jesuits, publication license revoked, d'Alembert resigned. Diderot carried the remaining ten volumes alone in secret workshops — 'they put out the torch, so I write on in the dark.'

famousEvents.title: 访问叶卡捷琳娜二世
famousEvents.desc: 俄国女皇叶卡捷琳娜二世买下狄德罗的私人图书馆（并聘他为终身馆员、预付 50 年薪水），邀请他到圣彼得堡。他此行的直言不讳（当面批评女皇的专制）成为启蒙「哲学家-君主」关系的经典场景。
famousEvents.descEn: Catherine II bought Diderot's library (retaining him as lifetime librarian, paying 50 years' salary in advance) and invited him to St. Petersburg; his outspoken criticism of her despotism became the classic scene of Enlightenment philosopher-king relations.

philosophers.scientificEval: 狄德罗的唯物主义与生命观在科学史上有特殊位置：他的「物质可能具有感受性」假说、生物自组织观，被视为 18 世纪「先于实验的生命哲学」代表；其《生理学原理》对感觉与神经系统的思辨性讨论，部分被 19 世纪实验生理学证实。他主持的《百科全书》把工艺技术纳入知识体系，客观上为法国工业革命准备了知识基础设施，也是「技术史」学科的思想源头之一。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: Diderot's materialism holds a special place in the history of science: his pansensism and self-organizing biology represent pre-experimental life-philosophy; Elements of Physiology's speculations on sensation and nerves were partly confirmed by 19th-century experimental physiology. His Encyclopédie put technology into the knowledge system, preparing France's industrial revolution and originating the discipline of history of technology.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 狄德罗的思想经历了「从信仰到怀疑再到唯物主义」的转变：早年是天主教徒与神学生，翻译过沙夫茨伯里（转向自然神论）；1730-1740 年代通过翻译《医学史》与哲学写作转向感觉主义与无神论；1750 年代主持《百科全书》确立其启蒙领袖地位；晚年（1760-1780）写下《拉摩的侄儿》《宿命论者雅克》等，把唯物主义推向「世界是活的、矛盾的、自我运动的」的辩证方向。他的哲学像他的生活一样：没有体系，但处处是思想的火种。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: From faith to doubt to materialism: early Catholic and seminarian, translated Shaftesbury (toward deism); 1730s-40s toward sensationalism and atheism via medical translation and essays; 1750s the Encyclopédie; late years (1760-80) Rameau's Nephew and Jacques the Fatalist pushing materialism toward the living, contradictory, self-moving world. His philosophy like his life: no system, sparks everywhere.
philosophers.aiReview: 狄德罗是启蒙运动里最不像「哲学家」的哲学家——他不写体系，写辞书、小说、对话、剧本、艺术评论，像一台思想的永动机，把一切严肃问题都用最不严肃的形式抛出来。他的《拉摩的侄儿》超前地写出了现代人的分裂意识：清醒地看穿一切虚伪，却依然在虚伪中活着。他作为「辩证法的精神之父」（马克思语）的遗产：在机械唯物论盛行的时代，他坚持物质能长出感觉、感觉能长出思想、对立能走向统一——这个直觉在两百多年后的涌现论、复杂系统科学中重新获得回声。今天读他，仍能感到那个时代的乐观：一个人相信，只要把知识交到每个人手里，世界就会变好。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: The Enlightenment's least philosopher-like philosopher: no systems, but encyclopedias, novels, dialogues, plays, art criticism — a perpetual-motion machine of thought, tossing every serious question in the most unserious forms. Rameau's Nephew wrote the modern divided consciousness in advance: seeing through all hypocrisy while living in it. His dialectical legacy (Marx): in an age of mechanical materialism, insisting matter grows sensation, sensation grows thought, opposites unite in motion — echoed today in emergence theory and complexity science. Reading him still conveys the age's optimism: one man's faith that putting knowledge in everyone's hands will improve the world.

philosophers.anecdote: 狄德罗晚年经济窘迫，靠变卖藏书维持。叶卡捷琳娜二世得知后，出 1.5 万银币买下他的全部藏书，条件是「书留在原地直到他去世」，还聘他为图书馆长、预付了 50 年薪水——用买书的方式包养了哲学家。狄德罗到圣彼得堡后，两人常常争得面红耳赤，女皇后来说：「和他谈话，我的手都要被他捏碎了——但这样的谈话，让我聪明了十年。」
philosophers.anecdoteEn: Late in life, poor, Diderot sold his library; Catherine the Great paid 15,000 silver pieces on condition the books stay with him until death, hiring him as librarian with 50 years' salary in advance — subsidizing a philosopher by buying his books. In St. Petersburg they argued fiercely; the empress said later: 'Talking with him, my hands were nearly crushed — but such conversation made me ten years wiser.'

philosophers.name: 亚当·斯密
philosophers.role: 现代经济学之父，《国富论》作者
philosophers.summary: 苏格兰启蒙运动的巨人，「现代经济学之父」。他的《国富论》（1776）第一次系统论证了市场经济如何通过「看不见的手」协调千百万人的自利行为——分工、竞争、自由贸易构成财富增长的机制；而他的另一部巨著《道德情操论》（1759）则论证了人性中的「同情」如何构成道德的基础。两本书合起来是一个完整的「斯密问题」：自利与同情如何共存于同一人性？他终身未婚、心不在焉、以「最伟大的道德哲学家和自利经济学的开创者」的双重身份影响了两个世纪——马克思从分工说起，凯恩斯从需求说起，都从《国富论》出发。
philosophers.summaryEn: Giant of the Scottish Enlightenment, father of modern economics. The Wealth of Nations (1776) first systematically showed how the 'invisible hand' coordinates millions of self-interested acts — division of labor, competition, free trade — while the Theory of Moral Sentiments (1759) grounded morality in human sympathy. Together they pose 'the Adam Smith problem': how do self-interest and sympathy coexist in one nature? Unmarried, absent-minded, he shaped two centuries — Marx starting from division of labor, Keynes from demand, both from the Wealth of Nations.

representativeWorks.title: 《道德情操论》
representativeWorks.content: 道德哲学巨著：道德判断的根源是「同情」（sympathy）——我们通过想象把自己放进他人的处境来感受其感受，并由「公正的旁观者」视角形成道德评判。自我控制、正义感、仁慈皆由此生长。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Moral philosophy: moral judgment roots in sympathy — we imagine ourselves into others' situations and judge from the 'impartial spectator' standpoint. Self-command, the sense of justice, and benevolence all grow from this.

representativeWorks.title: 《国富论》
representativeWorks.content: 五卷本经济学奠基作：劳动分工是财富增长的源泉；「看不见的手」——个人追求私利时被引导去促进公共福利；自由市场、自由贸易与有限政府。与《独立宣言》同年出版，被称为「政治经济学圣经」。
representativeWorks.titleEn: An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations
representativeWorks.contentEn: Five books founding economics: division of labor as the source of wealth; the 'invisible hand' — individuals pursuing self-interest are led to promote the public good; free markets, free trade, limited government. Published in the same year as the Declaration of Independence; the bible of political economy.

coreThoughts.desc: 《国富论》中最著名的意象：面包师、屠夫、酿酒师为我们提供晚餐，靠的不是仁慈而是自利——「我们期待的晚餐不是来自屠夫、酿酒师或面包师的恩惠，而是来自他们对自身利益的关切」。每个人追求自己的利益，仿佛被一只「看不见的手」引导着去实现并非他本意的社会目的：价格机制把无数分散的私人决策协调成整体秩序。斯密并不天真：同一本书里他反复警告商人的垄断倾向、资本家的合谋，并要求政府维持竞争、提供公共品——「看不见的手」是市场奇迹的比喻，不是对市场的盲目崇拜。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：你买面包不是因为面包师爱你，是因为他想赚钱——但大家都为自己的利益努力时，整个社会的财富反而涨了，像有只看不见的手在安排。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像城市交通：没有总调度，每个司机只想着自己怎么最快到家，结果路网大体顺畅——个体自利加在一起，偶然形成了整体秩序。
coreThoughts.l3: 「看不见的手」（invisible hand）在《国富论》第四卷出现（该词最早见于《道德情操论》）。其机制：价格信号 + 竞争 + 激励。注意斯密的三重限定：①必须存在竞争（垄断除外）；②政府需提供国防、司法与公共工程；③商人「合谋抬高价格」是斯密明言的威胁。现代经济学将其形式化为「一般均衡」（瓦尔拉斯、阿罗-德布鲁），也围绕「市场失灵」（外部性、信息不对称）展开批评。
coreThoughts.descEn: The famous image: the baker, butcher, and brewer supply our dinner from self-interest, not benevolence — 'It is not from the benevolence of the butcher, the brewer, or the baker that we expect our dinner, but from their regard to their own interest.' Each pursuing his own interest is led by an invisible hand to promote an end no part of his intention. Not naive: the same book warns of merchants' monopoly, capitalists' collusion, demanding competition and public goods. A metaphor of market miracle, not blind market worship.
coreThoughts.l1En: You get bread not because the baker loves you but because he wants money — yet when everyone pursues self-interest, society's wealth grows, as if an invisible hand arranged it.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like city traffic: no central dispatcher, every driver just wants to get home fastest, yet the network mostly flows — individual self-interest accidentally forms an overall order.
coreThoughts.l3En: The invisible hand (Wealth of Nations IV; first in Moral Sentiments) works via price signals, competition, incentives. Smith's three qualifications: competition must exist (no monopoly); government provides defense, justice, public works; merchants' collusion is an explicit threat. Modern economics formalizes it as general equilibrium and criticizes market failure.

coreThoughts.desc: 《道德情操论》的道德心理学：道德不是理性的计算，也不是神的命令，而是「同情」的产物——我们天生能想象他人的处境，感受他人的感受（看见别人挨打，我们的肌肉会不自觉地收缩）。由此我们学会换位思考，并进一步设想一个「公正的旁观者」如何评判我们的行为：我们据此培养自制、正义与仁爱。「公正的旁观者」内化于心，就是良心的机制。斯密由此把道德建立在人的自然情感之上（道德感学派），又为自利与道德的统一提供了心理学基础——同一个「想象他人」的能力，既让我们能合作（道德），也让我们能交易（经济）。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：斯密说道德不是算出来的，是「感同身受」长出来的——你心疼别人，是因为你能想象他的疼。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像看球赛：球员摔倒，观众会「嘶」地吸一口气——斯密说这种身体反应就是道德的地基：我们天生能共享别人的感受。
coreThoughts.l3: 同情（sympathy）≠ 怜悯（pity）：斯密的 sympathy 是「想象的换位」（imaginative transposition），中性词。公正的旁观者（impartial spectator）：内化的评判者，即良心的运作机制。「斯密问题」（Adam Smith Problem）：《道德情操论》的同情 vs《国富论》的自利——现代学界公认二者并不矛盾（同情的旁观者同样要求自我关切的适度），斯密本人从不认为它们是两个体系。
coreThoughts.descEn: Moral psychology of the Moral Sentiments: morality is neither rational calculation nor divine command but sympathy — we naturally imagine others' situations and feel their feelings (watching someone struck, our muscles flinch). From this we learn perspective-taking, then imagine how an 'impartial spectator' would judge our conduct: self-command, justice, benevolence. The internalized spectator is conscience. Morality rooted in natural sentiment — and the same capacity to imagine others enables both cooperation (morality) and exchange (economy).
coreThoughts.l1En: Morality isn't calculated but grown from empathy — you feel for others because you can imagine their pain.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like watching a game: a player falls, the crowd gasps — that bodily response is morality's foundation: we naturally share others' feelings.
coreThoughts.l3En: Sympathy ≠ pity: Smith's sympathy is imaginative transposition, neutral. The impartial spectator: the internalized judge, the mechanism of conscience. The 'Adam Smith Problem' (sympathy vs self-interest) is now widely seen as false — sympathy's spectator equally endorses due self-regard; Smith never saw two systems.

famousEvents.title: 《国富论》与《独立宣言》同年
famousEvents.desc: 1776 年《国富论》与《独立宣言》同年问世——自由市场与自由国家同时登上历史舞台。斯密后来写道，这两件事是「人类自由的双生子」般的巧合（实为其友人语）。
famousEvents.descEn: The Wealth of Nations and the Declaration of Independence appeared the same year — free markets and free statehood on the stage together; the coincidence was remarked upon by Smith's friends.

famousEvents.title: 格拉斯哥的道德哲学讲席
famousEvents.desc: 斯密 28 岁任格拉斯哥大学逻辑学教授，次年转任道德哲学教授——他的《道德情操论》正是这门课讲义的扩展；而《国富论》则源于其中关于「治安、司法、税收与军备」的讲座。两本书出自同一门课，是「斯密问题」的原始证据。
famousEvents.descEn: At 28 professor of logic, then of moral philosophy at Glasgow — the Moral Sentiments grew from this course; the Wealth of Nations from its lectures on police, justice, revenue, and arms. Two books, one course: the original evidence on the 'Adam Smith Problem'.

philosophers.scientificEval: 《国富论》奠基了政治经济学：劳动价值论（李嘉图、马克思继承）、分工理论（对工业革命的解释框架）、自由放任政策（19 世纪古典自由主义的纲领）。其「看不见的手」被现代经济学形式化为一般均衡理论（阿罗-德布鲁），其市场失灵思想（外部性、公共品）则是福利经济学与政府干预理论的源头。斯密被誉为「经济学三百年里最重要的经济学家」，其方法论（从人性与历史经验出发的归纳）预示了后来的社会科学方法。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: The Wealth of Nations founded political economy: the labor theory of value (Ricardo, Marx), division of labor (the frame for explaining the industrial revolution), laissez-faire (the 19th-century liberal program). The invisible hand was formalized as general equilibrium (Arrow-Debreu); market-failure analysis grounds welfare economics and intervention theory. Arguably the most important economist in three centuries; his inductive method from human nature and history prefigures modern social science.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 斯密的思想发展是一条从道德哲学到政治经济学的连续线：格拉斯哥的道德哲学讲义（1750s）包含《道德情操论》与《国富论》的种子；《道德情操论》（1759）确立同情心理学；1764-1766 年赴法担任贵族导师，结识魁奈、杜尔哥（重农学派），使其经济学视野成熟；《国富论》（1776）完成经济学的独立；晚年修订《道德情操论》第六版（1790，去世前一年）——他始终认为自己首先是道德哲学家。临终前他焚毁了未发表的文稿，留下的两本书足以撑起一个学科。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: A continuous line from moral philosophy to political economy: the Glasgow lectures (1750s) contained both books' seeds; Moral Sentiments (1759) the sympathy psychology; 1764-66 French tutorship meeting Quesnay and Turgot matured his economics; Wealth of Nations (1776); he revised the Moral Sentiments' sixth edition in 1790, the year he died — always a moral philosopher first. He burned unpublished manuscripts on his deathbed; two books sufficed to found a discipline.
philosophers.aiReview: 斯密是那种「被引用最多、被误读也最多」的思想家。他被后世塑造成「自由放任的旗手」，但他本人明确反对商人合谋、支持累进税、关心贫困工人——他的「看不见的手」从来不是「政府别管」的同义词，而是「竞争 + 制度 + 有限政府」的复杂公式。他的另一面常被遗忘：《道德情操论》里的斯密认为人首先是道德存在，经济学只是道德生活的一部分——两本书必须合起来读。今天 AI 时代的算法市场、平台经济再次把「看不见的手 vs 看得见的规则」的问题摆上桌面，斯密两百多年前的告诫依然适用：市场是奇迹，但奇迹需要秩序。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: The most quoted and most misread thinker. Posterity made him the banner of laissez-faire, but he opposed merchant collusion, favored progressive taxation, cared for the working poor — the invisible hand was never 'government hands off' but a complex formula of competition, institutions, and limited state. The forgotten half: in the Moral Sentiments, man is first a moral being; economics is part of moral life — read both books together. In the age of algorithmic markets and platforms, the question of invisible hand vs visible rules returns; his warning still applies: markets are miracles, and miracles need order.

furtherReading.title: 《国富论》（郭大力/王亚南中译本）
furtherReading.desc: 现代经济学奠基作

philosophers.anecdote: 斯密是哲学史上最著名的心不在焉者：据说他在海关税吏任上，一次签字时竟把自己的签名写成了别人的名字；还有一次他穿着睡袍出门散步，走了十五英里才想起自己没换衣服，到家时已在思考中走完了全程。他终身未娶，与母亲同住一生，被格拉斯哥的孩子们称为「那个没结婚的哲学家」。
philosophers.anecdoteEn: Philosophy's most famous absent-minded man: as a customs commissioner he once signed his own name as another's; another time he walked out in his dressing gown, strolled fifteen miles lost in thought, and arrived home having forgotten to change. Unmarried, he lived with his mother all his life, known to Glasgow's children as 'the philosopher who never married.'

philosophers.name: 孔多塞
philosophers.role: 启蒙最后的哲人，进步观念的系统化者
philosophers.summary: 法国大革命时代的数学家、哲学家与社会改革家，启蒙运动最后的代言人。他是概率论（孔多塞投票悖论、陪审团定理）的奠基人，也是「人类进步观念」的系统化者——《人类精神进步史表纲要》把历史读作理性不断战胜偏见的十个阶段，预言未来社会的平等、教育与科技进步。作为吉伦特派成员，他在雅各宾恐怖中被通缉，逃亡中写下这部「进步宣言」，被捕后死于狱中——他用生命证明了进步的道路从来不平坦。
philosophers.summaryEn: Mathematician, philosopher, and social reformer of the French Revolution, the Enlightenment's last voice. Founder of probability applications to society (Condorcet's voting paradox, the jury theorem) and systematizer of the idea of progress — the Sketch for a Historical Picture of the Progress of the Human Mind reads history as reason's ten-stage victory over prejudice, foreseeing equality, universal education, and technological advance. A Girondin proscribed in the Terror, he wrote the 'manifesto of progress' in hiding and died in prison — proving the road of progress was never smooth.

representativeWorks.title: 《人类精神进步史表纲要》
representativeWorks.content: 逃亡中写成的绝笔：人类精神进步的十阶段史表——从部落社会到大革命；未来三个预言：国家间不平等消失、阶级内平等、人的可完善性（教育、科技延长生命）。「进步论」的经典文本，也是法国大革命的哲学遗嘱。
representativeWorks.titleEn: Sketch for a Historical Picture of the Progress of the Human Mind
representativeWorks.contentEn: Written in hiding: the ten-stage table of human progress — from tribal society to the Revolution — plus three future predictions: equality among nations, equality within classes, and human perfectibility (education, science lengthening life). The classic of progress-theory and the French Revolution's philosophical testament.

representativeWorks.title: 《论陪审团裁决的概率》
representativeWorks.content: 孔多塞陪审团定理：每个投票者正确判断的概率大于一半时，多数裁决正确的概率随人数增加趋于 1——用数学证明「众人之智」。现代社会选择理论的奠基文献。
representativeWorks.titleEn: Essay on the Application of Analysis to the Probability of Majority Decisions
representativeWorks.contentEn: The Condorcet jury theorem: if each voter is more likely than not to be right, the probability that majority rule is right approaches 1 as numbers grow — a mathematical proof of the wisdom of crowds. A founding text of modern social choice theory.

coreThoughts.desc: 孔多塞把人类历史划分为十个阶段：从狩猎部落（第一阶段）到法国大革命（第十阶段），每一阶段都是理性与知识对偏见与压迫的推进。历史不是循环（古代史观）也不是神意剧本（中世纪史观），而是「人类精神」可完善的进程——科学每进一步，政治与道德就跟着进步。他进一步预言未来：①国家之间的不平等将消失；②同一国家内的平等（财产、教育）将实现；③人类将趋向「可完善性」——科技进步延长生命、教育普及提升理性。「进步」从此成为现代政治的核心信念，也是后来一切历史乐观主义与历史主义的源头。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：孔多塞说人类的历史是「打怪升级」——每一关（阶段）都是理性打败偏见，最后会通关到一个平等、开明、长命的世界。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像游戏的角色成长：从部落到文明不是循环，而是经验条在涨——孔多塞相信人类这个「角色」的经验条永远在涨。
coreThoughts.l3: 十阶段史表（tableau historique）：第 1-9 阶段为历史描述，第 10 阶段即法国大革命，末尾进入「未来之展望」。进步论（perfectibilism）：人可完善性（perfectibilité）概念。影响：圣西门、孔德（实证主义三阶段）、马克思（历史进步观）、自由主义（渐进改良）——也孕育了后来对「历史进步论」的批判（本雅明「进步的风暴」、波普尔「历史主义」）。
coreThoughts.conceptEn: The Ten Stages of Human Progress
coreThoughts.descEn: History as ten stages from tribal hunting (I) to the French Revolution (X), each a step of reason and knowledge over prejudice and oppression. Not cycle (antiquity) nor providence (medieval) but the perfectibility of the human mind: each scientific advance carries politics and morality forward. Predictions: equality among nations; equality within nations (property, education); perfectibility — science extending life, education spreading reason. 'Progress' became the core modern political belief, the source of all later historical optimism and historicism.
coreThoughts.l1En: History is leveling up: each stage is reason defeating prejudice, ending in an equal, enlightened, long-lived world.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like an RPG: from tribe to civilization is not a cycle but an XP bar rising — Condorcet believed humanity's bar never stops.
coreThoughts.l3En: The tableau historique: stages 1-9 historical, stage 10 the Revolution, then the future prospect. Perfectibility as the human essence. Feeds Saint-Simon, Comte's positivism, Marx's progressivism, liberal gradualism — and later critiques of progress (Benjamin's storm, Popper's historicism).

coreThoughts.concept: 孔多塞悖论与集体理性
coreThoughts.desc: 孔多塞在数学上发现了民主的难题：即使每个选民都理性，简单多数规则也可能产生「循环」——三个选项 A、B、C 中，多数人偏好 A 胜过 B，多数人偏好 B 胜过 C，多数人又偏好 C 胜过 A。这个「孔多塞悖论」说明：集体偏好不等于个体偏好的简单加总，民主的制度设计（投票规则、议程）本身就是政治问题。他同时给出陪审团定理：多数裁决在「每人正确概率>½」时随人数逼近必然正确——同一人既发现集体决策的缺陷，又证明其价值，堪称社会选择理论的奠基者。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：孔多塞发现「投票可能没有赢家」——三个人对三个方案各有偏好时，多数决可能转圈圈，谁都比不过谁。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像石头剪刀布：石头赢剪刀、剪刀赢布、布赢石头——三个方案也能玩出这种「循环」，这时「大多数人的意见」就说不清是谁的意见了。
coreThoughts.l3: 孔多塞悖论（Condorcet paradox）：多数偏好可循环（非传递）。陪审团定理（jury theorem）：P(多数正确) → 1，当个人正确概率 > ½。此两结果开创社会选择理论，后经阿罗不可能定理（1951，诺贝尔奖）系统化——阿罗定理正是孔多塞悖论的严格推广，证明「没有完美的投票规则」。
coreThoughts.descEn: He found democracy's mathematical problem: even rational voters under majority rule can cycle — among A, B, C, majorities prefer A>B, B>C, C>A. Collective preference is not a simple sum of individual preferences; voting rules and agendas are themselves political. Yet he also proved the jury theorem: majority verdict approaches certainty as numbers grow when each person is more likely right than wrong — the same man discovering collective choice's defect and its value: the founder of social choice theory.
coreThoughts.l1En: Voting can have no winner — three voters, three options, and majority rule cycles like rock-paper-scissors.
coreThoughts.l2En: Rock beats scissors, scissors beats paper, paper beats rock — alternatives can cycle too, and then 'the majority's opinion' is no one's opinion.
coreThoughts.l3En: The paradox: majority preference can be intransitive. The jury theorem: majority correctness → 1 if individual accuracy > ½. Both open social choice theory, systematized by Arrow's impossibility theorem (1951, Nobel): no perfect voting rule — the rigorous generalization of Condorcet.

famousEvents.title: 逃亡中的绝笔
famousEvents.desc: 雅各宾派掌权后，孔多塞因反对处死路易十六、反对恐怖统治而被通缉。他在巴黎友人家中躲藏九个月，写下《人类精神进步史表纲要》，书名与内容形成悲壮的对照——为一个相信进步的人，逃亡是进步最好的注脚。
famousEvents.descEn: Proscribed by the Jacobins for opposing the king's execution and the Terror, he hid nine months in a Paris friend's house, writing the Sketch for the Progress of the Human Mind — the title and content forming a tragic contrast: for a believer in progress, flight was the best footnote to progress.

famousEvents.title: 狱中逝世
famousEvents.desc: 1794 年 3 月孔多塞离开藏身处被捕（一说自杀，一说猝死），两天后被发现死在狱中。他死后仅四个月，罗伯斯庇尔倒台，恐怖结束——他最终未能看到自己预言的「进步」在法国降临。
famousEvents.descEn: Leaving hiding in March 1794, he was arrested and found dead in his cell two days later (suicide or sudden death — disputed). Four months later Robespierre fell and the Terror ended — he never saw the progress he predicted arrive in France.

philosophers.scientificEval: 孔多塞的数学贡献具有持久的科学价值：陪审团定理是现代社会选择理论、统计决策论与「群体智慧」研究的基石；孔多塞悖论是阿罗不可能定理的直接前身；他在概率论、积分学（1786 年「孔多塞积分」）上也有贡献。他将概率方法引入社会科学的尝试，被视为「量化社会科学」的源头——尽管 19 世纪的主流转向统计学而非投票理论，但 20 世纪以来其社会选择理论全面复兴（阿罗、森、帕菲特）。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: His mathematics endures: the jury theorem is bedrock of social choice theory, statistical decision theory, and 'wisdom of crowds'; the paradox is Arrow's immediate predecessor; he contributed to probability and integral calculus (the 1786 Condorcet integral). His attempt to bring probability to social science is the origin of quantitative social science — sidelined in the 19th century, fully revived in the 20th (Arrow, Sen, Parfit).
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 孔多塞的轨迹是「数学家走向政治」：早年是科学院数学家（达朗贝尔的学生），把概率论用于陪审团与投票（1785）；大革命爆发后成为共和派（吉伦特），起草公共教育法案（1792），主张全民教育、政教分离、女性权利（他是最早的女性权利倡导者之一）；1793 年恐怖时期转入地下，写下进步史表；1794 年死于狱中。他从数学出发，相信「社会也可以被精确地理解与设计」——这个信念本身，就是启蒙运动最激进也最天真的遗产。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: From mathematician to politician: academician (student of d'Alembert) applying probability to juries and voting (1785); Girondin republican drafting the education bill (1792) for universal education, separation of church and state, and women's rights (an early feminist); underground 1793 writing the Sketch; dead 1794. From mathematics he believed society too could be precisely understood and designed — the Enlightenment's most radical and most naive legacy.
philosophers.aiReview: 孔多塞是一个时代的完美缩影：把数学的精确带给政治（陪审团定理），把理性的乐观带给历史（进步史表），把宽容带给社会（教育法案、女性权利）——然后被不宽容的社会处死。他的悲剧在于：他相信进步是必然的，而他的死恰恰证明进步不是必然的，是需要斗争与守护的。今天重读他，最动人的不是十阶段的宏大叙事（两百年后我们已对「进步」心存戒惧），而是他对「可完善性」的信念：人可以通过教育与制度变得更好——这个信念，无论经历多少挫折，都值得被保留。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Condorcet is his age's perfect mirror: mathematical precision for politics (jury theorem), rational optimism for history (the Sketch), tolerance for society (education, women's rights) — then killed by an intolerant society. His tragedy: he believed progress inevitable, and his death proved it is not inevitable but must be fought for and guarded. Reading him today, the moving part is not the ten-stage narrative (we've grown wary of progress) but the belief in perfectibility: humans can become better through education and institutions — a belief worth keeping through every setback.

philosophers.anecdote: 孔多塞逃亡时躲在巴黎一位朋友家中，房东太太每天给他送饭，只知道他是「一个怕被抓的先生」。九个月里他靠回忆写下《进步史表》（没有一本书可以参考——全靠记忆中的藏书）。被捕入狱后，据说他随身携带的唯一物品是荷马的《伊利亚特》——一个写「进步」的人，在最后时刻读的是「毁灭」。
philosophers.anecdoteEn: In hiding, his landlady fed 'a gentleman afraid of arrest' for nine months; he wrote the Sketch from memory, no library available. In prison his sole possession was said to be Homer's Iliad — a man writing 'progress', reading 'destruction' at the end.

philosophers.name: 伽达默尔
philosophers.role: 哲学诠释学奠基人，《真理与方法》作者
philosophers.summary: 20 世纪最重要的诠释学哲学家，「哲学诠释学」（philosophical hermeneutics）的奠基人。他的《真理与方法》（1960）提出：理解不是中立地「复原作者原意」，而是「视域融合」——带着自己的前见（传统、历史、语言）去与文本对话，在差异中生成新的意义。这本书动摇了近代以来「客观认识」的神话，成为 20 世纪后半叶人文学科（文学、法学、神学、史学）的方法论基石。他活了 102 岁，是 20 世纪哲学的活化石：听过海德格尔、胡塞尔的课，与哈贝马斯论战，见证了现象学、存在主义、分析哲学、后结构主义的兴衰。
philosophers.summaryEn: The most important hermeneutical philosopher of the 20th century, founder of philosophical hermeneutics. Truth and Method (1960) holds that understanding is not neutral recovery of an author's intention but 'fusion of horizons' — dialogue with the text carrying one's own prejudices (tradition, history, language), generating new meaning in difference. It shook the myth of objective knowledge and became the methodological cornerstone of the human sciences. He lived 102 years, a living fossil of 20th-century philosophy: hearing Heidegger and Husserl, debating Habermas, witnessing phenomenology, existentialism, analytic philosophy, and post-structuralism rise and fall.

representativeWorks.title: 《真理与方法》
representativeWorks.content: 哲学诠释学的奠基之作：艺术、历史与语言中的理解经验。核心命题：理解是「视域融合」；「前见」不是理解的障碍而是理解的条件；诠释学循环（整体-部分的循环）是理解的普遍结构。「理解总是不同的理解」——不是更正确，而是不同。
representativeWorks.contentEn: The founding text: understanding as experienced in art, history, and language. Understanding is fusion of horizons; prejudice is not an obstacle but a condition of understanding; the hermeneutic circle is universal. 'Understanding is always different understanding' — not more correct, but different.

representativeWorks.title: 《真理与方法》之后的哲学诠释学论文集
representativeWorks.content: 《科学时代的理性》等论文集：把诠释学从方法扩展到「实践哲学」（phronesis）——理解不仅是文本的技术，更是人的存在方式；诠释学是「实践智慧」的现代形态。
representativeWorks.titleEn: Post-Truth-and-Method Essays (Reason in the Age of Science)
representativeWorks.contentEn: Extending hermeneutics from method to practical philosophy (phronesis): understanding is not textual technique but a way of human being; hermeneutics is the modern form of practical wisdom.

coreThoughts.desc: 伽达默尔对「理解」的重构：传统诠释学以为理解 = 复原作者原意（像考古学家清理壁画）；伽达默尔说理解 = 对话——你带着自己的视域（前见、传统、当下处境）走近文本的视域（历史、作者、当时语境），两个视域相遇、碰撞、交融，产生新的意义。这就是「视域融合」（Horizontverschmelzung）。所以「理解一部古典著作」不是「猜中作者想什么」，而是「让它对我们说话」——同一部《论语》在两千年后的中国人和古希腊人那里产生不同的理解，这不同不是失败，而是意义的生长。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：伽达默尔说理解不是「猜作者原意」，而是「两个世界碰出火花」——你的世界和书的世界对话，产生新的意思。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像和老朋友聊天：你带着自己的经历听他说他的经历，聊完你会发现——你听懂的不是「他原来想说的」，而是「你们的对话里长出来的」。
coreThoughts.l3: 视域（Horizont）= 从某个立场所能看到的一切；前见（Vorurteil）= 理解的先决条件（伽达默尔为其「正名」：前见不是偏见之贬义，而是传统在个体中的沉淀）。视域融合 = 理解事件的结构。此概念重塑了诠释学：施莱尔马赫（复原原意）→ 狄尔泰（生命表达）→ 海德格尔（理解的生存论结构）→ 伽达默尔（理解的普遍性）。
coreThoughts.descEn: Understanding is not recovering an author's original intention (like an archaeologist cleaning a fresco) but dialogue: you approach the text's horizon (history, context) with your own horizon (prejudices, tradition, present situation); the two meet, collide, and fuse into new meaning — Horizontverschmelzung. Understanding a classic is not guessing what the author meant but letting it speak to us; differing interpretations across centuries are not failure but the growth of meaning.
coreThoughts.l1En: Understanding isn't guessing the author's intent; it's two worlds colliding — your world and the book's world conversing into something new.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like talking with an old friend: you hear his story through your own experience, and what you understand is not 'what he meant' but 'what grew in your conversation'.
coreThoughts.l3En: Horizon = all that is visible from a standpoint; prejudice (Vorurteil) = the condition of understanding, rehabilitated as tradition's sedimentation in the individual. Fusion of horizons = the structure of the understanding event. Reshapes hermeneutics: Schleiermacher (recovery) → Dilthey (expression) → Heidegger (existential structure) → Gadamer (universality).

coreThoughts.desc: 启蒙运动以来，「前见」（偏见）与「权威」是理性的敌人；伽达默尔翻转了这一定式：任何理解都从前见开始——你不可能从「白板」出发理解任何东西，前见不是理解的障碍而是理解的起点。同样，「权威」不必然是盲从：真正的权威来自「承认」（有人因其知识或经验被承认），而承认本身就是理性的行为。传统（传统 = 被传递下来的前见）不是理性的对立面，而是理性借以生长的土壤。这个「为前见和权威正名」的立场惊世骇俗，却也深刻：它说明理性主义对「无预设之起点」的追求本身就是一种神话。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：伽达默尔说「你不可能不带任何想法地去理解」——那些你以为要先扔掉的「偏见」，其实正是你理解任何东西的起点。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像戴眼镜：你不戴眼镜看不清，但戴了眼镜看到的也不是「纯客观」——前见就是你那副镜片，关键不是摘掉它，而是知道它存在。
coreThoughts.l3: 伽达默尔对启蒙「反前见之偏见」的批判：启蒙把「无前见」本身变成新偏见。权威（Autorität）= 基于承认而非服从；传统（Überlieferung）= 有效的历史延续。此立场引发与哈贝马斯的著名论战：哈贝马斯认为伽达默尔为传统辩护过头，忽视了权力对传统的塑造——「传统是否也系统性地扭曲沟通？」（批判诠释学 vs 哲学诠释学）。
coreThoughts.conceptEn: The Rehabilitation of Prejudice and Authority
coreThoughts.descEn: Since the Enlightenment, prejudice and authority are reason's enemies; Gadamer inverts: all understanding begins from prejudice — no one understands from a blank slate; prejudice is understanding's starting point, not obstacle. Authority need not be blind obedience: true authority rests on recognition (of knowledge or experience), and recognition is rational. Tradition is not reason's opposite but its soil. The shocking-but-profound claim: the rationalist pursuit of a presuppositionless starting point is itself a myth.
coreThoughts.l1En: You cannot understand anything without already carrying ideas — the 'prejudices' you want to discard are exactly the starting points of understanding.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like glasses: without them you see nothing, but with them you never see 'purely objectively' — prejudice is your lens; the point is not to remove it but to know it's there.
coreThoughts.l3En: His critique of the Enlightenment's prejudice against prejudice: the presuppositionless ideal is itself a prejudice. Authority = recognition, not submission; tradition = effective history. The Habermas debate: is tradition systematically distorted by power? (critical vs philosophical hermeneutics).

famousEvents.title: 与哈贝马斯的诠释学之争
famousEvents.desc: 《真理与方法》出版后，哈贝马斯撰文批评其为「保守的诠释学」——把传统理想化而忽视权力对传统的扭曲。两人论战十余年，成为 20 世纪德国哲学最重要的公开论争之一；论战本身最终也变成「对话生成意义」的生动演示——谁也没说服谁，但双方都因对方而更精确。
famousEvents.descEn: Habermas attacked Truth and Method as 'conservative hermeneutics' — idealizing tradition while ignoring power's distortions. A decade of debate, one of 20th-century German philosophy's most important public controversies — itself a demonstration of dialogue generating meaning: neither persuaded the other, both sharpened by the exchange.

famousEvents.title: 世纪的见证者
famousEvents.desc: 伽达默尔百岁寿辰时已是 20 世纪哲学的活档案：他是海德格尔最著名的学生（马堡时期）、胡塞尔现象学的亲历者，见证过纳粹时期海德格尔的失足、战后现象学的传播、分析哲学的登陆、后结构主义的喧嚣。他在访谈中总结世纪：「20 世纪教会我们的是：不要迷信任何体系——包括对体系的迷信。」
famousEvents.descEn: At 100 he was a living archive of 20th-century philosophy: Heidegger's most famous student (Marburg), witness to Husserl's phenomenology, Heidegger's Nazi lapse, the postwar spread of phenomenology, the analytic landing, post-structuralist noise. His summary: 'The 20th century taught us: don't fetishize any system — including the fetish of systemlessness.'

philosophers.scientificEval: 《真理与方法》对「自然科学 vs 人文科学」的方法论分工提出了经典论证：自然科学追求「方法保证的客观性」，人文科学（精神科学）的理解则是「参与者式的」——诠释学揭示的是理解本身的存在论结构，而非一套可操作的方法。此说引发与科学哲学的持久对话：波普尔、哈贝马斯批判其相对主义倾向，而当代科学诠释学（库恩范式的「视域」性、科学文本的诠释学维度）反而部分印证了伽达默尔的洞见。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: Truth and Method's classic argument: natural science pursues method-guaranteed objectivity, while understanding in the human sciences is participatory — hermeneutics discloses understanding's ontological structure, not an operable method. Long dialogue with philosophy of science: Popper and Habermas attack its relativism; contemporary scientific hermeneutics (Kuhn's paradigms as horizons, the hermeneutic dimension of scientific texts) partly confirms his insight.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 伽达默尔的学术生涯：马堡学派的古典语文学训练 → 师从海德格尔（1923 年起）转向存在论 → 以柏拉图和亚里士多德研究成名（《柏拉图的辩证伦理学》）→ 战后任教法兰克福、海德堡 → 1960 年出版《真理与方法》（时年 60 岁，成名作即代表作）→ 此后四十年不断回应批评（与哈贝马斯论战、与德里达的巴黎相遇 1981），把诠释学发展为实践哲学。他晚年说：「我一生的工作就是证明：理解比方法更根本。」
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: Marburg classical philology → Heidegger's student (1923) toward ontology → Plato and Aristotle studies (Platonic Dialectical Ethics) → Frankfurt and Heidelberg chairs → Truth and Method at 60 (masterpiece as debut) → forty years of responses (Habermas debate, the Paris encounter with Derrida 1981), developing hermeneutics into practical philosophy. His late summary: 'My life's work is proving that understanding is more fundamental than method.'
philosophers.aiReview: 伽达默尔在「客观主义」与「相对主义」之间走了一条极窄的钢索：他既反对「理解=复原原意」的客观主义神话，也拒绝「怎么理解都行」的相对主义——理解受传统约束，但传统本身也在对话中改变。这条钢索让他在 20 世纪方法论大战中两头挨打（科学家说他不客观，后现代说他不够激进），却也让他的理论成为最有韧性的那一个。今天，当 AI 文本生成让「理解」本身成为问题、当跨文化对话成为全球议题，「视域融合」比 1960 年更需要被重读——我们从来不是「客观地」理解彼此，而是在各自的视域里生成共同的视域，这正是对话的意义。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Gadamer walked an extremely narrow wire between objectivism and relativism: against the myth of recovering original meaning, against 'anything goes' — understanding is bound by tradition, yet tradition itself changes in dialogue. The wire drew fire from both sides (scientists: not objective; postmodernists: not radical enough), yet made his theory the most resilient. Today, when AI text generation makes 'understanding' itself a problem and cross-cultural dialogue a global agenda, fusion of horizons needs rereading more than in 1960: we never 'objectively' understand each other — we generate shared horizons from our own, which is what dialogue is.

philosophers.anecdote: 伽达默尔 102 岁去世，但他与 20 世纪哲学的缘分从「拒绝」开始：1923 年他在弗莱堡听了海德格尔的第一堂课，立刻被吸引，却拒绝了海德格尔的助手职位——他说「我不想成为海德格尔的影子」。这个决定让他保持了独立的学术道路。他晚年回忆纳粹时期：海德格尔当校长时，他（年轻的讲师）曾当面顶撞这位大师，海德格尔反而欣赏他的勇气——「他后来对我说：你是我唯一敢反驳我的人。」
philosophers.anecdoteEn: He died at 102, but his bond with the century began with a refusal: hearing Heidegger's first lecture at Freiburg in 1923, he was drawn yet declined the assistantship — 'I did not want to become Heidegger's shadow.' The decision kept him independent. Recalling the Nazi era: as a young lecturer he once contradicted Heidegger to his face; Heidegger appreciated the courage — 'He told me later: you are the only one who ever dared contradict me.'

philosophers.name: 梅洛-庞蒂
philosophers.role: 身体现象学创始人，「具身性」概念的哲学奠基人
philosophers.summary: 法国现象学的代表人物，与萨特齐名又分道扬镳。他的《知觉现象学》（1945）提出：我们不是「先有心灵、后有身体」的二元存在，而是「我就是我的身体」——身体是知觉世界的主体，一切意义都从身体的在世存在（être-au-monde）中涌现。「具身性」（embodiment）由此成为 20 世纪哲学最富成果的概念之一，深刻影响了认知科学、心理学、人工智能与神经科学。他 53 岁猝然去世，留下未完成的巨著《可见者与不可见者》——「我们是自己身体的观察者，也是被身体观察者」。
philosophers.summaryEn: The representative of French phenomenology, Sartre's peer and eventual rival. The Phenomenology of Perception (1945): we are not dual beings of mind plus body but 'I am my body' — the body is the subject that perceives the world, all meaning emerges from bodily being-in-the-world (être-au-monde). 'Embodiment' became one of the 20th century's most fruitful concepts, shaping cognitive science, psychology, AI, and neuroscience. He died suddenly at 53, leaving The Visible and the Invisible unfinished — 'we are observers of our body and observed by our body.'

representativeWorks.title: 《知觉现象学》
representativeWorks.content: 梅洛-庞蒂的奠基之作：以「被体验的身体」取代「客观的身体」——身体不是心灵的工具，而是我们「在世存在」的方式。空间、时间、他者、自由都从身体出发重新解释。现象学与心理学的经典交叉。
representativeWorks.contentEn: His founding work: the lived body replaces the objective body — the body is not the mind's instrument but our way of being-in-the-world. Space, time, others, and freedom re-derived from the body. A classic at the phenomenology-psychology interface.

representativeWorks.title: 《可见者与不可见者》
representativeWorks.content: 遗著（编辑整理）：提出「肉身」（chair）概念——主体与客体、可见与不可见、看与被看都来自同一个「世界之肉」。晚期梅洛-庞蒂对二元论的最终解构，被视为 20 世纪最深奥的哲学文本之一。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Posthumous: the concept of 'flesh' (la chair) — subject and object, visible and invisible, seeing and seen all arise from one 'flesh of the world'. The late deconstruction of dualism; among the 20th century's most profound philosophical texts.

coreThoughts.desc: 笛卡尔说「我思故我在」——心灵才是认识的主体；梅洛-庞蒂反过来说：在「我思」之前，我已经「我在」——我首先是世界中的身体，我的知觉、动作、习惯都先于反思。身体不是「拥有」的物件（我的身体）而是「存在」的方式（我就是我的身体）。你不需要「想」怎么开门，你的手已经知道；你不「计算」楼梯的间距，你的腿已经知道——这种「身体知道」（savoir du corps）比理智更根本。梅洛-庞蒂称之为「意向弧」：身体是一个整体地、前反思地朝向世界的意向结构。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：梅洛-庞蒂说「我不是有一个身体，我就是身体」——你不需要想就知道怎么走路、开门、接球，因为身体本身就是认识的主体。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像打篮球：球飞来时你来不及「想」怎么接，手自己动了——那个「自己动」的身体，就是梅洛-庞蒂说的真正的「我」。
coreThoughts.l3: 身体主体性（corps propre / lived body）：身体是「在世存在」的载体。意向弧（arc intentionnel）：身体的前反思意向结构。习惯（habitude）作为身体知识。此概念对笛卡尔二元论的解构直接影响了：认知科学的具身认知（embodied cognition，瓦雷拉/汤普森）、神经现象学、人工智能中的「身体化智能」、以及设计学中的「身体经验」。
coreThoughts.descEn: Descartes: I think therefore I am — mind is the knowing subject. Merleau-Ponty inverts: before 'I think', I already am — I am first a body in the world; perception, movement, habit precede reflection. The body is not a thing I have (my body) but a way I am (I am my body). You needn't think to open a door; your hand knows. You don't calculate stair spacing; your legs know. This 'body knowledge' (savoir du corps) is more fundamental than intellect — the 'intentional arc': the body as a holistic, pre-reflective orientation toward the world.
coreThoughts.l1En: I don't have a body; I am my body — you don't need to think to walk, open doors, catch balls; the body itself is the knowing subject.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like basketball: when the ball comes you can't 'think' how to catch — the hand moves itself. That self-moving body is the true 'I'.
coreThoughts.l3En: The lived body as being-in-the-world; the intentional arc; habit as bodily knowledge. His deconstruction of Cartesian dualism directly shapes embodied cognition (Varela, Thompson), neurophenomenology, embodied AI, and bodily-experience design.

coreThoughts.desc: 晚期梅洛-庞蒂的终极命题：为什么我能看见世界，也能被世界看见？（镜子里我看见自己的脸——既是看者又是被看者。）他的回答：因为看与被看来自同一个「肉身」（la chair）——我身体的肉与世界之肉是同一种质地。我的手能摸自己，说明「可摸者」与「摸者」是同一个世界的两面；我的眼睛能看见自己（通过镜子、他人），说明「可见者」与「看者」互通。由此，主体与客体、心灵与自然的二元对立被溶解：我们都是世界之肉的褶皱。「肉身」不是物质也不是精神，而是两者的共同源头。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：梅洛-庞蒂说「我能看见世界，世界也能看见我」——因为我和世界是用同一种「肉」做的，看者和被看者是同一块料子。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像左手摸右手：右手是「摸者」，左手是「被摸者」，但它们是一只手的两面——梅洛-庞蒂说你和世界就是这只手的两面。
coreThoughts.l3: 肉身（la chair）概念（《可见者与不可见者》）：非二元论的「元素」——像水、火一样是构成性的元素而非实体。「可逆性」（réversibilité）：看/被看、触/被触的可逆结构。此概念影响：梅洛-庞蒂式的生态现象学（人与自然共属）、后人类主义（人与非人共享世界之肉）、以及当代对「具身人工智能」的哲学批判。
coreThoughts.conceptEn: Flesh and the Flesh of the World
coreThoughts.descEn: His final thesis: why can I see the world and be seen by it (the mirror shows my face — I am both seer and seen)? Because seeing and being-seen arise from one flesh (la chair): my body's flesh and the world's flesh share one texture. My hand touching itself shows toucher and touched are two sides of one world; my eye seeing itself (mirror, others) shows visible and seer interpenetrate. The dualisms of subject/object, mind/nature dissolve: we are folds of the world's flesh. Flesh is neither matter nor spirit but their common source.
coreThoughts.l1En: I can see the world and the world can see me — because I and the world are made of the same 'flesh'; seer and seen are one cloth.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like the left hand touching the right: right is toucher, left is touched, but they are two sides of one hand — you and the world are the two sides of that hand.
coreThoughts.l3En: La chair (The Visible and the Invisible): a non-dualist 'element' — constitutive like water or fire, not a substance. Reversibility: the see/seen, touch/touched structure. Influences ecological phenomenology, posthumanism (humans and nonhumans sharing world-flesh), and philosophical critique of embodied AI.

famousEvents.title: 与萨特的「存在主义兄弟情」与决裂
famousEvents.desc: 二战期间梅洛-庞蒂与萨特并肩抵抗，共同创办《现代》杂志（1945）。1950 年代朝鲜战争爆发后，两人就「苏联与暴力」激烈分歧——萨特支持苏联立场，梅洛-庞蒂退出编辑部，兄弟决裂。这段友谊的破裂是法国知识界 20 世纪中叶最重要的分裂事件之一。
famousEvents.descEn: Together in the Resistance, they co-founded Les Temps modernes (1945). After Korea they split over the USSR and violence — Sartre toward the Soviet side, Merleau-Ponty resigning from the editorial board. The rupture was among mid-century French intellectual life's most important schisms.

famousEvents.title: 法兰西学院讲席
famousEvents.desc: 梅洛-庞蒂当选法兰西学院「哲学讲席」教授（此前为柏格森、拉韦勒的席位）——34 岁成为法国哲学界最高讲席的持有者，与萨特（无教职的「独立知识分子」）形成对照：学院派哲学 vs 广场哲学的两条路。
famousEvents.descEn: Elected to the philosophy chair at the Collège de France in 1952 (Bergson's seat) at 34 — the academy's highest philosophy post, contrasting with Sartre's independent-intellectual path: institutional vs public philosophy.

philosophers.scientificEval: 梅洛-庞蒂是 20 世纪与科学对话最深的哲学家之一：《知觉现象学》大量引用当时的行为主义与格式塔心理学、神经病理学（施奈德病例），其「身体图式」概念与神经科学高度兼容；他直接启发了「具身认知」运动（瓦雷拉、汤普森、拉科夫）、神经现象学（瓦雷拉）、以及「4E 认知」（具身/嵌入/生成/延展）。当代触觉科学、运动控制研究与机器人触觉交互都从「身体知识」概念获益。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: Among the 20th century's deepest philosopher-scientist dialogues: the Phenomenology of Perception cites behaviorism, Gestalt psychology, and neuropathology (the Schneider case); his body schema is neuroscience-compatible. He directly inspires embodied cognition (Varela, Thompson, Lakoff), neurophenomenology, and 4E cognition (embodied/embedded/enactive/extended). Touch science, motor control, and robotic haptics draw on 'body knowledge'.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 梅洛-庞蒂的思想三部曲：早年《行为的结构》（1942）与《知觉现象学》（1945）从格式塔心理学出发确立身体主体性；中期（1950s）转入历史与政治哲学（《人道主义与恐怖》《辩证法的历险》），试图把身体的存在论与社会历史结合；晚期（1955-1961）回归存在论，《可见者与不可见者》把身体论深化为「肉身」存在论——从「我的身体」到「世界之肉」。他 53 岁因心脏病猝死，第三阶段戛然而止——他留下的计划与笔记，成为 20 世纪现象学最珍贵的未完成稿。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: Three phases: early (The Structure of Behavior 1942, Phenomenology of Perception 1945) establishing bodily subjectivity from Gestalt psychology; middle (1950s) history and politics (Humanism and Terror, Adventures of the Dialectic) seeking to join body-ontology with social history; late (1955-61) returning to ontology, The Visible and the Invisible deepening the body into 'flesh' ontology — from my body to the world's flesh. Sudden cardiac death at 53 cut the third phase short; his plans and notes are among phenomenology's most precious unfinished manuscripts.
philosophers.aiReview: 梅洛-庞蒂在 20 世纪哲学里是个「迟到者」——他的身体现象学在分析哲学与后结构主义的喧嚣中沉寂了几十年，却在 21 世纪被重新发现：因为认知科学、AI 和机器人学撞上了同一个问题——「智能真的可以脱离身体存在吗？」当大语言模型用纯符号「思考」时，梅洛-庞蒂的警告显得格外刺耳：理解世界的方式首先是身体的（婴儿先会抓握才会计数），没有身体的知识是残缺的。他的「肉身」概念也让生态哲学找到了表达「人与自然同一」的哲学语言。这个在 53 岁猝然离世的人，留下的问题比他活过的年代更长寿。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: A late bloomer in 20th-century philosophy: his bodily phenomenology slept for decades amid analytic and post-structural noise, rediscovered in the 21st century because cognitive science, AI, and robotics hit the same wall — can intelligence exist without a body? When LLMs 'think' in pure symbols, his warning sounds sharper: understanding the world is first bodily (babies grasp before counting); knowledge without a body is crippled. His flesh gives ecological philosophy a language for 'human and nature as one'. Dying at 53, he left questions longer-lived than his era.

furtherReading.desc: 身体现象学奠基之作

philosophers.anecdote: 梅洛-庞蒂与萨特的友谊曾是巴黎最著名的知识分子组合，两人几乎形影不离，萨特写《恶心》、他写《知觉现象学》。破裂后，梅洛-庞蒂有一次在街上偶遇萨特，两人沉默相对——梅洛-庞蒂后来说：「我们像两座互相背对的山。」他去世时萨特在《现代》杂志上写了悼文，两人和解于死亡。这段友谊的始末，本身就是一部法国知识分子的存在主义小说。
philosophers.anecdoteEn: His friendship with Sartre was Paris' most famous intellectual duo — almost inseparable, Sartre writing Nausea, Merleau-Ponty the Phenomenology of Perception. After the rupture they once met on the street and stood silent; Merleau-Ponty said later: 'We were like two mountains facing away from each other.' At his death Sartre wrote the eulogy in Les Temps modernes — reconciled by death. The friendship's arc is itself an existentialist novel of French intellectuals.

philosophers.name: 列维纳斯
philosophers.role: 「他者哲学」奠基人，伦理学第一哲学的提出者
philosophers.summary: 20 世纪最重要的伦理学-现象学哲学家，将「他者」（the Other）置于哲学的核心。他出生于立陶宛犹太家庭，在斯特拉斯堡学习哲学，师从胡塞尔、海德格尔，却反叛了他们的存在论——「存在论把他人化约为同一，而伦理学要求：他者先于自我」。他的《总体与无限》（1961）提出「伦理学是第一哲学」：我的责任不是从我的自由推出，而是被「他者的面容」（le visage）所召唤——他者的脸对我发出「不可杀人」的绝对命令。纳粹大屠杀夺走了他在立陶宛的全部家人（父母与兄弟），这段经历使他的哲学成为对 20 世纪暴力最深沉的回应。
philosophers.summaryEn: The most important ethicist-phenomenologist of the 20th century, placing the Other at philosophy's center. Born into a Lithuanian Jewish family, studied philosophy at Strasbourg, disciple of Husserl and Heidegger — whom he rebelled against: 'ontology reduces the other to the same, but ethics demands: the other precedes the self.' Totality and Infinity (1961): ethics is first philosophy; my responsibility is not derived from my freedom but summoned by the other's face (le visage), issuing the absolute command 'you shall not kill'. The Holocaust took his entire family in Lithuania; his philosophy became the century's deepest response to violence.

representativeWorks.title: 《总体与无限》
representativeWorks.content: 「伦理学作为第一哲学」的奠基作：自我（same）与世界的关系是「享受」与「居住」，而与他者的关系是「面对」——他者的面容以其赤裸与脆弱向我发出「不可杀人」的命令，我的无限责任由此被唤醒。
representativeWorks.contentEn: The founding work of ethics as first philosophy: the self's relation to the world is enjoyment and dwelling, but the relation to the other is facing — the other's face, in its nakedness and vulnerability, issues 'you shall not kill', awakening my infinite responsibility.

representativeWorks.title: 《别于存在或超越本质》
representativeWorks.content: 晚期代表作：把伦理学推进到「替代」（substitution）的极端——主体不是自由的主体而是「人质」（hostage），为他者承担到「代他受苦」的地步。被德里达称为「20 世纪最深刻的伦理学著作」。
representativeWorks.titleEn: Otherwise than Being or Beyond Essence
representativeWorks.contentEn: His late work: ethics pushed to the extreme of substitution — the subject is not a free agent but a hostage, responsible for the other to the point of suffering in their place. Derrida called it the 20th century's most profound ethical work.

coreThoughts.desc: 列维纳斯的起点：西方哲学（从巴门尼德到黑格尔到海德格尔）都是一种「存在论」——把一切存在者化约为一个总体（totality），自我去「同一化」他者（把他者纳入我的概念、我的世界、我的体系）。列维纳斯说：这整个传统就是「暴力的哲学」。与之相对，他者的「面容」（le visage）打断了我的同一化——一张脸看着我，它不服从我的概念，它拒绝被纳入总体；面容对我说话，说出第一句话：「不可杀人。」面对他者，我的第一个反应不是认识而是责任。伦理学因此先于存在论：不是「我思故我在」，而是「他在故我在」。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：列维纳斯说别人不是「你要认识的对象」，而是「向你发出命令的脸」——看到那张脸，你的第一句话不是「你是谁」而是「我不能伤害你」。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像对视：你可以把任何东西变成你研究的东西，但当一双眼睛看着你，你没法再把它当物品——列维纳斯说，伦理就从这双眼睛里长出来。
coreThoughts.l3: 面容（le visage）≠ 具体的脸：它是他者的「现象学显现」——不可把捉、不可概念化、诉诸责任的「表达」。第一诫「不可杀人」（Tu ne tueras point）＝面容的语言。列维纳斯由此重建伦理学：从「义务论/功利论」（自我中心的道德计算）转向「他者中心的无限责任」。影响：德里达（对他者性的思考）、保罗·利科、以及当代「他者伦理学」与战争/大屠杀研究。
coreThoughts.descEn: His starting point: Western philosophy (from Parmenides through Hegel to Heidegger) is ontology — reducing all beings to a totality, the self 'same-ifying' the other (absorbing the other into my concepts, my world, my system). This whole tradition, he says, is the philosophy of violence. Against it: the face (le visage) interrupts my same-ification — a face looks at me, obeys no concept, refuses totality; it speaks, and its first word is 'you shall not kill'. Facing the other, my first response is not knowledge but responsibility. Ethics precedes ontology: not 'I think therefore I am' but 'the other is, therefore I am obligated'.
coreThoughts.l1En: The other is not an object of knowledge but a face that commands: seeing that face, your first word is not 'who are you' but 'I must not harm you'.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like eye contact: you can turn anything into your research object, but when eyes look at you, it's no longer a thing — ethics grows from that gaze.
coreThoughts.l3En: The face is the other's phenomenological expression — unmasterable, un-concept-izable, calling to responsibility. 'You shall not kill' is the face's language. Ethics rebuilt from ego-centered moral calculation to other-centered infinite responsibility. Influences Derrida, Ricoeur, otherness-ethics, and Holocaust studies.

coreThoughts.concept: 作为第一哲学的伦理学
coreThoughts.desc: 列维纳斯的纲领性命题：伦理学不是哲学的一个分支（如「应用伦理学」），而是哲学的「第一哲学」——一切哲学问题（认识论、存在论、政治哲学）都必须从「对他者的责任」出发重新奠基。为什么？因为「自我」从来不是自足的起点：我出生时已欠世界，我说话时已在回应，我存在时已在他者之中。「我」是由责任构成的——不是先有自由的我、再选择负责，而是责任先于自由：「我在」即是「我在此为他者负责」。这个倒转让 20 世纪的伦理学从「我应该做什么」（康德/功利主义）转向「他者要求我什么」——从权利伦理学转向责任伦理学。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：列维纳斯说「负责」不是你可以选的事——你一生下来就欠着别人（母亲、社会、世界），伦理不是选修课，是第一课。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像出生的那一刻：你没法先「决定」要不要被照顾——你已经被照顾了，已经欠下了——列维纳斯说责任就是这样，先于你的一切选择。
coreThoughts.l3: 「伦理学作为第一哲学」（éthique comme philosophie première，1982 年同名演讲）：从笛卡尔-康德的主体性哲学转向「为他者」的责任哲学。批评者（德里达）追问：他者的命令是否也是一种暴力？列维纳斯回应：他者的命令是「非暴力」的——它不强迫，只召唤。此命题深刻影响当代：责任伦理学（乔纳斯）、关怀伦理学（诺丁斯）、后殖民的「倾听他者」、以及大屠杀后的神学（犹太思想传统）。
coreThoughts.descEn: His programmatic thesis: ethics is not a branch of philosophy (like 'applied ethics') but first philosophy — all philosophical questions (epistemology, ontology, politics) must be re-founded from responsibility to the other. Why? The self is never a self-sufficient starting point: I am born already indebted, I speak already responding, I exist already among others. 'I' is constituted by responsibility — not a free self that chooses responsibility, but responsibility before freedom: 'to be' is 'to be-here for the other'. Turning 20th-century ethics from 'what should I do' (Kant/utilitarianism) to 'what does the other demand of me' — from rights-ethics to responsibility-ethics.
coreThoughts.l1En: Responsibility is not optional: from birth you owe others (mother, society, world) — ethics is not an elective but the first course.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like the moment of birth: you cannot first 'decide' to be cared for — you are already cared for, already indebted. Responsibility precedes every choice.
coreThoughts.l3En: Ethics as first philosophy: from Cartesian-Kantian subjectivity to responsibility-for-the-other. Derrida's question: is the other's command itself a violence? Levinas: the other's command is non-violent — it summons, not forces. Influences responsibility ethics (Jonas), care ethics (Noddings), postcolonial listening-to-the-other, and post-Holocaust theology.

famousEvents.title: 战俘营中的《存在与时间》
famousEvents.desc: 作为法国军官被德军俘虏，列维纳斯在战俘营度过五年。期间他反复研读海德格尔的《存在与时间》——这位曾给他「思想新生」的哲学家，正是迫害他族人的纳粹阵营中人。他在营中写下的笔记，成为后来批判海德格尔存在论、转向他者哲学的最初种子。
famousEvents.titleEn: Being and Time in the POW Camp
famousEvents.descEn: Captured as a French officer, he spent five years in a POW camp, repeatedly studying Heidegger's Being and Time — the philosopher who had given him 'intellectual rebirth' yet stood in the camp of his people's persecutors. His camp notes grew into the critique of ontology and the turn to the other.

famousEvents.title: 全家罹难
famousEvents.desc: 纳粹入侵立陶宛后，列维纳斯的父母与兄弟在考纳斯遇害。他出狱后得知噩耗，毕生背负这重创——他后来几乎不谈自己的家庭悲剧，但「他者的苦难」「不可杀人」贯穿他全部著作，正是这段历史的思想回响。
famousEvents.descEn: After the Nazi invasion of Lithuania, his parents and brothers were murdered in Kaunas. Learning of it after release, he carried the wound for life — rarely speaking of the tragedy, yet 'the other's suffering' and 'you shall not kill' running through all his work as its intellectual echo.

philosophers.scientificEval: 列维纳斯对社会科学的影响主要在伦理学与临床领域：「他者伦理学」被引入医学伦理（患者的他者性、医患关系的责任结构）、护理伦理学（照护作为对他者的回应）与心理治疗（治疗师作为「为他者」的存在）；其对「总体的暴力」的分析被后殖民研究与战争伦理学引用；在 AI 伦理兴起的当下，其「他者不可化约」思想被用于讨论「算法对他者的治理」的伦理边界。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: His influence lands mainly in ethics and the clinic: otherness-ethics in medical ethics (the patient's otherness, the responsibility structure of the clinical encounter), nursing ethics (care as response to the other), and psychotherapy (the therapist as being-for-the-other); his analysis of the violence of totality is cited in postcolonial studies and the ethics of war; in the AI-ethics boom, 'the other is irreducible' frames debates on algorithmic governance of others.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 列维纳斯的轨迹：斯特拉斯堡（哲学训练）→ 弗莱堡听胡塞尔、海德格尔（1928-29）→ 1930 年代以现象学介绍者成名（《胡塞尔现象学中的直观理论》）→ 战俘营五年 → 战后执教巴黎多校、参与犹太教育（巴黎以色列师范学院院长）→ 《总体与无限》（1961，教授资格论文）→ 《别于存在》（1974）→ 晚年与德里达的对话与「人质」伦理学。他的哲学从不改变方向——从早期「存在论批判」到晚期的「替代/人质」，始终在说同一件事：他者先于自我，责任先于存在。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: Strasbourg training → Freiburg hearing Husserl and Heidegger (1928-29) → 1930s as phenomenology's introducer in France (The Theory of Intuition in Husserl's Phenomenology) → five POW years → postwar Paris chairs and Jewish education (director of the Alliance Israélite school) → Totality and Infinity (1961, his habilitation) → Otherwise than Being (1974) → late dialogues with Derrida and the hostage-ethics. His direction never changes — from early ontology-critique to late substitution/hostage, always one message: the other precedes the self; responsibility precedes being.
philosophers.aiReview: 列维纳斯是那种「你无法和他辩论，只能被他质问」的哲学家——他的命题（他者先于自我、责任先于自由、伦理学先于存在论）不是论证出来的，而是从极端处境里硬长出来的：一个全家死于大屠杀的人，写下了「不可杀人」的哲学。他常被批评「不现实」（无限责任谁能承担？），但他的回答恰恰是：正因为承担不了，责任才是无限的——你永远可以做更多，这就是责任。在「自我优先」成为时代默认值的今天（算法推荐、个人主义、自我实现的话语），列维纳斯像一记逆行的钟声：他提醒我们，最深的自由不是「做自己」，而是「为他者负责」——而拒绝这个，才是真正的失败。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: The philosopher you cannot argue with, only be questioned by — his theses (other before self, responsibility before freedom, ethics before ontology) were not argued but grown from extremity: a man whose family died in the Holocaust writing the philosophy of 'you shall not kill'. Accused of unreality (who can bear infinite responsibility?), his answer: precisely because it's unbearable, responsibility is infinite — you can always do more; that's what responsibility is. In an age of self-priority (algorithms, individualism, self-realization discourse), Levinas is a bell ringing backward: the deepest freedom is not 'be yourself' but 'be for the other' — and refusing that is the real failure.

philosophers.anecdote: 列维纳斯晚年在访谈中被问：「什么是你给 20 世纪哲学的遗产？」他沉默片刻说：「我不确定。我只知道，我一生都在试图回答一个问题：在奥斯维辛之后，我们还能不能谈论上帝与伦理？我的答案是：可以——但必须先谈论他者。」他一生回避谈论自己家庭的悲剧，唯一一次被记者追问时，他说：「我的家人死于考纳斯。但这与你无关，与他们有关——他们的脸，还欠我一个回答。」
philosophers.anecdoteEn: Asked in a late interview what he leaves to 20th-century philosophy, he said after a pause: 'I am not sure. I only know I spent my life answering one question: after Auschwitz, can we still speak of God and ethics? My answer: yes — but we must first speak of the other.' Asked about his family's fate, he replied once: 'They died in Kaunas. But that concerns you not at all — it concerns them. Their faces still owe me an answer.'
