philosophers.name: 卡纳普
philosophers.role: 逻辑实证主义核心人物，维也纳学派旗手
philosophers.summary: 逻辑实证主义（维也纳学派）的旗手，20 世纪分析哲学最重要的体系建筑师之一。他的《世界的逻辑构造》（1928）试图用逻辑构造全部知识；《语言的逻辑句法》（1934）提出「宽容原则」：哲学问题多是伪问题，语言规则是约定的选择；《可检验性与意义》（1936）给出「可验证原则」的经典表述——一个命题有意义，当且仅当它原则上可被经验验证。他 1935 年因纳粹压力移居美国，把逻辑实证主义带入英语世界，深刻塑造了此后三十年英美科学哲学。他的「消除形而上学」计划争议巨大，却是 20 世纪哲学最著名的转向之一。
philosophers.summaryEn: The banner-carrier of logical positivism (the Vienna Circle) and one of the 20th century's greatest system-builders in analytic philosophy. The Logical Structure of the World (1928) tried to construct all knowledge by logic; The Logical Syntax of Language (1934) gave the tolerance principle — philosophical problems are mostly pseudo-problems, language rules are conventional choices; Testability and Meaning (1936) formulated the verification principle: a proposition is meaningful iff verifiable in principle. Emigrating to the U.S. in 1935 under Nazi pressure, he imported logical positivism into the English-speaking world, shaping Anglo-American philosophy of science for three decades. His 'elimination of metaphysics' is among the century's most controversial and famous turns.

representativeWorks.title: 《世界的逻辑构造》
representativeWorks.content: 以「我自己的经验流」为基本元素，用现代逻辑（类、关系）构造出全部经验概念——「构造系统」（Aufbau）。逻辑实证主义「一切知识可还原为经验+逻辑」纲领的极致演示。
representativeWorks.titleEn: The Logical Structure of the World (Der logische Aufbau der Welt)
representativeWorks.contentEn: From 'my own stream of experience' as base elements, constructing all empirical concepts by modern logic (classes, relations) — the constitution system. The maximal demonstration of the positivist program that all knowledge reduces to experience plus logic.

representativeWorks.title: 《语言的逻辑句法》
representativeWorks.content: 提出「宽容原则」与「形式化语言」：哲学错误源于语言误用，真正的哲学工作是用逻辑分析语言；形而上学命题是「伪命题」。维特根斯坦《逻辑哲学论》的体系化与温和化。
representativeWorks.contentEn: The tolerance principle and formal languages: philosophical error is linguistic misuse; real philosophy is logical analysis of language; metaphysical propositions are pseudo-propositions. The systematization and moderation of Wittgenstein's Tractatus.

coreThoughts.desc: 逻辑实证主义的核心武器：一个命题是否有意义，取决于它是否原则上可以被经验验证。「这桌上有本书」——有可验证条件（看一眼）→ 有意义；「绝对精神在自我运动中展开」——没有任何经验能验证或反驳它 → 不是「假命题」，而是「伪命题」（听起来像命题，其实没有真值条件）。由此，「形而上学」不是被证明为假，而是被诊断为「无意义」。这个原则把哲学从「玄学辩论」变成「语言分析」：哲学家的任务是澄清陈述的意义，而不是建构关于世界的宏大理论。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：卡纳普说「一句话有没有意义，看能不能检验」——能检验的（桌上有本书）有意义，永远检验不了的（绝对精神在动）就是废话，不值得吵。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像做实验：你说「这个药有效」——那就要能设计实验验证；你说「这个药被宇宙意志祝福」——没有实验能验证，那这句话就不能算科学陈述。
coreThoughts.l3: 可验证原则（verification principle）的历史形态：强验证（维也纳学派早期）→ 弱化（可确认性 confirmation，卡纳普 1936 后）→ 波普尔的反驳（falsification 替代验证）。批评：①自身不可验证（「验证原则」自己违反自己）；②全称命题（「所有乌鸦皆黑」）不可完全验证——故卡纳普转向「可确认度」与概率逻辑。此原则虽被修正，却是「意义理论」与科学划界问题的持久起点。
coreThoughts.descEn: Logical positivism's core weapon: a proposition is meaningful iff it is in principle verifiable by experience. 'There is a book on the table' — verifiable conditions (look) → meaningful. 'The absolute spirit unfolds in self-movement' — no experience verifies or refutes it → not false but a pseudo-proposition (sounds like a proposition, has no truth conditions). Metaphysics is not refuted but diagnosed as meaningless. Philosophy becomes language analysis: clarifying the meaning of statements, not building grand theories of the world.
coreThoughts.l1En: A sentence is meaningful if it can be tested — testable claims (a book on the table) have meaning; untestable ones (the absolute spirit moves) are nonsense not worth arguing about.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like experiments: 'this drug works' must have a testable design; 'this drug is blessed by cosmic will' has no test — it's not a scientific claim.
coreThoughts.l3En: The principle's history: strong verification (early Circle) → confirmation (Carnap post-1936) → Popper's falsification. Criticisms: self-refutation (the principle cannot verify itself); universal statements ('all ravens are black') are not fully verifiable — hence Carnap's turn to degrees of confirmation and probability logic. Revised but permanent: the starting point of meaning theory and demarcation.

coreThoughts.desc: 《语言的逻辑句法》的纲领：逻辑和数学的真理不是「关于世界的发现」，而是语言规则的约定——「我们不需要禁止任何语言形式，我们只需要给出规则，然后自由选择」。选择哪种语言（欧氏几何还是非欧几何？经典逻辑还是直觉主义逻辑？）取决于实用目的，而不是「哪个更真实」。「宽容原则」的激进含义：哲学家的「本体论争论」（共相存在吗？数存在吗？）多半是伪问题——真正的分歧在于选择了不同的语言框架，而框架的选择是实践的而非认知的。这个立场后来被奎因批判（「本体论承诺」无法回避），但「语言框架的可选择性」深刻影响了科学哲学与逻辑哲学。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：卡纳普说「用什么语言和规则是你自己的事」——没有「唯一正确的逻辑」，只有「适合你目的的规则」，别为这个吵架。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像度量衡：米还是英尺？没有「哪个更真实」，只有「哪个更方便」——卡纳普说逻辑体系的选择也是这样。
coreThoughts.l3: 宽容原则（principle of tolerance，1934）：「In logic, there are no morals」——每个人都可以自由构建自己的逻辑。语言框架（linguistic framework）与内部/外部问题的区分（1950《经验论、语义学与本体论》）：框架内部的问题可判真伪，框架本身的选择是实践问题。奎因《论有什么》（1948）反驳：接受一个框架=作出本体论承诺，无法纯实用化。
coreThoughts.descEn: The program of Logical Syntax: logical and mathematical truths are not discoveries about the world but conventions of language — 'we do not need to forbid any linguistic form; we only give rules and choose freely.' Which language (Euclidean or non-Euclidean? classical or intuitionist logic?) is a matter of practical purpose, not of 'which is more real'. Radical implication: philosophers' ontological debates (do universals exist? do numbers exist?) are mostly pseudo-questions — real disagreement is about choosing linguistic frameworks, and framework choice is practical, not cognitive. Quine later attacked (ontological commitment is unavoidable), but framework-selectability shaped philosophy of science and logic.
coreThoughts.l1En: Which language and rules you use is your choice — there is no 'only correct logic', only 'rules suited to your purpose'; don't fight over it.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like units: meters or feet? Neither is 'more real', only 'more convenient' — logic systems are chosen the same way.
coreThoughts.l3En: Tolerance (1934): 'In logic, there are no morals.' The linguistic framework and the internal/external question (1950): within a framework, questions are decidable; the framework itself is a practical choice. Quine's On What There Is (1948): accepting a framework is an ontological commitment — not purely pragmatic.

famousEvents.title: 维也纳学派的星期聚会
famousEvents.desc: 维也纳大学的石里克小组每周四晚聚会讨论（「维也纳学派」），卡纳普是核心成员。石里克死后，卡纳普与汉恩等主编《认识》杂志，把逻辑实证主义推向国际。这个「星期四之夜」的讨论组，成为 20 世纪最著名的哲学俱乐部之一。
famousEvents.descEn: Schlick's group met Thursday evenings at Vienna ('the Vienna Circle'), Carnap a core member. After Schlick's murder, Carnap and Hahn edited Erkenntnis, internationalizing logical positivism. The Thursday-night seminar became one of the 20th century's most famous philosophical clubs.

famousEvents.title: 流亡美国
famousEvents.desc: 纳粹吞并奥地利前，卡纳普移居美国（先芝加哥大学，后加州大学洛杉矶分校）。他在美国的三十年，把逻辑实证主义、概率逻辑与归纳逻辑带入英语世界——「维也纳学派在芝加哥的重生」。
famousEvents.descEn: Before the Anschluss he emigrated (Chicago, then UCLA). His thirty American years imported logical positivism, probability logic, and inductive logic into the English-speaking world — 'the Vienna Circle reborn in Chicago'.

philosophers.scientificEval: 卡纳普对科学哲学的贡献是奠基性的：他把「理论的结构」分析引入科学哲学（理论语句/观察语句的区分，1956《理论概念的方法论性质》）；他的归纳逻辑与概率逻辑（《逻辑概率的基础》1950）试图为「证据支持假说」建立形式理论；其「可确认度」概念预示了贝叶斯主义的方向。他的形式化方法直接滋养了计算机科学的形式语义、程序语言设计与逻辑编程。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: His contribution to philosophy of science is foundational: structural analysis of scientific theories (the theoretical/observational distinction, 1956); inductive and probability logic (Logical Foundations of Probability 1950) formalizing evidential support; degree of confirmation anticipating Bayesianism. His formal methods directly nourish formal semantics, programming-language design, and logic programming in computer science.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 卡纳普的轨迹：弗莱堡/耶拿学数学与物理（听过弗雷格的学生——他自称受弗雷格逻辑熏陶）→ 1920s 加入维也纳学派，出版《世界的逻辑构造》（1928）→ 1930s 语言哲学转向（《语言的逻辑句法》1934）→ 1935 移美后转向归纳逻辑与概率（《逻辑概率的基础》1950）与科学理论结构（1956）→ 晚年（UCLA，1954-1970）与奎因的「分析与综合」之争。他的一生是从「构造世界」到「分析语言」再到「概率与理论」的不断自我修正——一个始终相信「哲学可以像科学一样精确」的人。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: Mathematics and physics at Freiburg and Jena (hearing Frege's logic — he credited Frege's influence) → Vienna Circle and the Aufbau (1928) → linguistic turn (Logical Syntax 1934) → American turn to inductive logic and probability (1950) and theory structure (1956) → late UCLA years (1954-70) and the analytic/synthetic dispute with Quine. A life of continuous self-correction — from constructing the world, to analyzing language, to probability and theory: a man who always believed philosophy can be as exact as science.
philosophers.aiReview: 卡纳普在今天看来既「正确」又「天真」：正确在于——哲学确实大量是关于语言的澄清，科学理论的检验确实需要形式化；天真在于——「可验证性」作为意义标准过于干净，形而上学问题没有按他的诊断消失，而是以「本体论承诺」「理论实体」「反事实条件句」等新形式回归。但他的宽容原则在今天获得了意想不到的复活：当 AI 研究者面对「大语言模型是否真在思考」的争论时，卡纳普会说——别吵「真实性」，先明确你用的「框架」；当量子力学出现「多世界解释 vs 哥本哈根解释」时，他也会说——框架的选择是实践问题。一个被时代批评「太窄」的哲学家，其方法论却在新时代不断被证明「有用」。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Today Carnap looks both right and naive: right — much philosophy is linguistic clarification, and theory-testing needs formalization; naive — verifiability as a meaning criterion was too clean; metaphysics did not disappear but returned as ontological commitment, theoretical entities, counterfactuals. Yet his tolerance principle gains an unexpected revival: facing 'does the LLM really think?', Carnap says — don't argue 'reality', first specify your framework; facing many-worlds vs Copenhagen, he says framework choice is practical. A philosopher once criticized as too narrow, whose method keeps proving useful in new ages.

philosophers.anecdote: 卡纳普以「没有敌人的哲学家」著称：他待人谦和，连与他哲学立场相反的对手都与他保持友谊。奎因（他最著名的论敌）在悼文中写道：「卡纳普是我见过的唯一一个讨论哲学从不带火气的人——他的哲学是建筑，不是战争。」据说他晚年仍坚持每天做逻辑练习，像数学家保持手感的运动员——「哲学是手艺，需要每天磨。」
philosophers.anecdoteEn: Known as 'the philosopher without enemies': so gentle that even his philosophical opponents stayed friends. Quine, his most famous adversary, wrote in his obituary: 'Carnap was the only person I ever saw discuss philosophy without heat — his philosophy was architecture, not war.' In old age he still did logic exercises daily, like an athlete keeping his hand — 'philosophy is a craft; it needs daily grinding.'

philosophers.name: 诺齐克
philosophers.role: 自由至上主义哲学家，《无政府、国家与乌托邦》作者
philosophers.summary: 20 世纪后半叶最重要的自由至上主义（libertarian）哲学家。他的《无政府、国家与乌托邦》（1974）以权利论对抗罗尔斯的分配正义：个人拥有不可侵犯的权利（生命、自由、财产），任何再分配都是对权利的侵犯——「个人是目的，不能被当作他人的资源」。他与罗尔斯的对峙构成当代政治哲学最著名的双峰：左边是「差别原则」的罗尔斯，右边是「持有正义」的诺齐克。他还是横跨知识论（《哲学解释》）、人生意义（《被检验的生活》）的通才。晚年他承认自己早期的部分观点需要修正——「自由至上主义把政治看得太重」。
philosophers.summaryEn: The most important libertarian philosopher of the late 20th century. Anarchy, State, and Utopia (1974) answered Rawls with rights-theory: individuals have inviolable rights (life, liberty, property); any redistribution violates them — 'individuals are ends, not resources for others'. His standoff with Rawls is contemporary political philosophy's most famous twin peaks: Rawls' difference principle on the left, Nozick's entitlement theory on the right. Also a polymath (Philosophical Explanations, The Examined Life). Late in life he revised early views — 'libertarianism takes politics too seriously'.

representativeWorks.title: 《无政府、国家与乌托邦》
representativeWorks.content: 政治哲学的里程碑：从「不可侵犯的个人权利」出发，论证最小国家（只保护人身与财产）是唯一正当的国家；再分配是「对劳动的征税」与「强制劳动」；任何更大的国家都侵犯权利。与罗尔斯《正义论》的正面交锋。
representativeWorks.contentEn: The milestone: from inviolable individual rights, the minimal state (protecting only persons and property) is the only just state; redistribution is 'taxation of labor' and 'forced labor'; any larger state violates rights. The head-on clash with Rawls' A Theory of Justice.

representativeWorks.title: 《哲学解释》
representativeWorks.content: 知识论巨著：提出「真理追踪」理论（知识 = 追踪真理的信念，反事实条件分析），挑战盖梯尔问题后的知识论格局；以「解释」而非「证明」重构哲学方法。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Epistemology: the truth-tracking theory of knowledge (knowledge as belief that tracks truth, counterfactual analysis), reshaping post-Gettier epistemology; philosophy as explanation rather than proof.

representativeWorks.title: 《被检验的生活》
representativeWorks.content: 人生哲学随笔：意义、价值、爱、死亡与智慧——「一个未经检验的生活不值得过，但一个被检验的生活也会累」。知识分子大众哲学写作的典范。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Philosophical essays on meaning, value, love, death, wisdom — 'the unexamined life is not worth living, but the examined life can also tire one out'. A model of public philosophy.

coreThoughts.desc: 诺齐克对分配正义的正面理论：正义不关心「结果」而关心「过程」——只要每个人的持有（财产）是通过正当途径获得的（①初始获取正当：如洛克式的劳动混合，但不损害他人的处境；②转让正当：自愿交易、赠与、继承），那么这个分配无论如何不平等，都是正义的。「模式化原则」（按需分配、按劳分配、按贡献分配……）都是错的：任何模式都会不断被自由交易破坏，而自由交易本身是正当的——除非你不断干预（再分配），否则模式无法维持，而干预就是侵犯权利。「从每个人那里按其所持有来征收，给每个人按其所应得来分配」——诺齐克嘲笑这只是在分配「假想的饼」。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：诺齐克说正义看的是「怎么来的」不是「分得均不均」——只要你的钱是合法挣的、自愿交易的，那不管贫富差距多大，都是正义的。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像下棋：输赢不重要，重要的是每一步都按规则走——诺齐克说财产也一样，只要每一步（获取和转让）都正当，结果就该被接受。
coreThoughts.l3: 持有正义（entitlement theory）三原则：获取正义（justice in acquisition）、转让正义（justice in transfer）、矫正正义（rectification of past injustice）。「威茨基」例子：球迷自愿给张伯伦一角钱门票溢价——收入差距产生了，但每一步都自愿，谁也无权拿走。「模式化 vs 历史化」：罗尔斯的差别原则是模式化的（结果导向），诺齐克是历史化的（过程导向）。
coreThoughts.descEn: Justice concerns process, not outcome: if every holding is acquired justly (initial acquisition, e.g., Lockean labor without worsening others; transfer, e.g., voluntary exchange, gift, inheritance), then any resulting distribution, however unequal, is just. Patterned principles (to each according to need/merit/contribution) are all wrong: any pattern is constantly disrupted by free exchange, and free exchange is legitimate — maintaining the pattern requires continual intervention (redistribution), which violates rights. 'From each as they have, to each as they are due' — he mocks this as dividing a mythical pie.
coreThoughts.l1En: Justice is about how things were acquired, not how evenly they're distributed — if your money was earned legitimately and traded voluntarily, the result is just however unequal.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like chess: winning or losing aside, what matters is each move following the rules — property likewise; accept the result if every step was legitimate.
coreThoughts.l3En: Three principles: justice in acquisition, in transfer, rectification of past injustice. The Wilt Chamberlain example: fans voluntarily pay a dime; inequality arises, but every step is voluntary — no one may take it back. Patterned (Rawls, outcome-oriented) vs historical (Nozick, process-oriented).

coreThoughts.concept: 权利的边界与最小国家
coreThoughts.desc: 诺齐克的国家论证：如果个人拥有不可侵犯的权利，那么国家只能是「最小国家」——其唯一功能是防止暴力、盗窃、欺诈与执行契约。任何超出此功能的国家（福利国家、家长制立法、强制再分配）都侵犯权利。「我们不是国家的资源，国家才是我们的工具。」他承认无政府状态（每个人自我防卫）逻辑上更纯净，但通过「支配性保护机构」的洛克式论证，最小国家甚至可以从无政府中「不侵犯权利地」诞生。这个「看不见的手」论证：国家不是社会契约的产物，而是市场竞争（保护服务市场）的自然结果。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：诺齐克说国家就像守夜人——只管人身和财产的安全，其他都别管；管得越多（福利、家长式规定），就越侵犯你的权利。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像公寓保安：他的职责是防小偷，不是替你决定晚饭吃什么——诺齐克说国家也该是这个保安，不是你的保姆。
coreThoughts.l3: 最小国家（minimal state）= 守夜人国家（night-watchman state）。论证：无政府状态 → 支配性保护机构（通过竞争）→ 最小国家（禁止私力救济的非侵犯性扩展）。对福利国家的批判：再分配 = 强制劳动（对劳动成果的征税）。「模式化分配 vs 历史的权利」；其结论被批评为「把财产权置于一切权利之上」「忽视了权利的积极维度」。
coreThoughts.descEn: If individuals have inviolable rights, the state can only be minimal — its sole function protecting against violence, theft, fraud, and enforcing contracts. Any state beyond this (welfare, paternalist legislation, forced redistribution) violates rights. 'We are not the state's resources; the state is our instrument.' He admits anarchy is logically purer, but via the dominant protective agency argument, the minimal state can arise from anarchy without violating rights — an invisible-hand account: the state as the natural product of market competition in protection services, not social contract.
coreThoughts.l1En: The state is a night-watchman: protect persons and property, nothing more; the more it manages (welfare, paternalist rules), the more it violates your rights.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a building's security guard: his job is catching thieves, not deciding your dinner — the state should be that guard, not your nanny.
coreThoughts.l3En: The minimal/night-watchman state; argument: anarchy → dominant protective agency (by competition) → minimal state (non-violating extension prohibiting private justice). Against the welfare state: redistribution = forced labor (taxing labor's fruits). Criticized for privileging property rights over all others and ignoring rights' positive dimension.

famousEvents.title: 与罗尔斯的世纪对峙
famousEvents.desc: 罗尔斯《正义论》（1971）出版三年后，诺齐克《无政府、国家与乌托邦》（1974）以「权利论」正面回应。哈佛校园里，罗尔斯在 Emerson Hall 讲「差别原则」，诺齐克在隔壁教室讲「持有正义」——当代政治哲学的「双峰对决」成为学界传奇。
famousEvents.descEn: Three years after Rawls' A Theory of Justice (1971), Nozick's Anarchy, State, and Utopia (1974) answered with rights-theory. At Harvard, Rawls lectured the difference principle in Emerson Hall while Nozick lectured entitlement in the next room — the twin-peaks duel of contemporary political philosophy became legend.

famousEvents.title: 晚年自我修正
famousEvents.desc: 《被检验的生活》中诺齐克坦言：「自由至上主义把政治看得太重了。」他承认自己早年的论证过于绝对，开始关心「意义」「爱」「智慧」等超越权利的问题——这次「软化」让他的自由至上主义追随者困惑，却让他的思想更完整。
famousEvents.descEn: In The Examined Life (1989) he admitted: 'libertarianism takes politics too seriously.' Acknowledging his early arguments too absolute, he turned to meaning, love, and wisdom — puzzling his followers, completing his thought.

philosophers.scientificEval: 诺齐克的「真理追踪」知识论（《哲学解释》）被当代认识论广泛讨论：其反事实分析（如果 p 为假，你不会相信 p；如果 p 为真，你会相信 p）成为知识与怀疑论讨论的经典框架，罗伯特的「安全/灵敏」理论（Sosa、Pritchard）均承其脉络。其哲学方法（「解释」而非「证明」）影响了分析哲学的写作风格。在政治哲学领域，其权利论持续塑造关于税收、福利与财产权的当代争论。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: His truth-tracking epistemology (Philosophical Explanations) is widely discussed: the counterfactual analysis (if p were false you wouldn't believe it; if p were true you would) became the classic frame for knowledge and skepticism — Sosa and Pritchard's safety/sensitivity theories are its heirs. His 'explanation not proof' method influenced analytic style. In politics, his rights-theory continues to shape debates on taxation, welfare, and property.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 诺齐克的轨迹：普林斯顿（师从亨普尔）→ 牛津访学 → 哈佛任教终身。哲学上从「政治哲学单一主题」走向「百科全书式探索」：1974 年以《无政府、国家与乌托邦》一战成名（年仅 36 岁），1981 年《哲学解释》转向知识论与形而上学，1989 年《被检验的生活》转向人生意义，1993 年《理性的本性》探讨决策与价值。他晚年承认早期自由至上主义的绝对化，但从未放弃「个人权利不可侵犯」的核心——变的只是对权利之限度的认识。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: Princeton (under Hempel) → Oxford → Harvard for life. From single-theme politics to encyclopedic exploration: famous at 36 with Anarchy, State, and Utopia (1974); Philosophical Explanations (1981) to epistemology and metaphysics; The Examined Life (1989) to meaning; The Nature of Rationality (1993). Late revisions of his early libertarian absolutes, but never abandoning inviolable individual rights — only the recognition of their limits.
philosophers.aiReview: 诺齐克是「一个让所有立场都不舒服的人」：自由派嫌他冷酷（再分配=强制劳动），保守派嫌他不稳定（晚年自我修正），哲学同行嫌他太聪明（几乎每个反驳都带着令人恼火的机灵）。但正是这种「让所有人不舒服」，让他的思想有了生命力：当你觉得「多收点税帮助穷人天经地义」时，他逼你想——如果那是「我」的劳动果实，凭什么不经我同意被拿走？这个问题的力量不在于你同意他，而在于你无法假装它不存在。他的《被检验的生活》里有一句被引用无数次的温柔：「智慧不是知道答案，而是知道哪些问题值得追问。」
philosophers.aiReviewEn: The man who makes everyone uncomfortable: liberals find him cold (redistribution as forced labor), conservatives find him unstable (late self-revision), peers find him too clever. But this discomfort is his vitality: when you think 'taxing more to help the poor is self-evident', he forces the question — if that's my labor's fruit, how can it be taken without my consent? Its power lies not in agreement but in the impossibility of pretending it away. The Examined Life holds the much-quoted gentleness: 'Wisdom is not knowing the answers but knowing which questions are worth asking.'

furtherReading.title: 《无政府、国家与乌托邦》（姚大志中译本）
furtherReading.desc: 自由至上主义经典，与罗尔斯对峙的右翼高峰

philosophers.anecdote: 诺齐克 36 岁出版《无政府、国家与乌托邦》即成名，但他讨厌「自由至上主义旗手」的标签。有一次演讲后，听众把他当作自由市场布道者提问，他回答：「我不是自由市场的传教士——我只是一个对权利问题着迷的哲学家，碰巧发现罗尔斯的差别原则需要回答。」他后来在《被检验的生活》里写：「如果我的书让我赢得了太多追随者，那一定是我写错了什么。」
philosophers.anecdoteEn: Famous at 36, he disliked the 'libertarian banner' label. After one lecture, addressed as a free-market preacher, he replied: 'I'm not a missionary of the free market — just a philosopher fascinated by rights, who happened to find Rawls' difference principle needing an answer.' In The Examined Life: 'If my book won me too many disciples, I must have written something wrong.'

goldenQuotes.textEn: Individuals have rights, and there are things no person or group may do to them (without violating those rights).

goldenQuotes.textEn: Individuals are ends, not means; they may not be sacrificed for the benefit of others.

philosophers.name: 罗蒂
philosophers.role: 新实用主义代表，分析哲学的解构者
philosophers.summary: 20 世纪后期最有争议也最有影响力的美国哲学家之一：一个「从内部拆解分析哲学」的人。他的《哲学与自然之镜》（1979）宣告：心灵是「自然之镜」的比喻早已破产，哲学没有特殊的「第一性」地位，它只是文化中的一种对话。他主张「反表象主义」（真理不是对实在的镜像）、「反基础主义」（没有一切知识赖以立足的阿基米德点）、「种族中心主义」（我们只能从自己的语言出发）与「自由主义反讽者」（承认自己信念的偶然性，却仍坚持自由主义理想）。他让实用主义（经杜威、詹姆斯）在 20 世纪末重新成为美国哲学的主流声音，并深刻影响了文学理论、政治理论与公共讨论。
philosophers.summaryEn: The most controversial and influential American philosopher of the late 20th century: one who dismantled analytic philosophy from within. Philosophy and the Mirror of Nature (1979) declared the mind-as-mirror metaphor bankrupt and philosophy's first-status a fiction — philosophy is one conversation among many in culture. Anti-representationalism (truth is not a mirror of reality), anti-foundationalism (no Archimedean point), ethnocentrism (we can only speak from our own language), and the 'liberal ironist' (acknowledging the contingency of one's beliefs while holding liberal ideals). He returned pragmatism (via Dewey and James) to American philosophy's mainstream and shaped literary theory, political theory, and public debate.

representativeWorks.title: 《哲学与自然之镜》
representativeWorks.content: 新实用主义的宣言：批判「心灵是反映自然的镜子」「哲学是文化的女王」两大神话。认识论的基础主义传统（笛卡尔-洛克-康德）被诊断为「一个失败的比喻」。分析哲学内部最著名的「反叛之书」。
representativeWorks.titleEn: Philosophy and the Mirror of Nature
representativeWorks.contentEn: The neopragmatist manifesto: attacking the myths of 'mind as mirror of nature' and 'philosophy as queen of culture'. The foundationalist tradition (Descartes-Locke-Kant) diagnosed as a failed metaphor. The most famous 'rebellious book' inside analytic philosophy.

representativeWorks.title: 《偶然、反讽与团结》
representativeWorks.content: 政治哲学与人生哲学：语言、自我与自由主义的偶然性；「自由主义反讽者」——把终极语汇看作偶然，却仍愿为减少残酷而奋斗。私人（自我创造）与公共（团结）的二分。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Politics and life: the contingency of language, self, and liberalism; the 'liberal ironist' — seeing one's final vocabulary as contingent yet still fighting to reduce cruelty. The private (self-creation) / public (solidarity) split.

coreThoughts.concept: 反表象主义：真理不是镜像
coreThoughts.desc: 罗蒂对「心灵-世界」关系的颠覆：从柏拉图到分析哲学，主流都假设——心灵像一面镜子，真理就是镜子对实在的准确映照；知识论的任务是「磨镜子」（清除偏见、建立正确方法）。罗蒂说：这个「镜子比喻」从根上就是错的。没有「世界本来的样子」可以对照，因为「描述世界」永远离不开我们的语言，而语言是人类历史的偶然产物。真理不是「与实在相符」，而是「我们的信念体系中经得起辩护的部分」——一句话：真理是「我们被说服相信的东西」，而不是「世界在镜子里的倒影」。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：罗蒂说「别信『真理是世界的照片』」——我们的语言不是照相机，真理只是「我们现在最说得通的看法」，以后可能还会变。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像地图不是地形本身：地图是人为约定的符号，好用就好——罗蒂说我们的理论也一样，没有一张地图是「真正的地形」。
coreThoughts.l3: 反表象主义（anti-representationalism）：语言不是世界的图像（对抗维特根斯坦《逻辑哲学论》的图像论与弗雷格-罗素传统）；真理 = 辩护的极限（反实在论）。«镜喻»批判继承杜威（经验主义）、维特根斯坦（语言游戏）、海德格尔（存在之思）与塞拉斯（「所予的神话」）——罗蒂自称把四位「疗愈型哲学家」熔于一炉。批评：被指控为相对主义/虚无主义（罗蒂回应：相对主义是一个「没人和自己站对立面的立场」——他是「种族中心主义」而非相对主义）。
coreThoughts.conceptEn: Anti-Representationalism: Truth is Not a Mirror
coreThoughts.descEn: From Plato to analytic philosophy, the mainstream assumed: the mind is a mirror, truth is its accurate reflection of reality; epistemology polishes the mirror. Rorty: the mirror metaphor is wrong from the root. There is no 'way the world is' to check against, because describing the world always depends on our language — a contingent product of human history. Truth is not correspondence to reality but 'what survives justification within our beliefs': truth is what we are persuaded to believe, not the world's reflection.
coreThoughts.l1En: Don't trust 'truth as photograph of the world' — language is not a camera; truth is just 'what we currently find most defensible', subject to change.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a map, not the terrain: maps are conventional symbols that work — our theories likewise; no map is 'the real terrain'.
coreThoughts.l3En: Anti-representationalism: language is not a picture of the world (against the Tractatus's picture theory and the Frege-Russell tradition); truth as the limit of justification (anti-realism). The mirror-critique fuses Dewey, Wittgenstein, Heidegger, and Sellars (the myth of the given) — four 'therapeutic philosophers'. Accused of relativism/nihilism; his reply: relativism is the position nobody stands against — he is 'ethnocentric', not relativist.

coreThoughts.concept: 反基础主义与哲学作为对话
coreThoughts.desc: 罗蒂对「哲学之死」的诊断与救赎：哲学自柏拉图以来一直自认为是「文化的女王」——提供一切知识（科学、道德、艺术）的最终基础（foundation）。罗蒂说：这个王座是空的。数学、自然科学、道德、文学各自有各自的玩法，不需要一个「超级学科」来奠基。哲学因此不是「第一科学」，而是文化中的一种「对话」——像文学批评、历史叙事一样，是让各种话语互相倾听的「有教养的闲聊」。哲学家的新角色：不是「给出终极答案」，而是「保持对话开放」——他称之为「哲学作为教化」（edification）：与过去的哲学家对话，不是为了继承他们的结论，而是为了让自己不被任何结论困住。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：罗蒂说「哲学不是所有学问的老板」——数学自己玩自己的，科学自己玩自己的，哲学只是其中一种「聊天方式」，负责让各门学问互相听得懂。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像聚会的主人：他不是最博学的人，但负责让学者、诗人、科学家坐到一张桌上聊起来——罗蒂说哲学家的新工作就是这个「主人」。
coreThoughts.l3: 反基础主义（anti-foundationalism）：拒绝「一切知识的基础」这一追求（黑格尔、胡塞尔、罗尔斯仍在寻求某种基础）。哲学作为对话/教化（edification）——与杜威「哲学是文化的批评」、伽达默尔「对话」共鸣；与「系统哲学」（罗尔斯式建构）相对。其后果被保守派哀叹（「相对主义泛滥」），被自由派欢呼（「终结了哲学帝国主义」）——罗蒂自称：「我的工作只是让哲学别再吓唬人。」
coreThoughts.descEn: His diagnosis and cure for philosophy: since Plato, philosophy claims to be the queen of culture, providing the foundations of all knowledge (science, morality, art). Rorty: the throne is empty. Mathematics, science, morals, literature each play their own games; no super-discipline is needed to ground them. Philosophy is not first science but one conversation among many — educated chatter letting discourses listen to each other. The philosopher's new role: not final answers but keeping the conversation open — 'philosophy as edification': conversing with past philosophers not to inherit conclusions but to avoid being imprisoned by any.
coreThoughts.l1En: Philosophy is not the boss of all knowledge — math plays its own game, science its own; philosophy is one way of talking, helping disciplines understand each other.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a party host: not the most learned, but making scholars, poets, scientists sit at one table — that's philosophy's new job.
coreThoughts.l3En: Anti-foundationalism: rejecting the search for a foundation of all knowledge (Hegel, Husserl, Rawls still seek one). Philosophy as conversation/edification — resonating with Dewey's culture-critique and Gadamer's dialogue; against 'system philosophy' (Rawlsian construction). Conservatives mourn ('relativism'), liberals cheer ('end of philosophical imperialism'); Rorty: 'My work is just stopping philosophy from bullying.'

famousEvents.title: 从分析哲学「叛逃」
famousEvents.desc: 罗蒂本是分析哲学体制内的明星（普林斯顿哲学系教授，《哲学与自然之镜》出版），该书却全面批判分析哲学的基础主义。此后他转到弗吉尼亚大学人文系任教，从「分析哲学家」变成「文学理论家眼中的哲学英雄」——一次罕见的知识分子「跨界」。
famousEvents.descEn: An analytic insider (Princeton professor) until Philosophy and the Mirror of Nature (1979) comprehensively attacked analytic foundationalism; he then moved to Virginia's humanities department — from analytic philosopher to literary theory's philosophical hero: a rare intellectual cross-over.

famousEvents.title: 从文学理论家到公共知识分子
famousEvents.desc: 《偶然、反讽与团结》出版后，罗蒂成为美国最著名的公共哲学家之一：《纽约时报》书评、《异议》杂志专栏、与哈贝马斯和德里达的对话、911 后对美国外交的批评。他坚持「哲学应该对公共生活说话」——这是杜威传统的复兴。
famousEvents.descEn: After Contingency, Irony, and Solidarity (1989) he became America's most famous public philosopher: NYT reviews, Dissent columns, dialogues with Habermas and Derrida, post-911 critiques of U.S. foreign policy. Philosophy must speak to public life — the Deweyan revival.

philosophers.scientificEval: 罗蒂对科学哲学的影响是「解构性」的：他拆除了「科学=客观真理的典范」这一形象（科学只是「一种特别可靠的交谈方式」），其反表象主义被科学哲学中的社会建构论与 STS（科学技术研究）部分吸收；他与科学实在论的争论（「真理是成功预测的奖赏还是与实在的符应？」）持续影响当代科学哲学；对「方法崇拜」的批判（科学方法不是通往真理的独特阶梯）预示了多元主义科学观。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: His influence on philosophy of science is deconstructive: dismantling 'science as the paradigm of objective truth' (science is 'one especially reliable way of talking'); his anti-representationalism absorbed by social constructivism and STS; his debate with scientific realism ('is truth a reward for successful prediction or correspondence?') continues; his critique of method-worship prefigures pluralist views of science.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 罗蒂的轨迹是「从内部人到外部人」：芝加哥（古典哲学训练）→ 耶鲁（分析哲学博士）→ 普林斯顿（分析哲学教授，1961-1982）→ 《哲学与自然之镜》（1979）内部反叛 → 弗吉尼亚/斯坦福（比较文学系，1982-1998）→ 晚年成为公共知识分子。他的思想表面「转向」极大（从分析到实用主义），内核却一贯：拒绝一切形式的「权威主义」——无论是科学主义的、宗教的还是哲学的。他自称受四种「疗愈」影响：杜威（经验主义无镜）、维特根斯坦（语言游戏）、海德格尔（存在之思）、塞拉斯（所予神话）。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: From insider to outsider: Chicago (classics) → Yale (analytic PhD) → Princeton (analytic professor 1961-82) → the 1979 internal rebellion → Virginia/Stanford (comparative literature 1982-98) → late public intellectual. Surface 'turns' are enormous (analytic to pragmatist), the core constant: refusing every authority — scientific, religious, philosophical. His four 'therapeutic' influences: Dewey, Wittgenstein, Heidegger, Sellars.
philosophers.aiReview: 罗蒂是那种「你越认真反驳他，越发现他早就预料到」的哲学家。他承认自己是相对主义者（「我们只能从自己的语言出发」），却拒绝虚无主义（「我们仍然可以努力减少残酷」）；他宣布「哲学没有特权」，却一辈子都在写哲学。批评者说他解构一切却不提供建设，但罗蒂的回答是：建设的任务不归哲学——社会进步靠的是诗人的想象、工程师的创造和公民的团结，不是靠哲学家给出「终极基础」。在「后真相」「算法茧房」的今天，罗蒂显得格外有先见：他早就说过，真理不是「镜像」，而是「我们共同辩护出来的」——问题是，当辩护的公共空间被算法拆散，我们还能不能共同辩护？
philosophers.aiReviewEn: The philosopher you can't refute without discovering he predicted it. He admits relativism ('we can only speak from our language') yet refuses nihilism ('we can still work to reduce cruelty'); he declares philosophy has no privilege yet wrote it all his life. Critics say he deconstructs without building; his answer: building isn't philosophy's job — progress comes from poets' imagination, engineers' creation, and citizens' solidarity, not foundational answers. In the age of post-truth and algorithmic echo chambers he looks prescient: truth is not mirror but 'what we justify together' — and when algorithms dismantle the public space of justification, can we still justify together?

philosophers.anecdote: 罗蒂在斯坦福的课堂上有个著名习惯：他会读一段分析哲学家的论证，然后停下来问：「这个论证想说服谁？说服之后又怎样？」——把「论证」还原为「修辞」。学生回忆，他最常说的一句话是：「哲学不是发现问题，而是决定什么问题值得问。」他去世前最后一本书叫《作为艺术的哲学》，在病榻上完成——他至死都在「艺术」与「哲学」之间画等号。
philosophers.anecdoteEn: A famous Stanford habit: he read an analytic argument, stopped, and asked: 'Who is this argument trying to persuade, and what happens after it succeeds?' — reducing argument to rhetoric. His students remember his constant line: 'Philosophy isn't finding problems but deciding which problems are worth asking.' His last book, Philosophy as Cultural Politics, was completed from his deathbed — he drew the equals sign between art and philosophy to the end.

philosophers.name: 阿多诺
philosophers.role: 法兰克福学派核心，文化工业批判与否定辩证法
philosophers.summary: 法兰克福学派（批判理论）的核心人物，20 世纪最具分量的文化批判者。他与霍克海默合著的《启蒙辩证法》（1947）提出震惊世界的命题：启蒙（理性）自己变成了新的神话与新的统治——「奥斯维辛之后，写诗是野蛮的」。他创造「文化工业」概念：大众文化不是人民的艺术，而是批量生产的、麻醉大众的意识形态。他的《否定辩证法》（1966）拒绝一切「同一性」——哲学的任务是让被概念压制的「非同一者」发声。他也是一位音乐理论家（勋伯格的研究者），一生在哲学与音乐之间保持张力。1969 年他在与学生运动的争论中心脏病发去世——批判的学生批判了批判者。
philosophers.summaryEn: The core of the Frankfurt School (critical theory) and the 20th century's most substantial cultural critic. With Horkheimer, the Dialectic of Enlightenment (1947) shocked the world: enlightenment (reason) became a new myth and a new domination — 'to write poetry after Auschwitz is barbaric'. He coined 'culture industry': mass culture is not the people's art but industrialized, narcotizing ideology. Negative Dialectics (1966) refuses all identity — philosophy must let the non-identical, suppressed by concepts, speak. Also a music theorist (Schönberg scholar), he lived the tension between philosophy and music. In 1969 he died of a heart attack amid student protests — the critical students criticizing the critic.

representativeWorks.title: 《启蒙辩证法》（与霍克海默合著）
representativeWorks.content: 20 世纪批判理论的里程碑：理性自我毁灭的悲剧史——从奥德修斯（狡计理性）到纳粹（工业化的屠杀），「启蒙」在征服自然的同时统治了人。著名命题：「神话已经是启蒙，启蒙倒退为神话。」
representativeWorks.contentEn: The milestone of critical theory: reason's self-destruction — from Odysseus (cunning reason) to the Nazis (industrialized murder), enlightenment dominates humanity while conquering nature. 'Myth is already enlightenment; enlightenment reverts to mythology.'

representativeWorks.title: 《否定辩证法》
representativeWorks.content: 阿多诺哲学体系的核心：拒绝黑格尔式「正反合」的同一性辩证法和一切「同一性思维」（把事物纳入概念的暴力）。哲学的任务：「坚持非同一性」——让概念无法穷尽的事物残余发声。「奥斯维辛之后写诗是野蛮的」在此得到哲学论证。
representativeWorks.contentEn: The core of his system: refusing Hegel's identity-dialectics (thesis-antithesis-synthesis) and all identity-thinking (the violence of subsuming things under concepts). Philosophy's task: insist on non-identity — letting the remainder that concepts cannot exhaust speak. 'To write poetry after Auschwitz is barbaric' finds its philosophical argument here.

representativeWorks.title: 《美学理论》
representativeWorks.content: 遗著：现代艺术作为「对世界的否定」——真正的艺术不是愉悦的装饰，而是用其形式对异化现实的抗议。「艺术是对被支配世界的无意识的批判。」
representativeWorks.contentEn: Posthumous: modern art as negation of the world — genuine art is not pleasant decoration but protest against alienated reality through its very form. 'Art is the unconscious critique of the dominated world.'

coreThoughts.desc: 阿多诺与霍克海默的世纪之问：为什么人类没有进入人性的新阶段，反而堕入野蛮的新形式？他们的回答：因为「启蒙」本身是辩证的——启蒙用理性征服自然（去神话化），但征服自然的同时，理性把自己变成了新的神话（工具理性成为新的权威），人反过来被自己的理性工具统治（理性化=物化）。奥德修斯用狡计战胜塞壬，但他是把自己绑在桅杆上才做到的——统治自然的代价是自我阉割。这条线的终点是奥斯维辛：理性化的屠杀。结论：「启蒙倒退为神话」——不是反理性，而是理性需要自我反思；「神话已经是启蒙」——最早的理性尝试已经包含统治。
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：阿多诺说「理性本来是帮人类解放的，结果理性自己变成了新的主人」——我们用科技征服自然，却被科技和效率统治，这就是「启蒙的倒退」。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像拿着手电筒走夜路：手电筒（理性）是为了照亮，但你要是只盯着手电筒看，反而看不见路——启蒙照亮世界，也把自己变成了新的黑暗。
coreThoughts.l3: 启蒙辩证法（Dialektik der Aufklärung）：①去神话化（Entzauberung，借韦伯）；②工具理性（instrumental reason）成为统治；③物化（reification，卢卡奇）→ 同一性思维（identity thinking）。奥德修斯-塞壬解读：理性=狡计=自我保存=自我压抑。「神话已经是启蒙，启蒙倒退为神话」是全书箴言。此论与韦伯的「理性化铁笼」、尼采的权力意志论互文，是 20 世纪「理性批判」的最深文本之一。
coreThoughts.descEn: Their century-question: why did humanity enter not a new human condition but new forms of barbarism? Answer: enlightenment is dialectical — reason disenchants nature (demythologization) yet turns itself into a new myth (instrumental reason becomes new authority), and man is ruled by his own rational tools (rationalization = reification). Odysseus defeats the Sirens by cunning but only by lashing himself to the mast — mastering nature costs self-castration. The line ends at Auschwitz: rationalized murder. 'Enlightenment reverts to mythology' — not anti-reason but reason needing self-reflection; 'myth is already enlightenment' — the earliest rational attempts already contain domination.
coreThoughts.l1En: Reason was to liberate humanity, but reason became the new master — we conquer nature with technology yet are ruled by technology and efficiency: enlightenment's regression.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like a flashlight: meant to illuminate, but stare only at the torch and you see nothing — enlightenment lit the world and became its own darkness.
coreThoughts.l3En: The dialectic: disenchantment (Weber) → instrumental reason as domination → reification (Lukács) → identity thinking. The Odysseus-Sirens reading: reason = cunning = self-preservation = self-repression. 'Myth is already enlightenment; enlightenment reverts to mythology.' In dialogue with Weber's iron cage and Nietzsche's will to power; among the deepest texts of 20th-century critique of reason.

coreThoughts.desc: 阿多诺创造的概念（与霍克海默共同）：大众文化不是「民间文化」或「为人民的文化」，而是「文化工业」——像工厂一样标准化、批量生产的文化商品（好莱坞电影、流行音乐、广告）。文化工业的欺骗性：它让你以为自己在娱乐和选择，其实是在被灌输与麻醉——同一首歌、同一个故事、同一种生活方式被无限复制，差异只是表面的。它的功能是「意识形态」：让大众安于现状（「接受你的命运，因为你已经得到了娱乐」）。阿多诺的名言：「在文化工业中，娱乐是延长的工作。」
coreThoughts.l1: 简单说：阿多诺说「你以为你在娱乐，其实你在被灌输」——电影、流行歌、广告都是工厂流水线，批量生产同一种想法。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像速食面：包装千变万化，撕开都是同一块面饼——文化工业就是思想的速食面，包装（明星、旋律）不同，口味（价值观）一样。
coreThoughts.l3: 文化工业（Kulturindustrie，1947）：标准化（standardization）+ 伪个性化（pseudo-individuality）。与「大众文化」（mass culture）区分：阿多诺坚持用「文化工业」以强调其工业性。「娱乐是延长的工作」；「自由时间」被文化产业殖民。影响：媒介研究（法兰克福学派媒介理论）、传播学、流行文化批判（赫伯特·席勒、乔姆斯基的宣传模型）。批评：过于精英主义（低估大众的能动性——霍尔的文化研究反驳之）。
coreThoughts.descEn: His coinage (with Horkheimer): mass culture is not folk culture or culture for the people but the culture industry — standardized, batch-produced cultural commodities (Hollywood, pop music, advertising). Its deception: you believe you're entertained and choosing, but you're being infused and narcotized — the same song, story, lifestyle endlessly reproduced, difference merely superficial. Its function is ideology: reconciling the masses to the status quo ('accept your fate, for you have been entertained'). His line: 'In the culture industry, amusement is the prolongation of work.'
coreThoughts.l1En: You think you're being entertained; you're being infused — films, pop songs, ads are assembly lines producing the same thought.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like instant noodles: packaging varies, inside is the same block — culture industry is ideological fast food; packaging (stars, melodies) differs, flavor (values) is identical.
coreThoughts.l3En: Culture industry (1947): standardization + pseudo-individuality; distinguished from 'mass culture' to emphasize industrial character. 'Amusement is the prolongation of work'; free time colonized. Influences media studies, communication theory, pop-culture critique (Schiller, Chomsky's propaganda model). Critics: elitist, underestimating audience agency (Hall's cultural studies reply).

famousEvents.title: 流亡美国
famousEvents.desc: 纳粹上台后，阿多诺流亡美国（先在哥伦比亚大学的社会研究所——法兰克福学派的流亡地，后在加州参与「广播研究项目」，研究流行音乐对听众的影响——文化工业概念的实证土壤）。1953 年他回到法兰克福重建研究所。
famousEvents.descEn: After the Nazi seizure of power he emigrated: Columbia's Institute for Social Research (the Frankfurt School's exile home), then California's radio research project studying popular music's effects — the empirical soil of the culture industry concept. He returned to rebuild the Institute at Frankfurt in 1953.

famousEvents.title: 与学生运动的冲突与逝世
famousEvents.desc: 1968 年学生运动高潮中，激进学生把「阿多诺：法兰克福学派之墓」标语贴满研究所。阿多诺反对学生的行动主义（「我建立理论不是为了被扔石头」），被迫报警驱散占领研究所的学生——批判者被批判。次年他在瑞士度假时心脏病发去世。
famousEvents.titleEn: The Student Movement and His Death
famousEvents.descEn: In the 1968 movement's heat, students pasted 'Adorno: tomb of the Frankfurt School' on the Institute. He opposed their activism ('I built a theory, not to have stones thrown at me') and called police on students occupying the Institute — the critic criticized. He died of a heart attack in Switzerland in 1969.

philosophers.scientificEval: 阿多诺对社会科学的影响是范式级的：文化工业概念是媒介研究与传播批判理论的基石；「权威人格」研究（他与同事合著《权威人格》1950，调查反犹主义的心理根源）是实证社会研究的重要里程碑（后经密尔格拉姆、阿希实验延续）；其「奥斯维辛之后」的命题引发关于「文明与野蛮」的持久学术讨论。他的否定辩证法与「星丛」（constellation）方法论影响了当代批判理论、后殖民研究与文学批评。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: His impact on social science is paradigmatic: the culture industry is bedrock of media studies and critical communication theory; the Authoritarian Personality (1950, investigating anti-Semitism's psychological roots) is a milestone of empirical social research (continued by Milgram and Asch); the 'after Auschwitz' thesis opened enduring debates on civilization and barbarism. His negative dialectics and constellation method shape contemporary critical theory, postcolonial studies, and literary criticism.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 阿多诺的轨迹：法兰克福（哲学与音乐）→ 维也纳跟勋伯格学作曲 → 法兰克福大学任教（1931）→ 流亡牛津、美国（1934-1953）→ 回法兰克福重建研究所（1953）→ 晚年与阿本德罗特等的实证主义之争、与学生运动的冲突（1969 去世）。思想线：早年音乐美学（勋伯格的否定性艺术）→ 与霍克海默合写《启蒙辩证法》（1947）→ 独著的《最低限度的道德》（1951，箴言体的幸存伦理）→ 《否定辩证法》（1966）→ 遗著《美学理论》。他一生坚持：哲学必须成为对苦难的见证，而非对苦难的辩护。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: Frankfurt (philosophy and music) → Vienna studying composition with Schönberg → Frankfurt chair (1931) → exile Oxford and America (1934-53) → return to rebuild the Institute (1953) → late positivism dispute and student conflict (died 1969). Line: early music aesthetics (Schönberg's negating art) → Dialectic of Enlightenment (1947) → Minima Moralia (1951, aphoristic ethics of survival) → Negative Dialectics (1966) → posthumous Aesthetic Theory. His constant: philosophy must bear witness to suffering, not justify it.
philosophers.aiReview: 阿多诺是那种「读起来让你绝望，却绝望得清醒」的哲学家：《启蒙辩证法》说理性本身会变成统治，文化工业说你的娱乐都是麻醉——按他的逻辑，似乎没有出路。但他的全部工作恰恰是一个悖论式的行动：他用最精密的哲学证明「行动无望」，而写下这些证明本身就是一种行动——坚持不闭嘴，坚持说出被掩盖的苦难。今天的语境里他依然锋利：算法推荐是「伪个性化」的终极形态，短视频是「娱乐延长工作」的极致版本，大数据是「同一性思维」的技术化身。但阿多诺也常被误读：他批判的不是「文化」，而是「文化被工业化」；他坚持现代艺术（勋伯格、卡夫卡、贝克特）恰恰是抵抗的样板——艺术的否定性，是那支不被驯服的火把。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: The philosopher who makes you despair yet despair lucidly: the Dialectic says reason itself becomes domination, culture industry says your entertainment is narcosis — by his logic, no exit. Yet his whole work is a paradoxical act: proving with the most precise philosophy that action is hopeless, while writing those proofs is itself action — refusing silence, naming covered suffering. He stays sharp today: algorithmic feeds are pseudo-individuality's final form, short videos the ultimate 'amusement as prolonged work', big data identity-thinking made technical. But he is often misread: he criticized not culture but its industrialization; he held modern art (Schönberg, Kafka, Beckett) as the model of resistance — art's negativity is the untamed torch.

furtherReading.title: 《启蒙辩证法》（渠敬东/曹卫东中译本）
furtherReading.desc: 批判理论里程碑

philosophers.anecdote: 阿多诺是「哲学与音乐的婚姻」：他一生都在写两本书——哲学的《否定辩证法》和关于音乐的《新音乐哲学》。他年轻时曾想当作曲家，跟勋伯格学过作曲，最后发现自己在「写作上的天赋大于作曲」，才转投哲学。但音乐从未离开：他一生收集唱片、研究贝多芬与马勒，晚年宣称「唯一让我觉得生活值得的，是贝多芬的晚期弦乐四重奏」。他在课堂上放唱片，先让研究生听，然后问：「你们听出了什么？」——据说大多数学生听不出，他就叹气说：「那我们需要再听一遍。」
philosophers.anecdoteEn: The marriage of philosophy and music: he spent his life writing two books — Negative Dialectics and the Philosophy of New Music. A would-be composer trained by Schönberg, he found his 'talent for writing exceeded composition' and turned to philosophy — but music never left: collecting records, studying Beethoven and Mahler, late in life declaring 'the only thing making life worth living is Beethoven's late string quartets.' In class he played records, then asked: 'What did you hear?' Most students heard nothing; he sighed: 'Then we must listen again.'

philosophers.name: 芝诺（基提翁）
philosophers.role: 斯多亚学派创始人
philosophers.summary: 塞浦路斯商人之子，船难后流落雅典，因在书店读到苏格拉底的传记而转向哲学，投师犬儒派克拉特斯。约公元前 301 年起在雅典彩绘柱廊（Stoa Poikile）讲学，学派由此得名「斯多亚」。他把犬儒的克己锻造成理性体系：宇宙是活生生的逻各斯，幸福在于「与自然一致地生活」，德性是唯一真正的善。他是世界主义（宇宙城邦）观念的先驱，也是西方逻辑学与语言学的重要起点。
philosophers.summaryEn: Son of a merchant family in Cyprus, Zeno was shipwrecked in Athens, read about Socrates in a bookshop, and turned to philosophy under the Cynic Crates. Around 301 BC he began teaching at the Painted Porch (Stoa Poikile), giving Stoicism its name. He forged Cynic self-mastery into a rational system: the cosmos is living logos, happiness is 'living in agreement with nature', and virtue is the only good. He is a pioneer of cosmopolitanism and a founding source of Western logic and linguistics.

representativeWorks.title: 《理想国》
representativeWorks.content: 芝诺的《理想国》与柏拉图同名著作针锋相对：废除货币与性别分工，贤者皆为公民——最早的世界主义乌托邦，主张全人类共居一个宇宙城邦（cosmopolis）。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Zeno's Republic counters Plato's: no money, no gender-based division of labor, sages as citizens — an early cosmopolitan utopia in which all humans dwell in one world-city (cosmopolis).

representativeWorks.title: 《论与自然一致的生活》
representativeWorks.content: 斯多亚伦理学的奠基文本：幸福（telos）在于与自然一致地生活，即遵循理性而活。这部佚失著作的核心命题成为整个学派三百年的纲领。
representativeWorks.contentEn: The founding text of Stoic ethics: the end (telos) is to live in agreement with nature, i.e., according to reason. The lost work's thesis governed the school for three centuries.

representativeWorks.title: 《逻辑学研究》（残篇）
representativeWorks.content: 芝诺与弟子开创以命题和「可陈述者」（lekta）为单位的语言—逻辑研究，为克律西波斯的命题逻辑铺路，是独立于亚里士多德路线的古典逻辑另一源头。
representativeWorks.contentEn: Zeno's school pioneered the study of propositions and sayables (lekta), laying the ground for Chrysippus' propositional logic — the other fountainhead of classical logic alongside Aristotle.

coreThoughts.concept: 与自然一致（依理性而活）
coreThoughts.desc: 幸福（telos）是「与自然一致地生活」：自然即宇宙理性（逻各斯），人因理性而成为宇宙的公民；过德性生活就是顺应自己的理性本性。
coreThoughts.l1: 幸福 = 顺着宇宙理性活，而不是顺着欲望活。
coreThoughts.l2: 把「自然」当作一个理性整体：人不是对抗环境，而是调谐自己与环境的一致——这既是宇宙论，也是生活态度。
coreThoughts.l3: 「与自然一致」（homologia）是斯多亚伦理学的纲领：德性（aretê）即「与自然一致的理性状态」，四主德（明智/节制/正义/勇敢）统一于理性。这一公式把犬儒的「自足」从消极避世改造成积极顺应，为后世自然法传统提供了原型。
coreThoughts.descEn: The end (telos) is to live consistently with nature: nature is cosmic reason (logos), and as rational beings humans are citizens of the cosmos; living virtuously is living according to one's own rational nature.
coreThoughts.l1En: Happiness = living with cosmic reason, not with appetite.
coreThoughts.l2En: Treat nature as one rational whole: don't fight your environment, tune yourself to it — at once cosmology and an attitude to life.
coreThoughts.l3En: Homologia (agreement with nature) is the program of Stoic ethics: virtue is the rational state consistent with nature; the four cardinal virtues reduce to reason. This formula turns Cynic self-sufficiency from withdrawal into active assent and provides a prototype for the later natural-law tradition.

coreThoughts.desc: 唯有德性（及参与德性者）是善，健康、财富、名声是「无关紧要之物」（adiaphora），只是「可取者」；幸福完全取决于内在状态，不依赖外物。
coreThoughts.l1: 外物都是「可用可不用的道具」，只有你的德性属于你。
coreThoughts.l2: 生病、贫穷、被流放——这些不是不幸，只是「不好不坏」的中性事件；它们的意义由你的判断赋予。
coreThoughts.l3: 芝诺区分「善」（德性及参与德性者）与「无关紧要」（adiaphora：健康、财富、名誉）。adiaphora 虽非善，但有「可取」（preferred）与「应避」（dispreferred）之分，因此斯多亚不是禁欲主义而是「价值分层」——这避免了犬儒的极端苦行，也使斯多亚伦理学成为「可控性哲学」的基石。
coreThoughts.descEn: Only virtue (and what participates in it) is good; health, wealth, reputation are 'indifferents' (adiaphora), merely 'preferred'. Happiness depends entirely on one's inner state, not on externals.
coreThoughts.l1En: Externals are props — usable or not; only your virtue belongs to you.
coreThoughts.l2En: Sickness, poverty, exile — these are not misfortunes but neutral events whose meaning is assigned by your judgment.
coreThoughts.l3En: Zeno separates 'good' (virtue and what participates in it) from 'indifferent' (adiaphora: health, wealth, reputation). Indifferents are not good but can be 'preferred' or 'dispreferred', so Stoicism is not asceticism but value-tiering — it avoids Cynic extremism and grounds the philosophy of controllability.

coreThoughts.concept: 宇宙理性与火的物理学
coreThoughts.desc: 宇宙是活生生的理性整体，火（或火性气息 pneuma）为基质；世界按理性周期生成与毁灭（大燃烧），灵魂是理性之火的一部分。
coreThoughts.l1: 整个宇宙是一个有生命、有理性的身体，你只是它的一部分。
coreThoughts.l2: 世界会「燃烧重生」——万物按理性循环，这不是宿命论，而是宇宙的节律。
coreThoughts.l3: 芝诺的物理学承袭赫拉克利特：基质是火，世界经历生成→凝聚→大燃烧（ekpyrosis）的永恒循环；灵魂是物质性的「火性气息」（pneuma）。这种彻底的唯物主义为「一切皆遵循理性必然」的决定论提供了宇宙论基础——自由不是对抗命运，而是认识并顺应命运。
coreThoughts.conceptEn: Cosmic reason and the physics of fire
coreThoughts.descEn: The cosmos is a living rational whole whose substrate is fire (or fiery breath, pneuma); the world generates and dissolves in rational cycles (ekpyrosis); the soul is a portion of rational fire.
coreThoughts.l1En: The whole universe is one living, rational body — you are part of it.
coreThoughts.l2En: The world 'burns and renews' — all things cycle by reason; not fatalism but the cosmos' rhythm.
coreThoughts.l3En: Zeno's physics inherits Heraclitus: substrate is fire; the world cycles through generation, condensation, and cosmic conflagration (ekpyrosis); the soul is material 'fiery breath' (pneuma). This thoroughgoing materialism grounds a determinism in which freedom is not fighting fate but recognizing and following it.

coreThoughts.desc: 人类因其同具理性而属于同一个城邦——宇宙城邦（cosmopolis）；贤者之间无民族与阶级之隔。这是世界主义思想的源头。
coreThoughts.l1: 你的真正国籍不是某国，而是「宇宙公民」。
coreThoughts.l2: 奴隶与皇帝、希腊人与蛮族——在理性面前都是同类。
coreThoughts.l3: 芝诺《理想国》提出废除货币与性别分工，所有人依理性共居宇宙城邦。「世界主义」（cosmopolitanism）一词即源于此（kosmos + polis）。这一观念经斯多亚传入罗马法哲学（万民法），并在启蒙时代重获新生。
coreThoughts.descEn: Because all humans share reason, they belong to one city — the cosmopolis; sages are not divided by ethnicity or class. This is the origin of cosmopolitanism.
coreThoughts.l1En: Your true citizenship is not a nation but the cosmos.
coreThoughts.l2En: Slave and emperor, Greek and barbarian — equals before reason.
coreThoughts.l3En: Zeno's Republic abolishes money and gender-based division of labor; all live by reason in one world-city. The word 'cosmopolitanism' derives from this (kosmos + polis). The idea passed into Roman legal philosophy (ius gentium) and was reborn in the Enlightenment.

famousEvents.title: 船难与哲学转向
famousEvents.desc: 传说芝诺运货的船在雅典附近失事，他走进书店读到苏格拉底传记，问「哪里能找到这样的人」，被指引到犬儒派克拉特斯门下，从此弃商从哲。
famousEvents.descEn: Legend: his cargo ship sank near Athens; reading about Socrates in a bookshop, he asked where such men could be found and was pointed to the Cynic Crates, abandoning commerce for philosophy.

famousEvents.title: 彩绘柱廊开讲
famousEvents.desc: 约此年起在雅典市场边的彩绘柱廊（Stoa Poikile）聚徒讲学，学派因讲学地点得名「斯多亚」，听众包括后来的国王安提柯二世。
famousEvents.descEn: Around this year he taught at the Painted Porch by the Athenian agora — the school's name comes from the porch; his audience included King Antigonus II Gonatas.

famousEvents.title: 从容辞世
famousEvents.desc: 传说 72 岁（一说 98 岁）离开讲堂时被门槛绊倒，他敲着地面说「我来了，为什么叫我」，随后屏住呼吸而死，死法贯彻了斯多亚的从容。
famousEvents.descEn: Legend says he tripped on a step, struck the ground saying 'I come of my own accord; why call me?', then held his breath until death — dying exactly as his philosophy taught.

philosophers.scientificEval: 芝诺的贡献在于把犬儒的伦理学实践整合为贯通宇宙论—逻辑学—伦理学的系统哲学。他对命题（lekta）与语言逻辑的早期研究，与亚里士多德词项逻辑并列为古典逻辑的两大源头；其「与自然一致」的伦理纲领与决定论宇宙论，成为西方自然法与普遍伦理观念的长期理论资源。主要限制在于全部著作佚失，学说只能依靠残篇与后世（尤其第欧根尼·拉尔修）转述复原，细节存在争议。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: Zeno's achievement was integrating Cynic ethical practice into a systematic philosophy spanning cosmology, logic, and ethics. His early study of propositions (lekta) and language-logic stands beside Aristotelian term-logic as one of the two sources of classical logic; his 'agreement with nature' ethics and determinist cosmology became a lasting resource for natural law and universal ethics. The main limitation: all his works are lost, and the doctrine must be reconstructed from fragments and later reports (especially Diogenes Laertius), leaving details disputed.
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 芝诺的思想经历了三次转向：从商人到犬儒弟子（船难后师从克拉特斯），再从犬儒的极端苦行中抽身，最后约公元前 301 年在彩绘柱廊自立门户——综合犬儒伦理、赫拉克利特物理学与苏格拉底—柏拉图的方法论，创立体系化的斯多亚哲学。晚年传说被门槛绊倒后屏息而亡，死前说「我来了，为什么还要召唤我？」，为其「顺应命运」的学说画上句号。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: Zeno's thought evolved through three turns: from merchant to Cynic disciple (under Crates after the shipwreck), then away from Cynic extremism, and finally, around 301 BC, to founding his own school at the Painted Porch — synthesizing Cynic ethics, Heraclitean physics, and Socratic–Platonic method into systematic Stoicism. Legend has him dying of held breath after tripping on a step, saying 'I come of my own accord; why call me?' — a fitting end to his doctrine of following fate.
philosophers.aiReview: 芝诺是「把苦行变成科学」的人：犬儒派把自足留给个别人，芝诺把它变成关于宇宙与理性的一般理论，让「不动心」成为可教、可学、可论证的学科。他的局限同样明显——在彻底的唯物主义决定论下，「自由」的落脚点始终是理论的薄弱处，这个问题直到克律西波斯的相容论才得到系统回应。今天他被记起，主要不是作为物理学家或逻辑学家，而是作为「可控性哲学」的开创者：两千三百年前就在教人分清「什么是我的，什么不是我的」。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Zeno is the man who turned asceticism into science: the Cynics left self-sufficiency to the few, Zeno made it a general theory of the cosmos and reason, so that 'freedom from disturbance' became a teachable, learnable, provable discipline. His limitation is equally clear — under thoroughgoing materialist determinism, the footing of 'freedom' remained weak until Chrysippus' compatibilism. Today he is remembered not as physicist or logician but as the founder of the philosophy of controllability: teaching, 2,300 years ago, to distinguish what is ours from what is not.

furtherReading.title: 《斯多亚主义》
furtherReading.desc: 约翰·塞拉斯，简明斯多亚哲学导论

furtherReading.title: 《希腊哲学史》第三卷
furtherReading.desc: 汪子嵩等，含斯多亚早期与芝诺专章

philosophers.anecdote: 芝诺本是塞浦路斯的富商之子。传说他的船在雅典附近沉没，货物尽失；他走进一家书店读到色诺芬《回忆苏格拉底》，问书商「哪里能找到这样的人」，恰好犬儒派克拉特斯路过，书商指着他说：「跟着那个人。」芝诺于是成了犬儒门徒——一次船难改变了两千年的哲学版图。据说他晚年离开讲堂时被门槛绊倒，摔在地上敲着地面说：「我来了，为什么叫我？」随后屏住呼吸死去，连死法都贯彻了他的哲学。
philosophers.anecdoteEn: Zeno was the son of a wealthy merchant family in Cyprus. Legend has his ship sinking near Athens with all cargo lost; in a bookshop he read Xenophon's Memorabilia of Socrates, asked where such men could be found, and was pointed to the passing Cynic Crates: 'Follow that man.' He became a Cynic disciple — one shipwreck changed two millennia of philosophy. In old age, it is said, he tripped on a step, struck the ground saying 'I come of my own accord; why call me?', and died holding his breath — his death itself an exercise of his philosophy.

relationships.description: 苏格拉底经犬儒学派（安提斯泰尼→第欧根尼→克拉特斯）构成芝诺的师承根源，其从容赴死是斯多亚的终身参照
犬儒的自足理想经克拉特斯传至芝诺；斯多亚继承了其克己精神，但将其改造为理性体系
宇宙逻各斯与火的宇宙论直接承袭赫拉克利特
与伊壁鸠鲁同时代开创两大希腊化学派：快乐主义对德性主义，针锋相对半个世纪
经克里安西斯传承，克律西波斯将芝诺的纲要发展为完整体系，被誉为「斯多亚第二奠基人」
开创的斯多亚主义在罗马结出果实，塞内卡是其道德散文传统的代表
「控制二分法」与依自然而活的伦理在爱比克泰德那里成为可执行的训练手册
《沉思录》是芝诺开创的斯多亚实践哲学的最后高峰

goldenQuotes.text: 幸福在于与自然一致地生活，即按照理性而活。
goldenQuotes.source: 《论与自然一致的生活》（佚失，第欧根尼·拉尔修引述）
goldenQuotes.textEn: The end is to live in agreement with nature, i.e., according to reason.
goldenQuotes.sourceEn: On Life According to Nature (lost; quoted by Diogenes Laertius)

goldenQuotes.text: 美德是唯一真正的善；健康、财富与名声皆是无关紧要之事。
goldenQuotes.source: 第欧根尼·拉尔修《名哲言行录》
goldenQuotes.textEn: Virtue is the only good; health, wealth, and reputation are indifferents.
goldenQuotes.sourceEn: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of the Philosophers

goldenQuotes.text: 人不是被事情本身所扰，而是被自己对事情的判断所扰。（斯多亚传统格言）
goldenQuotes.textEn: Men are disturbed not by things, but by their judgments about things.

timeline.title: 生于基提翁
timeline.desc: 生于塞浦路斯岛基提翁（今拉纳卡），商人家庭
timeline.descEn: Born in Citium, Cyprus (modern Larnaca), into a merchant family

timeline.title: 船难与投师犬儒
timeline.desc: 传说船难流落雅典，读苏格拉底传记后立志学哲学，投师犬儒派克拉特斯
timeline.descEn: Legend: shipwrecked in Athens, he read of Socrates, resolved to study philosophy, and became a disciple of the Cynic Crates

timeline.title: 彩绘柱廊开讲
timeline.desc: 约此年起在雅典彩绘柱廊（Stoa Poikile）聚徒讲学，「斯多亚」之名由此而来
timeline.descEn: Around this year he began teaching at the Painted Porch (Stoa Poikile) in Athens — hence the name 'Stoicism'

timeline.title: 辞世
timeline.desc: 传说被门槛绊倒后敲地说「我来了，为什么叫我」，随即屏息而终
timeline.descEn: Legend says he tripped on a step, said 'I come of my own accord; why call me?', and held his breath until death

influenceMap.desc: 「与自然一致」的纲领与德性唯一论成为西方伦理学的核心传统之一
influenceMap.descEn: The 'agreement with nature' program and virtue monism became a core Western ethical tradition

influenceMap.desc: 以命题与可陈述者（lekta）为单位的早期研究，与亚里士多德词项逻辑并列为古典逻辑双源
influenceMap.descEn: Early proposition-based study (lekta) stands beside Aristotle's term logic as one of the two classical sources

influenceMap.desc: 宇宙城邦（cosmopolis）观念是世界主义与万民法思想的源头
influenceMap.descEn: The cosmopolis is the origin of cosmopolitanism and the ius gentium tradition

influenceMap.desc: 「控制能控制之事」的二分思想是认知行为疗法的古代源头
influenceMap.descEn: The dichotomy of control is an ancient source of modern cognitive-behavioral therapy

contemporaryApplications.title: 现代斯多亚运动
contemporaryApplications.desc: 「斯多亚周」「斯多亚日记」等当代实践直接追溯至芝诺的学派纲领
contemporaryApplications.descEn: Stoic Week and Stoic journaling trace directly back to Zeno's school program

contemporaryApplications.title: 认知行为疗法（CBT）
contemporaryApplications.desc: 情绪源于判断的核心假设与芝诺开创的斯多亚认知理论一脉相承
contemporaryApplications.descEn: The premise that emotions stem from judgments descends from Zeno's cognitive theory

contemporaryApplications.title: 世界主义伦理
contemporaryApplications.desc: 当代全球伦理与「人类命运共同体」讨论频繁回溯斯多亚的宇宙城邦观念
contemporaryApplications.descEn: Contemporary global ethics frequently revisits the Stoic cosmopolis

philosophers.name: 克律西波斯
philosophers.role: 斯多亚第二奠基人，命题逻辑奠基者
philosophers.summary: 从索利来到雅典，师从芝诺的继承人克里安西斯，以惊人的勤奋把斯多亚从「纲要」写成「体系」——传说著书 705 卷。他奠定了命题逻辑，与亚里士多德词项逻辑并列为古典逻辑两大支柱；提出「理解的表象」作为真理标准；并以「共因」概念调和决定论与自由，是哲学史上最早的相容论者。古语称：「没有克律西波斯，就没有斯多亚。」
philosophers.summaryEn: From Soli to Athens, Chrysippus studied under Cleanthes, Zeno's successor, and with prodigious industry turned Stoicism from an outline into a system — said to have written 705 books. He founded propositional logic, the second pillar of classical logic beside Aristotle's term logic; proposed the 'cognitive impression' (katalepsis) as the criterion of truth; and reconciled determinism with freedom via 'common causes', making him philosophy's first great compatibilist. As the ancients said: 'Had there been no Chrysippus, there would have been no Stoa.'

representativeWorks.title: 《逻辑学研究》
representativeWorks.content: 命题逻辑的奠基之作：界定条件句、析取、合取与否定，提出五个「不可证明式」作为全部推理的公理基础。全书佚失，仅存残篇。
representativeWorks.contentEn: The founding work of propositional logic: defining conditionals, disjunction, conjunction, negation, and five 'undemonstrated' argument forms as the axiomatic base of all inference. Lost; only fragments survive.

representativeWorks.title: 《论命运》
representativeWorks.content: 回应「懒论证」（如果命运已定，努力无用）的经典文本：命运是「共因」链条，但人的同意（assent）是其中的必要环节——为决定论下的自由辩护。
representativeWorks.contentEn: The classic reply to the 'Idle Argument' (if fate is fixed, effort is pointless): fate is a web of 'common causes', but our assent is a necessary link in it — a defense of freedom within determinism.

representativeWorks.title: 《论情绪》
representativeWorks.content: 系统论证「情绪即判断」：愤怒、恐惧、欲望都是错误的判断（krisis），修正判断即消除情绪。
representativeWorks.contentEn: A systematic defense that emotions are judgments: anger, fear, desire are erroneous judgments (krisis); correcting the judgment removes the emotion.

coreThoughts.desc: 以命题为单位研究推理：条件句「如果 p 则 q」、析取、合取、否定，并给出五个不可证明的论证式作为推理公理——古典逻辑的另一大支柱。
coreThoughts.l1: 亚里士多德管「词」之间的推理，克律西波斯管「句子」之间的推理。
coreThoughts.l2: 「如果天下雨，地就湿；天在下雨；所以地湿」——这种推理形式被他系统化并证明有效。
coreThoughts.l3: 克律西波斯的命题逻辑以真值函项为基础（条件句的真值只取决于前后件真假），五个「不可证明式」（modus ponens 等）构成公理系统。这与亚里士多德词项逻辑互补，直到 19 世纪布尔与弗雷格才被全面超越——两千年前的另一半逻辑大厦。
coreThoughts.descEn: Reasoning at the level of propositions: conditionals 'if p then q', disjunction, conjunction, negation, and five 'undemonstrated' argument forms as axioms — the other pillar of classical logic.
coreThoughts.l1En: Aristotle handled inference between terms; Chrysippus handled inference between sentences.
coreThoughts.l2En: 'If it rains, the ground is wet; it rains; therefore the ground is wet' — inference forms like this were systematized and proved by him.
coreThoughts.l3En: Chrysippus' propositional logic rests on truth functions (a conditional's truth depends only on the truth of its parts); five 'undemonstrated' forms (modus ponens among them) form an axiom system. Complementary to Aristotle's term logic, it was not surpassed until Boole and Frege in the 19th century — the other half of the logical edifice built two millennia ago.

coreThoughts.desc: 认识以「表象」（phantasia）开始；能被理解、且无可置疑的表象（katalepsis）是真知的标准，是斯多亚认识论的基石。
coreThoughts.l1: 真正可靠的知识来自「看得清清楚楚、不容置疑」的印象。
coreThoughts.l2: 就像看清一个人的脸和远远瞥见一个人影——前者是「理解的表象」，后者不是。
coreThoughts.l3: 克律西波斯把认识论锚定在「表象」上：感觉产生表象，理性判断其清晰度；「理解的表象」（katalepsis）因来自真实对象且内容自明而成为真理标准（kriterion）。这与怀疑主义「一切表象都可怀疑」的立场正面冲突，是斯多亚对学园派怀疑论的直接回应。
coreThoughts.descEn: Knowledge begins with impressions (phantasiai); the impression that is graspable and indubitable (katalepsis) is the criterion of truth — the cornerstone of Stoic epistemology.
coreThoughts.l1En: Reliable knowledge comes from impressions that are clear and beyond doubt.
coreThoughts.l2En: Like clearly seeing a face versus glimpsing a figure in the distance — the former is a cognitive impression, the latter is not.
coreThoughts.l3En: Chrysippus anchored epistemology in impressions: sensation produces them, reason judges their clarity; the 'cognitive impression' (katalepsis), stemming from a real object and self-evident in content, becomes the criterion (kriterion) of truth. This directly opposes skepticism's claim that all impressions are dubitable — the Stoic reply to Academic skepticism.

coreThoughts.concept: 决定论与自由（共因与相容论）
coreThoughts.desc: 万物皆由命运（理性必然）决定，但人的「同意」（assent）是因果链条的必要环节——命运与自由可以相容。
coreThoughts.l1: 命运是一张大网，但你的「点头」是网上的一个结。
coreThoughts.l2: 石头滚下山是必然的，但「滚不滚」也取决于坡道上的每一个环节——人就是这样的环节。
coreThoughts.l3: 面对「懒论证」（若命运已定则努力徒劳），克律西波斯提出「共因」（common causes）：结果由多个原因共同产生，事件以「命运的方式」（fatalistic mode）取决于命运，但人的同意作为「促成原因」（auxiliary cause）参与其中。这是他最重要的原创概念之一，也是哲学史上最早的相容论（compatibilism）——当代自由意志论争至今仍在处理同一问题。
coreThoughts.conceptEn: Determinism and freedom (common causes and compatibilism)
coreThoughts.descEn: All things are determined by fate (rational necessity), yet our assent is a necessary link in the causal chain — fate and freedom are compatible.
coreThoughts.l1En: Fate is a great web, and your 'nod' is one of its knots.
coreThoughts.l2En: A stone rolls downhill by necessity, but whether it rolls also depends on every link of the slope — a human being is such a link.
coreThoughts.l3En: Against the Idle Argument (if fate is fixed, effort is futile), Chrysippus proposed 'common causes': outcomes arise from many causes together; events depend on fate 'in a fatalistic mode', yet human assent participates as an 'auxiliary cause'. This is among his most original concepts and philosophy's earliest compatibilism — the same problem contemporary free-will debates still address.

coreThoughts.desc: 情绪（pathos）不是被动降临的东西，而是理性做出的错误判断（krisis）：愤怒、恐惧、欲望本质上都是「判断失误」，可以通过理性训练消除。
coreThoughts.l1: 你生气，不是因为他惹了你，而是因为你判断「他应该被生气」。
coreThoughts.l2: 情绪像发红的温度计：指针动了不是温度计坏了，而是它「测量」了你的判断。
coreThoughts.l3: 克律西波斯把斯多亚认知理论推向极致：情绪 = 关于价值的错误判断，且这种判断「更新鲜、更有力量」（freshness of impression），故显得难以控制。治疗的路径是认知重评——这正是两千三百年后认知行为疗法（CBT）的核心假设。
coreThoughts.descEn: Emotions (pathê) are not things that befall us but erroneous judgments (krisis) of reason: anger, fear, desire are in essence 'errors of judgment' that rational training can remove.
coreThoughts.l1En: You are angry not because he provoked you, but because you judged that anger is warranted.
coreThoughts.l2En: An emotion is like a reddening thermometer: the pointer moves not because the thermometer is broken but because it 'measures' your judgment.
coreThoughts.l3En: Chrysippus pushed Stoic cognitive theory to its limit: emotion = an erroneous judgment of value, made vivid by the 'freshness' of the impression, hence hard to control. The cure is cognitive reappraisal — precisely the core hypothesis of cognitive-behavioral therapy 2,300 years later.

famousEvents.title: 赴雅典师从克里安西斯
famousEvents.desc: 从索利来到雅典，投入芝诺的继承人克里安西斯门下，此后终生在雅典讲学。
famousEvents.descEn: From Soli he came to Athens and studied under Cleanthes, Zeno's successor, teaching there for the rest of his life.

famousEvents.title: 继任斯多亚学园主持
famousEvents.desc: 约此年克里安西斯去世后继任第三任主持，此后学派在他的领导下进入全盛期，与学园派怀疑论和伊壁鸠鲁学派全面论战。
famousEvents.descEn: Around this year he succeeded Cleanthes as third head of the school, leading it through its golden age of polemics against Academic skepticism and Epicureanism.

famousEvents.title: 荒诞的辞世
famousEvents.desc: 第欧根尼·拉尔修记载：他看见驴吃无花果，叫仆人「给驴倒杯酒」，随后大笑而死——以逻辑严谨与生活荒唐并存的形象留名。
famousEvents.descEn: Diogenes Laertius records: seeing a donkey eating figs, he told a servant to give the donkey wine, then died laughing — remembered as a blend of logical rigor and absurdist life.

philosophers.scientificEval: 克律西波斯是古代逻辑学的双峰之一：他的命题逻辑（真值函项、五个不可证明式）在 19 世纪数理逻辑兴起之前未被实质超越；「理解的表象」认识论与「情绪即判断」的认知理论，被现代心理学视为认知疗法与情感科学的前驱；「共因/相容论」则成为当代自由意志论争的标准议题之一。学说散佚严重（仅约 476 个残篇），是客观评价的最大障碍。
philosophers.scientificEvalEn: Chrysippus is one of the two summits of ancient logic: his propositional logic (truth functions, five undemonstrated forms) was not substantively surpassed until 19th-century mathematical logic; his epistemology of the cognitive impression and his cognitive theory of emotion are recognized as forerunners of modern cognitive therapy and affective science; his common-cause compatibilism remains a standard topic in contemporary free-will debates. The chief obstacle to assessment is the near-total loss of his corpus (about 476 fragments).
philosophers.thoughtEvolution: 克律西波斯的哲学道路清晰而专注：索利出生→约前 260 年赴雅典师从克里安西斯→约前 232 年继任主持→直至约前 206 年去世，四十年间把芝诺的纲领体系化。他的独创性集中于逻辑学（命题逻辑）与形而上学（共因理论）两翼，其目标始终如一：让斯多亚在对怀疑论与伊壁鸠鲁的论战中立于不败之地——为此他甚至用一半著作篇幅转述并反驳对手观点，被后人戏称「斯多亚的刀」。
philosophers.thoughtEvolutionEn: Chrysippus' path was clear and single-minded: born in Soli; to Athens around 260 BC to study under Cleanthes; head of the school around 232 BC until his death around 206 BC — four decades systematizing Zeno's program. His originality concentrated on two wings, logic (propositional logic) and metaphysics (the theory of common causes), in service of one goal: making Stoicism invincible against skepticism and Epicureanism. He devoted half his output to restating and refuting opponents, earning the nickname 'the knife of the Porch'.
philosophers.aiReview: 克律西波斯是古代世界最被低估的巨匠：亚里士多德之后，逻辑学在他手中长出了另一条完整的枝干（命题逻辑），直到两千年后才被数理逻辑超越。他的「共因」与「情绪即判断」至今仍在当代哲学与心理学中回响。若说他有短板，那正是他的长处带来的——体系过于完备、论战过于好胜，让斯多亚在争论中越辩越严密，却也越辩越封闭；而后世罗马斯多亚更偏爱他的老师一辈的朴素与可执行性，克律西波斯式的高深逻辑反而被淡忘。
philosophers.aiReviewEn: Chrysippus is antiquity's most underrated giant: after Aristotle, logic grew a second complete branch in his hands (propositional logic), unsurpassed for two millennia. His 'common causes' and 'emotions as judgments' still echo in contemporary philosophy and psychology. If he has a flaw, it comes from his virtues: a system so complete and a polemical temper so keen made Stoicism ever sharper in debate yet ever more self-enclosed; later Roman Stoics preferred the plainness and practicality of the earlier generation, and Chrysippus' deep logic faded from memory.

furtherReading.title: 《希腊哲学史》第三卷
furtherReading.desc: 汪子嵩等，含克律西波斯逻辑与形而上学专章

furtherReading.title: 《斯多亚逻辑导论》
furtherReading.desc: S. Bobzien，英文斯多亚逻辑研究参考

philosophers.anecdote: 克律西波斯以「斯多亚的刀」闻名——专斩对手的论证，据说一天能写 500 行。第欧根尼·拉尔修记载他死于一个与哲学家身份极不相称的玩笑：看见一头驴在吃无花果，他叫仆人「给驴倒杯酒」，然后大笑不止，气绝身亡。逻辑的严谨与死亡的荒唐在他身上并存，让后世在严肃研究之余也记住了这位「笑着死去的逻辑学家」。
philosophers.anecdoteEn: Chrysippus was known as 'the knife of the Porch' — a refuter of opponents' arguments, said to write 500 lines a day. Diogenes Laertius records his death by a joke unworthy of a philosopher: seeing a donkey eating figs, he told a servant to give the donkey wine, then laughed until he died. The blend of logical rigor and absurd death made posterity remember this 'laughing logician' alongside his serious work.

relationships.description: 经克里安西斯传承芝诺衣钵，将学派纲要体系化——「没有克律西波斯，就没有斯多亚」
与整个斯多亚传统一致，视苏格拉底为先师与理想人格原型
以命题逻辑补足亚里士多德词项逻辑，构成古典形式逻辑的两大支柱
两大希腊化学派在命运论、快乐与德性上的长期论战，克律西波斯是斯多亚方的主辩手
克律西波斯的逻辑与情绪理论是塞内卡道德散文的学理底座
「情绪即判断」的理论在爱比克泰德手册中化为日常训练
《沉思录》的宇宙决定论底色源自克律西波斯的命运观

goldenQuotes.text: 如果命运规定了你生病，那么请医生也是白费；但如果命运规定的是「你因请医生而痊愈」，那么请医生恰恰是顺应命运。
goldenQuotes.textEn: If fate decrees that you will be ill, calling a doctor is futile; but if fate decrees that 'you recover because you called a doctor', then calling one is precisely what fate requires.

goldenQuotes.text: 情绪不是降临在我们身上的东西，而是我们自己的判断。
goldenQuotes.textEn: Emotions are not things that befall us, but our own judgments.

goldenQuotes.text: 智者并非没有情绪，而是不为错误的判断所奴役。
goldenQuotes.textEn: The sage is not without emotions, but is not enslaved by erroneous judgments.

timeline.title: 生于索利
timeline.desc: 生于小亚细亚索利（今土耳其南部）
timeline.descEn: Born in Soli, Cilicia (southern modern Turkey)

timeline.title: 赴雅典师从克里安西斯
timeline.desc: 赴雅典投入芝诺的继承人克里安西斯门下
timeline.descEn: Came to Athens and studied under Cleanthes, Zeno's successor

timeline.title: 继任斯多亚学园主持
timeline.desc: 约此年继任第三任主持，学派进入体系化与论战的全盛期
timeline.descEn: Succeeded as third head of the school; the age of systematization and polemics began

timeline.title: 辞世
timeline.desc: 第欧根尼·拉尔修记载其因目睹驴吃无花果大笑而终
timeline.descEn: Diogenes Laertius records he died laughing at the sight of a donkey eating figs

influenceMap.desc: 命题逻辑的奠基者，与亚里士多德词项逻辑并列为古典逻辑两大支柱
influenceMap.descEn: Founder of propositional logic, the second pillar of classical logic beside Aristotle

influenceMap.desc: 「情绪即判断」的认知理论是现代情感科学的前驱
influenceMap.descEn: The 'emotions are judgments' thesis anticipates modern affective science

influenceMap.desc: 共因理论与相容论是自由意志问题史上最早的体系化方案
influenceMap.descEn: Common causes and compatibilism are history's first systematic treatment of free will

influenceMap.desc: 认知重评路径与认知行为疗法（CBT）高度同构
influenceMap.descEn: The cognitive-reappraisal route is structurally identical to CBT

contemporaryApplications.title: 认知行为疗法（CBT）
contemporaryApplications.desc: 「情绪源于判断、改变判断即改变情绪」是 CBT 与 REBT 的直接理论前身
contemporaryApplications.descEn: 'Emotions stem from judgments; change the judgment, change the emotion' is the direct ancestor of CBT and REBT

contemporaryApplications.title: 自由意志当代论争
contemporaryApplications.desc: 共因与相容论立场仍是当代哲学自由意志辩论的标准选项之一
contemporaryApplications.descEn: The common-cause compatibilist position remains a standard option in contemporary free-will debates

contemporaryApplications.title: 现代逻辑教学
contemporaryApplications.desc: 条件句与推理式教学的基本框架可追溯至克律西波斯的五个不可证明式
contemporaryApplications.descEn: The basic framework of teaching conditionals and inference forms traces to Chrysippus' five undemonstrated arguments
